  be in effect January&nbsp;1, 2009.&nbsp; The

<h2 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PART&nbsp;I</font></b><a name="Parti_230618"></a></h2>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1 &#151; Business</font></b><a name="Item1Business_230620"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This report includes the
combined filing of <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L.&#160; DP&amp;L </b>is
the principal subsidiary of <b>DPL </b>providing
approximately 98% of <b>DPL&#146;s </b>total
consolidated revenue and approximately 95% of <b>DPL&#146;s </b>total
consolidated asset base.&#160; Throughout this
report, the terms &#147;we,&#148; us,&#148; &#147;our&#148; and &#147;ours&#148; are used to refer to both <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>,
respectively and altogether, unless the context indicates otherwise.&#160; Discussions or areas of this report that
apply only to <b>DPL</b> or <b>DP&amp;L</b>
will clearly be noted in the section.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">WEBSITE
ACCESS TO REPORTS</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>
file current, annual and quarterly reports and other information required by
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, with the SEC.&#160; You may read and copy any document we file at
the SEC&#146;s public reference room located at 100 F Street N.E., Washington, D.C.
20549, USA.&#160; Please call the SEC at (800)
SEC-0330 for further information on the public reference rooms.&#160; Our SEC filings are also available to the
public from the SEC&#146;s website at http://www.sec.gov.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
public internet site is http://www.dplinc.com.&#160;
We make available, free of charge, through our internet site, our annual
reports on Form&nbsp;10-K, quarterly reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q, current reports
on Form&nbsp;8-K, and Forms 3, 4 and 5 filed on behalf of our directors and
executive officers and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant
to the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, as soon as reasonably
practicable after we electronically file such material with, or furnish it to,
the SEC.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> is a regional energy
company organized in 1985 under the laws of Ohio.&#160; Our executive offices are located at 1065
Woodman Drive, Dayton, Ohio 45432 &#150; telephone (937) 224-6000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> principal subsidiary is <b>DP&amp;L</b>.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is a public utility incorporated in 1911 under the laws of Ohio.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
sells electricity to residential, commercial, industrial and governmental
customers in a 6,000 square mile area of West Central Ohio.&#160; Electricity for <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> 24 county service area is primarily generated at
eight coal-fired power plants and is distributed to more than 500,000 retail
customers.&#160; Principal industries served
include automotive, food processing, paper, plastic, manufacturing and
defense.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> sales reflect the general economic conditions and
seasonal weather patterns of the area.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> sells any excess energy and
capacity into the wholesale market.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> also sells electricity to DPLER, an affiliate, to
satisfy the electric requirements of its retail customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> other significant subsidiaries (all of which are wholly-owned)
include: DPLE, which engages in the operation of peaking generating facilities
and sells power in wholesale markets; DPLER, which sells retail electric energy
under contract to major industrial and commercial customers in West Central
Ohio; and MVIC, which is our captive insurance company that provides insurance
to us and our subsidiaries.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> also has a wholly-owned business trust,
DPL Capital Trust II, formed for the purpose of issuing trust capital
securities to investors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and <b>DP&amp;L</b> conduct
their principal business in one business segment &#151; Electric.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
electric transmission and distribution businesses are subject to rate
regulation by federal and state regulators while its generation business is not
subject to such regulation.&#160; Accordingly,
<b>DP&amp;L</b> applies the accounting
standards for regulated operations to its electric transmission and
distribution businesses and records regulatory assets when incurred costs are
expected to be recovered in future customer rates, and regulatory liabilities
when current recoveries in customer rates relate to expected future costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">and its subsidiaries employed 1,581
persons as of January&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2010, of which 1,403 were full-time
employees and 178 were part-time employees.&#160;
At that date, 1,396 of these full-time employees and all of the
part-time employees were employed by <b>DP&amp;L</b>.&#160; Approximately 55% of the employees are under
a collective bargaining agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)&nbsp; Credit rating relates to <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Senior

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Long-Term
Debt Redemption</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;31, 2009,<b> DPL</b> paid $175 million of the 8.00% Senior Notes when the
notes became due.&#160; In addition, on December&nbsp;21,
2009, <b>DPL</b> paid down $52.4 million of the $195
million 8.125% Note to DPL Capital Trust II which is due 2031.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">New
Revolving Credit Facility</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;21, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> entered into a $100 million
unsecured revolving credit agreement with a syndicated bank group.&#160; The agreement is for a 364-day term expiring
on April&nbsp;20, 2010.&#160; The facility
contains one financial covenant: <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
total debt to total capitalization ratio is not to exceed 0.65 to 1.00.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, this covenant
is met with a ratio of 0.40 to 1.00.&#160; As
of December&nbsp;31, 2009, there were no borrowings outstanding under this
facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Warrants
Repurchased and Exercised</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, <b>DPL</b> repurchased a total of 8.6 million
of its warrants at an average price of $2.94 each.&#160; The repurchased warrants were cancelled by <b>DPL </b>on the dates they were repurchased.&#160; Also during this period, warrant holders
exercised a total of 9.2 million warrants, of which 5.5 million were exercised
under cashless transactions and 3.7 million were exercised for cash.&#160; As a result of these warrant exercise
transactions, <b>DPL</b> issued a total of 5.0 million
shares of common stock from treasury stock and in turn received total cash
proceeds of $77.7 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stock
Repurchase Program</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;28, 2009,
the <b>DPL</b> Board of Directors approved a Stock
Repurchase Program under which <b>DPL</b> may use
proceeds from the exercise of warrants (discussed above) to repurchase common
stock and warrants from time to time in the open market, through private
transactions or otherwise. The Stock Repurchase Program will run through June&nbsp;30,
2012, which is approximately three months after the end of the warrant exercise
period.&#160; Through December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL</b> repurchased approximately 2.4 million shares of common
stock under the Stock Repurchase Program at an average price per share of
$26.96.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Approval
of Stipulation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In compliance with SB
221, <b>DP&amp;L </b>filed its ESP at the PUCO on October&nbsp;10,
2008. Subsequently on February&nbsp;24, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
filed the Stipulation signed by the Staff of the PUCO, the Office of the OCC
and various intervening parties.&#160; On June&nbsp;24,
2009, the PUCO issued an order granting approval of the Stipulation.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6<a name="PB_6_231028_5335"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Transmission,
Ancillary and Other PJM-related Costs</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;19,
2009, the PUCO approved <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
request to defer costs related to transmission, capacity, ancillary service and
other costs incurred since July&nbsp;31, 2008 consistent with the provisions of
SB 221.&#160; Subsequently, the PUCO approved
two separate riders in November&nbsp;2009, one for the recovery of RPM capacity
costs and another rider for the recovery of transmission, ancillary and other
PJM-related costs (TCRR).&#160; Accordingly,
during the period ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
deferred net RTO and other costs in the amount of $25.5 million.&#160; Of this amount, approximately $9.8 million
relates to the period August&nbsp;1, 2008 through December&nbsp;31, 2008, and
$15.7 million relates to the twelve month period ended December&nbsp;31,
2009.&#160; The deferral of these costs
resulted in a favorable impact to our results of operations.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Increase
in Dividends on DPL&#146;s Common Stock</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;9,
2009, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Board of Directors
authorized a quarterly dividend rate increase of approximately 6%, increasing
the quarterly dividend per <b>DPL </b>common
share from $.2850 to $.3025.&#160; If this
dividend rate is maintained, the annualized dividend would increase from $1.14
per share to $1.21 per share.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ELECTRIC SALES AND REVENUES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)</font></i><i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-style:italic;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></i></b><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;"> sells
power to DPLER (a subsidiary of <b>DPL</b>).&#160; The revenues associated with these sales are
classified as wholesale sales on <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
financial statements and retail sales for <b>DPL</b>. &#160;The kWh volumes contain all volumes
distributed on the <b>DP&amp;L</b> system
which include the retail sales by DPLER.&#160;
The sales for resale volumes are omitted from <b>DP&amp;L </b>to avoid duplicate reporting.</font></i></p>

  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
present summer generating capacity, including peaking units, is approximately
3,794 MW.&#160; Of this capacity,
approximately 2,827 MW, or 75%, is derived from coal-fired steam generating
stations and the balance of approximately 967 MW, or 25%, consists of
combustion turbine and diesel peaking units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
present summer generating capacity, including peaking units, is approximately
3,249 MW.&#160; Of this capacity,
approximately 2,827 MW, or 87%, is derived from coal-fired steam generating
stations and the balance of approximately 422 MW, or 13%, consists of
combustion turbine and diesel peaking units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our all-time net peak load was 3,270 MW,
occurring August&nbsp;8, 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Approximately 87% of the existing steam
generating capacity is provided by certain generating units owned as tenants in
common with Duke Energy-Ohio (or its subsidiaries The Cincinnati Gas&nbsp;&amp;
Electric Company [CG&amp;E], or Union Heat, Light&nbsp;&amp; Power) and AEP (or
its subsidiary Columbus Southern Power [CSP]).&#160;
As tenants in common, each company owns a specified share of each of
these units, is entitled to its share of capacity and energy output, and has a
capital and operating cost responsibility proportionate to its ownership
share.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
remaining steam generating capacity (approximately 365 MW) is derived from a
generating station owned solely by <b>DP&amp;L</b>.&#160; Additionally, <b>DP&amp;L,</b> CG&amp;E and CSP own, as tenants in common, 884
circuit miles of 345,000-volt transmission lines.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
has several interconnections with other companies for the purchase, sale and
interchange of electricity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
2009, we generated 99.5% of our electric output from coal-fired units and 0.5%
from oil and natural gas-fired units.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3,794</font></p>

  <td width="2%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.68%;">

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="1" width="25%" noshade color="black" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">*W
= Wholly-Owned</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;C
= Commonly-Owned</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the above, <b>DP&amp;L </b>also owns a 4.9% equity ownership interest in OVEC,
an electric generating company.&#160; OVEC has
two plants in Cheshire, Ohio and Madison, Indiana with a combined generation
capacity of approximately 2,265 MW.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> share of this generation capacity is
approximately 111 MW.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">has
substantially all of the total expected coal volume needed to meet its retail
and firm wholesale sales requirements for 2010 under contract.&#160; The majority of the contracted coal is
purchased at fixed prices.&#160; Some
contracts provide for periodic adjustments and some are priced based on market
indices.&#160; Fuel costs are impacted by
changes in volume and price and are driven by a number of variables including
weather, the wholesale market price of power, certain provisions in coal
contracts related to government imposed costs, counterparty performance and
credit, scheduled outages and generation plant mix.&#160; Our emission allowance consumption was
reduced in 2008 and 2009 due to the installation of FGD equipment (scrubbers)
at our jointly-owned electric generating stations.&#160; Due to the installation of this emission
control equipment and barring any changes in the regulatory environment in
which we operate, we expect to have emission allowance inventory in excess of
our needs, which we plan to sell during 2010 and in future periods.&#160; We were a net seller of SO</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;allowances and NOx allowances in 2009, and we
expect to be a net seller in 2010.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">SEASONALITY</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
power generation and delivery business is seasonal and weather patterns have a
material impact on operating performance.&#160;
In the region we serve, demand for electricity is generally greater in
the summer months associated with cooling and in the winter months associated
with heating as compared to other times of the year.&#160; Unusually mild summers and winters could have
an adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and cash
flows.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">RATE
REGULATION AND GOVERNMENT LEGISLATION</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> sales to retail customers are subject to rate
regulation by the PUCO.&#160; Beginning January&nbsp;1,
2010, <b>DP&amp;L</b> has a fuel rider in place for
the collection of our prudently incurred fuel, purchased power, emission and
other related costs.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> transmission rates and wholesale
electric rates to municipal corporations, rural electric co-operatives and
other distributors of electric energy are subject to regulation by the FERC
under the Federal Power Act.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ohio
law establishes the process for determining retail rates charged by public
utilities.&#160; Regulation of retail rates
encompasses the timing of applications, the effective date of rate increases,
the recoverable costs basis upon which the rates are based and other related
matters.&#160; Ohio law also established the
Office of the OCC, which has the authority to represent residential consumers
in state and federal judicial and administrative rate proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ohio
legislation extends the jurisdiction of the PUCO to the records and accounts of
certain public utility holding company systems, including <b>DPL</b>.&#160; The legislation extends the PUCO&#146;s
supervisory powers to a holding company system&#146;s general condition and
capitalization, among other matters, to the extent that such matters relate to
the costs associated with the provision of public utility service.&#160; Based on existing PUCO and FERC
authorization, regulatory assets and liabilities are recorded on the balance
sheets.&#160; See Note 3 of Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COMPETITION AND REGULATION</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Ohio Matters</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Ohio Retail Rates</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since January&nbsp;2001, <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> electric customers have been
permitted to choose their retail electric generation supplier.</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> continues to have the exclusive right to provide
delivery service in its state certified territory and the obligation to supply
retail generation service to customers that do not choose an alternative
supplier.&#160; The PUCO maintains jurisdiction
over <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> delivery of electricity,
standard service offer and other retail electric services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;1,
2008, substitute SB 221, an Ohio electric energy bill, was signed by the
Governor and went into effect July&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160; This law required that all Ohio distribution
utilities file either an electric security plan or a market rate option that
was to be in effect on January&nbsp;1, 2009.&#160;
Under the market rate option, a periodic competitive bid process will
set the retail generation price after the utility demonstrates that it can meet
certain market criteria and bid requirements set out in the bill.&nbsp; Also,
under this option, utilities that still own generation in the state are
required to phase in the market rate option over a period of not less than five
years.&#160; An electric security plan may
allow for adjustments to the standard service offer for costs associated with
environmental compliance; fuel and purchased power; construction of new or
investment in specified generating facilities; and the provision of standby and
default service, operating, maintenance, or other costs including taxes.&nbsp;
As part of its electric security plan, a utility is permitted to file an
infrastructure improvement plan that will specify the initiatives the utility will
take to rebuild, upgrade, or replace its electric distribution system,
including cost recovery mechanisms.&nbsp; Both the market rate option and
electric security plan option involve a &#147;substantially excessive earnings&#148; test
based on the earnings of comparable companies with similar business and
financial risks.&#160; The PUCO issued three
sets of rules&nbsp;related to implementation of the law.&#160; These rules&nbsp;address topics such as the
information that must be included in an electric security plan as well as a
market rate option, the significantly excessive earnings test requirements,
corporate separation revisions, rules&nbsp;relating to the recovery of
transmission related costs, electric service and safety standards dealing with
the statewide line extension policy, and rules&nbsp;relating to advanced energy
portfolio standards, renewable energy, demand reduction and energy efficiency
standards.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
compliance with SB 221, <b>DP&amp;L </b>filed
its ESP at the PUCO on October&nbsp;10, 2008.&#160;
This plan contained three parts: 1) a standard offer plan; 2) a CCEM
plan; and 3) an alternative energy plan.&#160;
The standard offer plan stated that <b>DP&amp;L </b>intends
to maintain its current rate plan through December&nbsp;31, 2010, and addressed
compliance issues related to the PUCO rules.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SB 221
and the implementation rules&nbsp;contain targets relating to advanced energy
portfolio standards, renewable energy, demand reduction and energy efficiency
standards.&#160; After several revisions,
rulings on rehearing and reissuance that occurred throughout 2009, the rules&nbsp;relating
to renewable energy, energy efficiency, demand reduction and integrated
resource plans were made effective on December&nbsp;10, 2009.&#160; The standards require that, by the year 2025,
25% of the total number of kWh of electricity sold by the utility to retail
electric consumers must come from alternative energy resources, which include &#147;advanced
energy resources&#148; such as distributed generation, clean coal, advanced nuclear,
energy efficiency and fuel cell technology; and &#147;renewable energy resources&#148;
such as solar, hydro, wind, geothermal and biomass. At least half of the 25%
must be generated from renewable energy resources, including 0.5% from solar
energy. &#160;The renewable energy portfolio,
energy efficiency and demand reduction standards began in 2009 with increases
in required percentages each year.&#160; The
annual targets for energy efficiency are expected to save 22.3% by 2025 and
peak demand reductions are expected to reach 7.75% by 2018 compared to baseline
energy usage.&#160; If any targets are not
met, compliance penalties will apply unless the PUCO makes certain findings
that would excuse performance.&#160; In December&nbsp;2009,
<b>DP&amp;L</b> and DPLER made several filings
relating to their renewable energy and energy efficiency compliance
plans.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b> and DPLER were able to
obtain Renewable Energy Certificates sufficient to meet their overall renewable
energy targets, but <b>DP&amp;L</b> and
DPLER together obtained only 36% of the separate requirement for 2009
Ohio-based solar power.&#160; The companies
asked for a waiver of any unmet 2009 Ohio solar requirements on grounds of
force majeure because there are insufficient solar renewable energy credits
available from Ohio resources.&nbsp; In two separate filings, <b>DP&amp;L</b> requested the PUCO&#146;s consent that <b>DP&amp;L</b> had met the requirements for energy efficiency and
for demand reduction based on <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
interpretation of how those requirements should be applied.&#160; These filings also requested that if the PUCO
disagreed with <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> interpretation, the
PUCO grant alternative relief and find that <b>DP&amp;L</b>
was unable to meet the targets due to reasons beyond its reasonable control,
i.e. uncertainty throughout 2009 caused by delays in finalizing the rules&nbsp;and
the lack of timely PUCO action on several of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
special contracts relating to demand response efforts which remain pending
before the PUCO.&#160; </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11<a name="PB_11_001801_141"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
addition, the rules&nbsp;that became effective December&nbsp;10, 2009 required
that on January&nbsp;1, 2010, <b>DP&amp;L</b> file
an extensive energy efficiency portfolio plan, outlining how <b>DP&amp;L </b>plans to comply with the energy efficiency and
demand reduction benchmarks.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed
a separate request for a finding that it had already complied with this
requirement in the form of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
portfolio plan that had been filed in 2008 as part of its electric security
plan, which had been approved by the PUCO and is being implemented.&#160; We are unable to predict at this time how the
PUCO will respond to these filings, but believe that the outcome will not be
material to our financial condition.&#160;
However, as the targets get increasingly larger over time, the costs of
complying with the SB 221 targets and the PUCO&#146;s implementing rules&nbsp;could
have a material impact on our financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;24,
2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed the Stipulation with the
PUCO which was signed by the Staff of the PUCO, the Office of the OCC and
various intervening parties.&#160; The
material terms agreed to under the Stipulation include the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
current rate plan will be extended through 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
will be permitted to implement a fuel and purchased power recovery mechanism
beginning January&nbsp;1, 2010 which will track and adjust fuel and purchased
power costs on a quarterly basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The rate stabilization surcharge remains a non-bypassable provider of
last resort charge at its current rate amount, but may be bypassable by
customers served by a government aggregator beginning 2011. If a government
aggregator elects to avoid this surcharge in 2011 and 2012, its customers can
only return to <b>DP&amp;L</b> at a market-based rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The last phase of the EIR increase will occur in 2010 as previously
approved by the PUCO and thereafter will remain at that level through 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
base distribution and generation rates will be frozen through 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
may seek recovery of certain cost increases such as storm damage expenses,
regulatory or tax changes, costs associated with new climate change or carbon
regulations, certain costs associated with the operation of the Hutchings
station, costs associated with TCRR and Regional Transmission Organization
costs not covered by the TCRR.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The significantly excessive earnings test will not apply to <b>DP&amp;L</b> until 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
will be permitted to begin its energy efficiency and demand response programs
immediately with recovery scheduled to begin in 2009, with a two-year
reconciliation.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
smart grid deployment initiative will be revised and resubmitted to the PUCO
for approval by September&nbsp;2009 with the anticipation that the plans and
recovery will begin January&nbsp;1, 2010 also with a two year reconciliation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
proposed alternative energy plans will be approved and recovery of these costs
will begin in 2009 with an annual reconciliation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mercantile (large use) customers can obtain exemption from the energy
efficiency rider if self-directed energy and demand programs generate reductions
equal to or greater than <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
energy and demand reduction benchmarks.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;24, 2009,
the PUCO issued an order granting approval of the Stipulation as filed and
authorized <b>DP&amp;L</b> to implement rates
associated with alternative energy and energy efficiency compliance costs,
which <b>DP&amp;L</b> implemented beginning on July&nbsp;1,
2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consistent with the
Stipulation, <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed its smart grid and
advanced metering infrastructure business cases with the PUCO on August&nbsp;4,
2009 seeking recovery of costs associated with a three-year plan to deploy
smart meter; and a ten-year plan for distribution and substation automation,
core telecommunications, supporting software and in-home technologies.&nbsp; On
August&nbsp;5, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
submitted an application for American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA)
funding under the Integrated and/or Crosscutting Systems topic area for the
Smart Grid Investment Grant Program, seeking $145.1 million of matching
funds.&#160; On October&nbsp;27, 2009, we were
notified by the United States Department of Energy (DOE) that we will not
receive funding under the ARRA.&#160; A
technical conference was held at the PUCO in October&nbsp;2009 for the smart
grid case, and a subsequent PUCO entry established a comment and reply comment
period.&#160; The PUCO Staff along with other
interested parties provided comments and reply comments on <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
plans.&#160; A hearing is not yet scheduled
for this case.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Stipulation provided
for the establishment of a fuel and purchased power recovery rider beginning January&nbsp;1,
2010.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
filed its proposed fuel rider on October&nbsp;30, 2009.&#160; On December&nbsp;16, 2009 the PUCO issued an
order stating the rate was consistent with the Stipulation provisions, that it
does not appear to be unjust or unreasonable, and approved the rate to be
implemented on January&nbsp;1, 2010. The fuel rider will fluctuate based on
actual costs and recoveries and will be modified at the start of each seasonal
quarter:&#160; March&nbsp;1, June&nbsp;1,
September 1, and December&nbsp;1 each year. Consistent with the Stipulation, an
annual review and audit is scheduled to take place in the first quarter of 2011
for calendar year 2010.</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a member of PJM, <b>DP&amp;L</b> incurs costs and receives revenues from the RTO
related to its transmission and generation assets, as well as its load
obligations for retail customers.&#160; SB 221
included a provision that allows Ohio electric utilities to seek and obtain a
reconcilable rider to recover RTO-related costs and credits.&#160; In early 2009, the PUCO approved <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> request to defer costs associated with its
transmission, capacity, ancillary service and other PJM-related charges
incurred as a member of PJM consistent with the provisions of SB 221.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
subsequently filed to establish the TCRR that would incorporate all charges and
credits from the RTO as well as the amounts approved for deferral.&#160; The TCRR was approved by the PUCO and on June&nbsp;1,
2009 <b>DP&amp;L</b> began recovery of these
costs.&#160; In June&nbsp;2009, an application
for rehearing was filed claiming the PUCO&#146;s order allowing for recovery of RPM
costs through this rider was unlawful.&#160;&#160;
On September&nbsp;9, the PUCO granted rehearing, and issued an entry
ordering <b>DP&amp;L</b> to remove the RPM costs from
the TCRR and refile its tariffs.&#160; On September&nbsp;23,
2009, the Company filed two separate riders, a TCRR without RPM costs, and an
RPM recovery rider, which were both subsequently approved per PUCO Finding and
Order issued on November&nbsp;18, 2009, and implemented December&nbsp;1,
2009.&#160; There was no change to the level
of recovery due to the rehearing process.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;9, 2009, the PUCO issued an entry
establishing a significantly excessive earnings test (SEET) proceeding.&#160; A workshop was held at the PUCO offices on October&nbsp;5,
2009 to allow interested parties to present concerns and discuss issues related
to the methodology for determining whether an electric utility has
significantly excessive earnings pursuant to the provisions contained in SB
221.&#160; On November&nbsp;18, 2009, the PUCO
Staff issued its recommendations to the PUCO.&#160;
<b>DP&amp;L</b> filed its comments
and reply comments along with other interested parties.&#160; Although <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s
</b>Stipulation provides that the SEET does not apply to it until 2013
based on 2012 earnings results, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is actively participating in this proceeding.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;28, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed its application to establish
reliability targets consistent with the most recent PUCO Electric Service and
Safety Standards (ESSS).&nbsp; The PUCO issued a procedural schedule and held a
technical conference on November&nbsp;10, 2009.&nbsp; Comments and reply
comments were filed.&#160; We expect this case will be set for hearing.&#160; According to the ESSS rules, <b>DP&amp;L</b> will be subject to financial
penalties if the established targets are not met for two consecutive years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While
the overall financial impact of SB 221 will not be known for some time,
implementation of the bill and compliance with its requirements could have a
material impact on our financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Ohio
Competitive Considerations and Proceedings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, six unaffiliated marketers were registered as CRES providers in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service territory.&#160; While there has been some customer switching
associated with unaffiliated marketers, it represented less than 0.11% of sales
in 2009.&nbsp; DPLER, an affiliated company, is also a registered CRES provider
and accounted for 99% of the total kWh supplied by CRES providers within <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service territory in 2009.&nbsp;
During the first quarter of 2010, DPLER will begin providing CRES services to
business customers who are currently not in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
service territory.&#160; At this time, we do
not expect these incremental costs and revenues to have a material impact on
our results of operations, financial position or cash flows.&#160; In 2003-2004, several communities in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service area passed ordinances
allowing the communities to become government aggregators for the purpose of
offering alternative electric generation supplies to their citizens.&#160; To date, none of these communities have
aggregated their generation load.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Federal Matters</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Like other electric
utilities and energy marketers, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
and DPLE may sell or purchase electric products on the wholesale market.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
and DPLE compete with other generators, power marketers, privately and
municipally-owned electric utilities and rural electric cooperatives when
selling electricity.&#160; The ability of <b>DP&amp;L</b> and DPLE to sell this electricity
will depend on how <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> and
DPLE&#146;s price, terms and conditions compare to those of other suppliers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As part of Ohio&#146;s
electric deregulation law, all of the state&#146;s investor-owned utilities are
required to join a RTO.&#160; In October&nbsp;2004,
<b>DP&amp;L</b> successfully integrated its
1,000 miles of high-voltage transmission into the PJM RTO.&#160; The role of the RTO is to administer a competitive
wholesale market for electricity and ensure reliability of the transmission
grid.&#160; PJM ensures the reliability of the
high-voltage electric power system serving 51 million people in all or parts of
Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, New Jersey, North
Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia and the
District of Columbia.&#160; PJM coordinates
and directs the operation of the region&#146;s transmission grid, administers the
world&#146;s largest competitive wholesale electricity market and plans regional
transmission expansion improvements to maintain grid reliability and relieve
congestion.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13<a name="PB_13_001843_8146"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
PJM RPM base residual auction for the 2012/13 period cleared at a per megawatt
price of $16/day for our RTO area.&nbsp; Prior to this auction, the per
megawatt price for the 2011/2012 period was $110/day.&nbsp; Future RPM auction
results will be dependent not only on the overall supply and demand of
generation and load, but may also be impacted by congestion as well as PJM&#146;s
business rules&nbsp;relating to bidding for Demand Response and Energy
Efficiency resources in the RPM auctions.&nbsp; We cannot predict the outcome
of future auctions but if the current auction price is sustained, our future
results of operations, financial condition and cash flows could be adversely
impacted.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a member of PJM, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is also subject to charges and costs associated with PJM operations as approved
by the FERC.&nbsp; FERC Orders issued in 2007 regarding the allocation of costs
of large transmission facilities within PJM, could result in additional costs
being allocated to <b>DP&amp;L </b>of
approximately $12 million or more annually by 2012.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed a notice of appeal to the
U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit on March&nbsp;18, 2008 challenging the
allocation method.&nbsp; The appeal was consolidated with other appeals taken
by other interested parties of the same FERC Orders and the consolidated cases
were assigned to the 7</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;Circuit.&nbsp; On August&nbsp;6, 2009, the 7</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;Circuit ruled that the
FERC had failed to provide a reasoned basis for the allocation method it had
approved.&#160; Rehearings were filed by other
interested litigants and denied by the Court, which then remanded the matter to
the FERC for further proceedings.&#160;&#160; On January&nbsp;21,
2010, the FERC issued a procedural order on remand establishing a paper hearing
process under which PJM will make an informational filing in late
February.&nbsp; Subsequently PJM and other parties, including <b>DP&amp;L</b>, will be able to file initial comments, testimony,
and recommendations and reply comments.&nbsp; Absent future changes to the
procedural schedule that may occur for a number of reasons including if
settlement discussions are held, the paper hearing process should be complete
and the case ready for FERC consideration in 2010.&nbsp; FERC did not establish
a deadline for its issuance of a substantive order.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
cannot predict the timing or the likely outcome of the proceeding.&#160; Until such time as FERC may act to approve a
change in methodology, PJM will continue to apply the allocation methodology
that had been approved by FERC in 2007.&#160;
Although we continue to maintain that these costs should be borne by the
beneficiaries of these projects and that <b>DP&amp;L</b> is not
one of these beneficiaries, any new credits or additional costs resulting from
the ultimate outcome of this proceeding will be reflected in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> TCRR rider which is already in place to pass
through RTO-related costs and credits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> provides transmission
and wholesale electric service to twelve&nbsp;municipal customers in its
service territory, which in turn distribute electricity principally within
their incorporated limits.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> also maintains an interconnection agreement with
one municipality that has the capability to generate a portion of its own
energy requirements.&#160; Approximately one
percent of total electricity sales in 2009 represented sales to these
municipalities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
June&nbsp;2009, the NERC, a FERC-certified electric reliability organization
responsible for developing and enforcing mandatory reliability standards,
commenced a routine audit of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
operations.&#160; The audit, which was for the
period June&nbsp;18, 2007 to June&nbsp;25, 2009, evaluated <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
compliance with 42 requirements in 18 NERC-reliability standards.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
currently subject to a compliance audit at a minimum of once every three years
as provided by the NERC Rules&nbsp;of Procedure. This audit was concluded in June&nbsp;2009
and its findings revealed that <b>DP&amp;L</b> had some
Possible Alleged Violations (PAVs) associated with five NERC Reliability
Standards.&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to the report, <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed mitigation plans with NERC to address the
PAVs.&#160; These mitigation plans have been
accepted and <b>DP&amp;L</b> is currently awaiting a
proposal for settlement from NERC.&#160; While
we are currently unable to determine the extent of penalties, if any, that may
be imposed on <b>DP&amp;L</b>, we do not believe such
penalties will have a material impact on our results of operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ENVIRONMENTAL CONSIDERATIONS</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and<b>
DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> facilities and operations are subject to a wide range of
environmental regulations and laws by federal, state and local
authorities.&nbsp; The environmental issues that may impact us include:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Federal CAA and state laws and regulations (including State
Implementation Plans) which require compliance, obtaining permits and reporting
as to air emissions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Litigation with federal and certain state governments and certain
special interest groups regarding whether modifications to or maintenance of
certain coal-fired generating plants require additional permitting or pollution
control technology, or whether emissions from coal-fired generating plants
cause or contribute to global climate changes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rules&nbsp;issued by the USEPA and Ohio EPA that require substantial
reductions in SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, particulates, mercury and NOx
emissions.&nbsp; <b>DPL</b> has installed emission control
technology and is taking other measures to comply with required and anticipated
reductions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rules&nbsp;issued by the USEPA and Ohio EPA that require reporting and
future reductions of GHGs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rules&nbsp;issued by the USEPA associated with the Federal Clean Water
Act (FCWA), which prohibits the discharge of pollutants into waters of the
United States except pursuant to appropriate permits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Solid and hazardous waste laws and regulations, which govern the
management and disposal of certain waste. The majority of solid waste created
from the combustion of coal and fossil fuels is fly ash and other coal
combustion by-products.&#160; The EPA has
previously determined that fly ash and other coal combustion by-products are
not hazardous waste subject to the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
(RCRA), but the EPA is reportedly reconsidering that determination.&#160; A change in determination could significantly
increase the costs of disposing of such by-products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As well as imposing
continuing compliance obligations, these laws and regulations authorize the
imposition of substantial penalties for noncompliance, including fines,
injunctive relief and other sanctions.&#160;
In the normal course of business, we have investigatory and remedial
activities underway at these facilities to comply, or to determine compliance,
with such regulations.&nbsp; We record liabilities for probable estimated loss
in accordance with the provisions of GAAP relating to the accounting for
contingencies.<b>&#160; DPL,</b> through its wholly-owned
captive insurance subsidiary MVIC, has an actuarially calculated reserve of
$1.2 million for environmental matters.&#160;
We evaluate the potential liability related to probable losses quarterly
and may revise&nbsp;our estimates.&nbsp; Such revisions in the estimates of the
potential liabilities could have a material effect on our results of
operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Environmental
Regulation and Litigation Related to Air Quality</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Air Quality</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1990, the federal
government amended the CAA to further regulate air pollution.&#160; Under the law, the USEPA sets limits on how
much of a pollutant can be in the air anywhere in the United States.&#160; The CAA allows individual states to have
stronger pollution controls, but states are not allowed to have weaker
pollution controls than those set for the whole country.&#160; The CAA has a material effect on our
operations and such effects are detailed below with respect to certain programs
under the CAA.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;27, 2003,
the USEPA published final rules&nbsp;regarding the equipment replacement provision
(ERP) of the routine maintenance, repair and replacement (RMRR) exclusion of
the CAA.&nbsp; Activities at power plants that fall within the scope of the
RMRR exclusion do not trigger new source review requirements, including the
imposition of stricter emission limits.&#160;
On December&nbsp;24, 2003, the United States Court of Appeals for the
D.C. Circuit stayed the effective date of the rule&nbsp;pending its decision on
the merits of the lawsuits filed by numerous states and environmental
organizations challenging the final rules.&#160;
On June&nbsp;6, 2005, the USEPA issued its final response on the
reconsideration of the ERP exclusion.&#160;
The USEPA clarified its position, but did not change any aspect of the
2003 final rules.&#160; This decision was
appealed and the D.C. Circuit vacated the final rules&nbsp;on March&nbsp;17,
2006.&#160; The scope of the RMRR exclusion
remains uncertain due to this action by the D.C Circuit, as well as multiple
litigations not directly involving us where courts are defining the scope of
the exception with respect to the specific facts and circumstances of the
particular power plants and activities before the courts.&#160; While we believe that we have not engaged in
any activities with respect to our existing power plants that would trigger the
new source review requirements, if new source review requirements were imposed
on any of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> existing power plants, the
results could be materially adverse to us.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15<a name="PB_15_002002_455"></a></font></p>
