<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The court&#146;s decision, in
part, invalidated the new NOx annual emission allowance trading program and the
modifications to the SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;emission trading program, and created
uncertainty regarding future NOx and SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;emission reduction requirements and their timing.&#160; On December&nbsp;23, 2008, the court reversed
part of its decision that vacated CAIR.&#160;
Thus, CAIR currently remains in effect, but the USEPA remains subject to
the court&#146;s order to revise the program.&#160;
In January&nbsp;2010, the Court ordered the USEPA to file a response to
a Petition for Mandamus filed by parties in the original case who are now
seeking a Court order to require the USEPA to issue new regulations by March&nbsp;1,
2010.&#160; We cannot at this time predict the
timing or the outcome of any new regulations in relation to CAIR.&#160; CAIR has and will continue to have a material
effect on our operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the fourth quarter of
2007, <b>DP&amp;L</b> began a program for selling
excess emission allowances, including annual NOx emission allowances and SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2 </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">emission allowances that were the subject of CAIR
trading programs.&#160; In subsequent
quarters, <b>DP&amp;L</b> recognized gains from the sale
of excess emission allowances to third parties.&#160;
The court&#146;s CAIR decision has affected the trading market for excess
allowances and impacted <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> program
for selling additional excess allowances.&#160;
The overall impact of the court&#146;s decision, and of the actions the USEPA
or others will take in response to this decision, on <b>DPL</b>
and <b>DP&amp;L</b> is not fully known at this
time and could have an adverse effect on us.&#160;
In January&nbsp;2009, we resumed selling excess emission allowances due
to the revival of the trading market.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COMPETITION
AND PJM PRICING</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">RPM Capacity Auction Price</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The PJM RPM base residual
auction for the 2012/2013 period cleared at a per megawatt price of $16/day for
our RTO area.&nbsp; Prior to this auction, the per megawatt price for the
2011/2012 period was $110/day.&#160; Future
RPM auction results will be dependent not only on the overall supply and demand
of generation and load, but may also be impacted by congestion as well as PJM&#146;s
business rules&nbsp;relating to bidding for Demand Response and Energy
Efficiency resources in the RPM auctions.&#160;
We cannot predict the outcome of future auctions but if the current
auction price is sustained, our future results of operations, financial
condition and cash flows could be adversely impacted.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Ohio Competitive Considerations
and Proceedings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overall power market
prices, as well as government aggregation initiatives, could lead to the
entrance of competitors in our marketplace, affecting our results of
operations, financial condition or cash flows.&#160;
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, two additional
unaffiliated marketers registered as CRES providers in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service territory, bringing to
six the total number of unaffiliated CRES providers in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
service territory.&#160; While there has been
some customer switching associated with unaffiliated marketers, it represented
less than 0.11% of sales in 2009.&nbsp; DPLER, an affiliated company, is also a
registered CRES provider and accounted for 99% of the total kWh supplied by
CRES providers within <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
service territory in 2009.&#160; During the
first quarter of 2010, DPLER will begin providing CRES services to business
customers in Ohio who are not in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s </b>service
territory.&#160; At this time, we do not
expect the incremental costs and revenues to have a material impact on our
results of operations, financial position or cash flows.&#160; We currently cannot determine the extent to
which customer switching to unaffiliated CRES providers will occur in the
future and the impact this will have on our operations.&#160; In 2003-2004, several communities in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service area passed ordinances
allowing the communities to become government aggregators for the purpose of
offering alternative electric generation supplies to their citizens.&#160; To date, none of these communities have
aggregated their generation load.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FUEL AND RELATED COSTS</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fuel and Commodity Prices</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2009 and 2008, the
coal market experienced significant price volatility.&#160; We are now in a global market for coal in
which our domestic price is increasingly affected by international supply
disruptions and demand balance.&#160; Coal
exports from the U.S. have increased significantly in recent years.&#160; In addition, domestic issues like
government-imposed direct costs and permitting issues are affecting mining
costs and supply availability.&#160; Our
approach is to hedge the fuel costs for our anticipated electric sales.&#160; For the year ending December&nbsp;31, 2010,
we have hedged our coal requirements to meet our committed sales.&#160; We may not be able to hedge the entire
exposure of our operations from commodity price volatility.&#160; To the extent our suppliers do not meet their
contractual commitments or we are not hedged against price volatility, our
results of operations, financial position or cash flows could be materially
affected.&#160; Beginning in January&nbsp;2010,
the Ohio retail jurisdictional share of fuel price changes will be reflected in
the operation of the fuel rider, subject to PUCO review.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">38<a name="PB_38_004105_6479"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Sales of Coal and Excess Emission
Allowances</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> sold coal and excess emission allowances to various
counterparties realizing total net gains of $56.3 million and $5.0 million,
respectively.&#160; These gains are recorded
as a component of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> fuel
costs and reflected in operating income.&#160;
Coal sales are impacted by a range of factors but can be largely
attributed to the following: variation in power demand, the market price of
power compared to the cost to produce power, as well as optimization
opportunities in the coal market.&#160; Sales
of excess emission allowances are impacted, among other factors, by: general
economic conditions; fluctuations in market demand and pricing; availability of
excess inventory available for sale; and changes to the regulatory environment
in which we operate.&#160; The combined impact
of these factors on our ability to sell coal and emission allowances in 2010
and beyond is not fully known at this time and could materially impact the
amount of gains that will be recognized in the future.&#160; In addition, beginning in January&nbsp;2010
as part of the operation of the fuel rider, the Ohio retail jurisdictional
share of the emission gains and a portion of the Ohio jurisdictional share of
the coal gains will be used to reduce the overall rate charged to customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FINANCIAL OVERVIEW</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
financial overview relates to <b>DPL</b>, which
includes its principal subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>.&#160; The results of operations for both <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b> are
separately discussed in more detail following this financial overview.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, Net income for <b>DPL</b> was $229.1 million, or $2.01 per share, compared to Net
income of $244.5 million, or $2.12 per share, for the same period in 2008.&#160; All EPS amounts are on a diluted share basis.
</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;The decrease in net income compared to the
prior year was primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a
decrease in retail sales volume due to the impacts of the economic slowdown and
milder weather throughout the year,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a
decrease in wholesale power sales prices,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a
decrease in gains recognized from the sale of coal,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a
decrease in gains recognized from the sale of excess emission allowances,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an
increase in the cost of fuel due to the increased volume of generation by our
power plants and higher average fuel costs, particularly for coal, and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an increase in pension and employee
benefit related costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Partially offsetting these items were:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an
increase in retail rates primarily as a result of an increase in the EIR and
the implementation of the TCRR, RPM and Energy Efficiency riders,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an
improvement in generating plant performance which resulted in an increase in
wholesale sales volume and a decrease in purchased power volumes,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a
decrease in power purchase prices and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a net
reduction in interest costs primarily as a result of certain outstanding debt
redemptions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 41.25pt;text-indent:-23.25pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)</font></i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">For
purposes of discussing operating results, we present and discuss gross margins.
This format is useful to investors because it allows analysis and comparability
of operating trends and includes the same information that is used by
management to make decisions regarding our financial performance.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL &#150; Revenues</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail
customers, especially residential and commercial customers, consume more
electricity on warmer and colder days.&#160;
Therefore,<b> DPL&#146;s</b> retail
sales volume is impacted by the number of heating and cooling degree days
occurring during a year.&nbsp; Since<b> DPL</b>
plans to utilize its internal generating capacity to supply its retail
customers&#146; needs first, increases in retail demand may decrease the volume of
internal generation available to be sold in the wholesale market and vice
versa.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The wholesale market
covers a multi-state area and settles on an hourly basis throughout the
year.&#160; Factors impacting<b> DPL&#146;s</b> wholesale sales volume each hour of
the year include wholesale market prices;<b> DPL&#146;s</b>
retail demand; retail demand elsewhere throughout the entire wholesale market
area;<b> DPL</b> and non-<b>DPL</b> plants&#146; availability to sell into the
wholesale market and weather conditions across the multi-state region.<b> DPL&#146;s</b> plan is to make wholesale sales when
market prices allow for the economic operation of its generation facilities not
being utilized to meet its retail demand or when margin opportunities exist
between the wholesale sales and power purchase prices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Revenues decreased $12.7 million, or 1%, to $1,588.9 million from
$1,601.6 million in the prior year.&nbsp; This decrease was primarily the
result of lower retail sales volume as well as decreased wholesale average
prices, partially offset by higher average retail rates, increased wholesale
sales volume and an increase in RTO capacity and other revenues.&#160; The revenue components for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009 are further discussed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail revenues increased $5.7 million
resulting primarily from an 11% increase in average retail rates due largely to
the incremental effect of the recovery of costs under the third phase of the
EIR combined with the implementation of the TCRR, RPM, Energy Efficiency and
Alternative Energy riders, partially offset by a 9% decrease in sales volume
driven largely by the effects of the economic recession and milder weather
conditions.&#160; The milder weather
conditions saw heating and cooling degree days decrease by 4% and 14% to 5,561
days and 734 days, respectively.&#160; As a
result, retail revenues had a favorable $119.6 million price variance and an
unfavorable $113.5 million sales volume variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wholesale revenues decreased $27.4
million primarily as a result of a 42% decrease in wholesale average prices
partially offset by a 40% increase in sales volume, resulting in an unfavorable
$87.0 million wholesale price variance and a favorable $59.6 million sales
volume variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RTO capacity and other revenues,
consisting primarily of compensation for use of <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
transmission assets, regulation services, reactive supply and operating
reserves as well as capacity payments under the RPM construct, increased $9.0
million compared to the same period in the prior year.&#160; This increase was primarily the result of
additional revenue of $29.4 million that was realized from the PJM capacity
auction, partially offset by a decrease in PJM transmission and congestion
revenues of $21.0 million.&#160; Beginning June&nbsp;1,
2009 when the TCRR and RPM rate riders became effective, the Ohio retail
jurisdiction share of this change had no impact on net income.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">41<a name="PB_41_004213_5893"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, Revenues increased $85.9 million, or 6%, to $1,601.6 million from
$1,515.7 million in the prior year.&nbsp; This increase was primarily the result
of higher average rates for retail and wholesale sales as well as an increase
in RTO capacity and other revenues, partially offset by lower retail and
wholesale sales volumes.&#160; The revenue
components for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 are further discussed
below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail revenues increased $17.1 million
resulting primarily from a 4% increase in average retail rates due largely to
the second phase of the EIR, partially offset by a 2% decrease in sales volume.
&nbsp;The decrease in retail sales volume was primarily a result of milder
weather which caused cooling degree days to decrease by 26% to 853 days,
combined with a 6% decrease in the volume of sales to industrial
customers.&#160; The lower sales volumes to
industrial customers were driven largely by the downturn in the economy which
severely affected the automotive and other related industries in the region
resulting in plant closures and reduced production.&#160; These decreases were partially offset by a 9%
increase in heating degree days.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wholesale revenues decreased $30.4
million primarily as a result of a 33% decrease in sales volume due largely to
unplanned outages, partially offset by a 25% increase in wholesale average
rates, resulting in an unfavorable $60.2 million sales volume variance and a
favorable $29.8 million wholesale price variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RTO capacity and other revenues,
consisting primarily of compensation for use of <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
transmission assets, regulation services, reactive supply and operating
reserves as well as capacity payments under the RPM construct, increased $99.2
million compared to the prior year.&#160; This
increase primarily resulted from additional income realized from the PJM
capacity auction and increased PJM transmission and congestion revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DPL
&#150; Cost of Revenues</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fuel costs, which include coal (net of gains on
sales), gas, oil and emission allowances (net of gains on sales), increased
$87.4 million, or 36%, compared to 2008, primarily due to the impact of lower
gains realized from the sales of coal and excess emission allowances combined
with a 7% increase in the usage of fuel due mainly to the improved performance
of our generating facilities.&#160; In 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> realized $56.3 million and $5.0 million in gains
from the sales of coal and excess emission allowances, respectively, compared
to $83.4 million and $34.8 million, respectively, during 2008.&#160; Also contributing to the increase in fuel
costs was a 2% increase in the average cost of fuel consumed per kilowatt-hour
largely resulting from higher market prices of coal combined with outages at
lower-cost units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchased power decreased $117.2 million compared to
2008.&#160; The net decrease in purchased
power was due in part to lower volumes of purchased power and lower average
market rates of $72.3 million and $29.5 million, respectively.&#160; The improved performance of our generating
facilities, as mentioned in the preceding paragraph, resulted in increased
generation output and a reduced demand for higher-cost purchased power.&#160; Also contributing to the decrease in purchased
power were lower costs relating to other RTO charges as well as the net
deferral during 2009 of costs relating to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
transmission, capacity and other PJM-related charges which were incurred as a
member of PJM.&#160; This deferral is
discussed in greater detail in Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.&#160; These decreases were
partially offset by increased RTO capacity charges.&#160; We
purchase power to satisfy retail sales volume when generating facilities are
not available due to planned and unanticipated outages, or when market prices
are below the marginal costs associated with our generating facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fuel costs, which include coal (net of gains on
sales), gas, oil, and emission allowances (net of gains on sales), decreased
$85.2 million, or 26%, compared to 2007, primarily due to increases in net
gains of $33.6 million from the sale of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
excess emission allowances and $82.8 million realized from the sale of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> coal combined with a decrease in the usage of
fuel due mainly to a 6% decrease in generation output largely attributable to
unplanned outages.&#160; These decreases were
partially offset by increased fuel prices.&#160;
The successful installation of FGD equipment at Miami Fort, Killen and
J.M. Stuart stations has allowed us the ability to burn coal with a wide range
of sulfur content and, accordingly, we purchase and sell coal as we seek to
achieve optimum levels of production efficiency.&#160; Gains or losses from sales of coal and
emission allowances are recorded as components of fuel costs.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

million, or 31%, compared to 2007.&#160; The
increase in purchased power primarily results from a $15.3 million increase
relating to higher average market rates and a $98.4 million increase in RTO
capacity and other RTO charges, partially offset by a $23.5 million decrease
relating to lower volumes of purchased power.&#160;

retail sales volume when generating facilities are not available due to planned
and unplanned outages, or when market prices are below the marginal costs

  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">24.0</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.06%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="1" width="25%" noshade color="black" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(1)&nbsp;There
is a corresponding increase in revenues associated with these programs
resulting in no impact to net income.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Operation and maintenance expense increased $24.0 million, or 8%,
compared to 2008.&#160; This variance was
primarily the result of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">higher pension costs due largely to a
decline in the values of pension plan assets from 2008 and increased benefit
costs,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increases in assistance for low-income
retail customers which is funded by the USF revenue rate rider,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">expenses related to new energy efficiency
programs put in place for our customers during 2009,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increased deferred compensation costs,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increases in employee benefit expense
funded by the ESOP and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increased health insurance costs that were partially
related to higher disability reserves</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These increases were partially offset by:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">lower amortization of regulatory assets
related to the 2004/2005 deferred storm costs and PJM administrative fees in
2009 as these deferred costs were fully recovered through rates during 2008 and
in the first quarter of 2009, respectively, and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">decreases in expenses for generating
facilities largely due to unplanned outages in 2008 at lower-cost production
units resulting in higher costs in that year.&#160;
These decreases were partially offset by increased maintenance expenses
associated with unplanned outages at jointly-owned production units during
2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008,
Operation and maintenance expense decreased $1.1 million, or less than 1%, as
compared to 2007.&#160; This variance was
primarily due to:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a decrease in legal costs due largely to
the litigation settlement with three of our former executives in May&nbsp;2007,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a decrease in deferred compensation costs
associated to a large degree with deferred compensation liabilities for the
three former executives,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a decrease in employee compensation expense
associated with the ESOP due mainly to the additional shares that were released
from the ESOP in 2007 and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">lower pension costs primarily due to the
plan funding made in November&nbsp;2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These decreases were partially offset by:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the 2007 insurance settlement which
reimbursed us for legal fees relating to the litigation with three former
executives,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an increase in operating expenses largely
due to the operation of FGD and SCR equipment and related gypsum disposal,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the gain on sale of the corporate aircraft
realized in 2007 and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an increase in turbine maintenance costs
incurred due to an unplanned outage at a jointly-owned production unit.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 39.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL &#150; Depreciation and Amortization</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, Depreciation and amortization expense
increased $7.8 million, or 6%, compared to 2008 primarily as a result of higher
asset balances at the generating stations.&#160;
These higher balances were due largely to the completion of the FGD projects
during 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, Depreciation and amortization expense
increased $2.9 million, or 2%, as compared to 2007.&#160; This increase was primarily a result of
higher plant balances due largely to the installation of the FGD equipment,
partially offset by the impact of lower depreciation rates for generation
property which were put into effect on August&nbsp;1, 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL
&#150; General Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, General taxes decreased $7.4 million, or 6%,
compared to 2008 primarily due to lower property tax accruals in 2009 compared
to 2008 and lower kWh excise taxes resulting from lower retail sales volumes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, General taxes increased $13.7 million, or
12%, as compared to 2007, primarily as a result of higher property taxes due
mainly to capital improvements which have led to higher assessed property
values, combined with increased tax rates.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DPL
</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&#150;</font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
Investment Income (Loss)</font></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Investment income (loss) decreased $4.2 million, or 117%, as compared to
2008 primarily as a result of lower cash and short-term investment balances
combined with overall lower market yields on investments in 2009.&#160; In addition, we also recorded a $1.4 million
expense during 2009 relating to a loss incurred by DPL Capital Trust II, a
nonconsolidated wholly-owned subsidiary.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, Investment income (loss) decreased $7.7 million, or 68%, as compared to
2007.&#160; This decrease was primarily the
result of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$3.2 million of gains realized in 2007
from the sale of financial assets held in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s </b>Master
Trust Plan for deferred compensation which were used for the settlement payment
to three former executives and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">lower cash and short-term investment
balances combined with overall lower market yields on investments in 2008
compared to 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL &#150; Net
Gain on Settlement of Executive Litigation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;21,
2007, we settled litigation with three former executives.&#160; In exchange for our payment of $25 million,
the three former executives relinquished and dismissed all of their claims,
including those related to deferred compensation, RSUs, MVE incentives, stock
options and legal fees.&#160; As a result of
this settlement, during 2007, <b>DPL</b> realized a
net pre-tax gain in continuing operations of approximately $31.0 million.&#160; See Note 17 of Notes to Consolidated
Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#150;</font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;"> Interest Expense</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Interest expense decreased $7.7 million, or 8%, compared to 2008
primarily due to:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a $12.8 million
reduction in Interest expense due to the redemption of <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$175 million 8.00%
Senior Notes and the $100 million 6.25%
Senior Notes in March&nbsp;2009 and May&nbsp;2008, respectively,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a $1.6 million
write-off in 2008 of unamortized debt issuance costs relating to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> $90 million variable rate pollution control bonds
following their repurchase from the bondholders in April&nbsp;2008 and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.0 million of deferred interest
carrying costs on regulatory assets primarily associated with the 2008
incremental storm costs and the riders for RPM and TCRR.&#160; These regulatory assets are further discussed
in Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The above decreases were
partially offset by $6.4 million of lower capitalized interest in 2009 compared
to 2008, due largely to the completion of the FGD projects at our <b>DP&amp;L</b> and partner-operated generating stations, as well
as a $3.7 million premium paid on the early redemption of a portion of <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Note to DPL Capital Trust II which is due 2031.&#160; In December&nbsp;2009, <b>DPL</b>
redeemed $52.4 million of this $195 million 8.125% note.&#160; This redemption is further discussed in Note
7 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, Interest expense increased $9.7 million,
or 12%, as compared to 2007 primarily due to:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$12.9 million of lower
capitalized interest due to the completion of the FGD projects at Miami Fort,
Killen and J.M. Stuart stations,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the write-off of unamortized
debt issuance costs amounting to $1.6 million relating to pollution control
bonds following their repurchase from the bondholders in April&nbsp;2008 and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$0.9 million of additional
interest expense associated with <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> $90
million variable rate pollution control bonds issued November&nbsp;15, 2007 and
repurchased in April&nbsp;2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These
increases were partially offset by a $7.0 million interest expense reduction
due to the redemption of the $225 million 8.25% Senior Notes in March&nbsp;2007
and the $100 million 6.25% Senior Notes in May&nbsp;2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#150; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Other Income (Deductions)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, there were no material fluctuations in the balances of Other income
(deductions).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, other deductions of $1.0 million changed from other income of $2.9
million recorded in 2007.&#160; The change
from other income to other deductions primarily resulted from the recognition
in 2007 of a $2.1 million deferred credit related to a litigation settlement
(which was not part of the executive litigation settlement).</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DPL
</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&#150;</font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
Income Tax Expense</font></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Income tax expense increased $9.6 million, or 9%, compared to 2008, due
to estimate to actual adjustments of 2008 taxes related to the Internal Revenue
Code Section&nbsp;199 deduction, adjustments to deferred tax liabilities and a
2008 settlement relating to the Ohio Franchise Tax.&#160; These increases were partially offset by a
decrease in pre-tax book earnings, estimate to actual adjustments of 2008 state
tax liabilities, adjustments to our current tax receivables and the phase-out
of the Ohio Franchise Tax.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2008, Income tax
expense decreased $19.6 million, or 16%, as compared to 2007, primarily due to
a decrease in the effective tax rate reflecting the phase-out of the Ohio
Franchise Tax and the 2008 settlement of the Ohio Franchise Tax issue which
resulted in a recorded tax benefit of $8.5 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">RESULTS OF OPERATIONS &#150; The Dayton
Power and Light Company (DP&amp;L)</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L &#150; Revenues</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail customers,
especially residential and commercial customers, consume more electricity on
warmer and colder days.&#160; Therefore,<b> DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> retail sales volume is impacted
by the number of heating and cooling degree days occurring during a year.&nbsp;
Since<b> DP&amp;L</b> plans to utilize
its internal generating capacity to supply its retail customers&#146; needs first,
increases in retail demand may decrease the volume of internal generation
available to be sold in the wholesale market and vice versa.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
wholesale market covers a multi-state area and settles on an hourly basis
throughout the year.&#160; Factors impacting<b> DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> wholesale sales volume each
hour of the year include wholesale market prices;<b> DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> retail demand, retail demand elsewhere throughout
the entire wholesale market area;<b> DP&amp;L</b>
and non-<b>DP&amp;L</b> plants&#146;
availability to sell into the wholesale market and weather conditions across
the multi-state region.<b>&#160; DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> plan is to make
wholesale sales when market prices allow for the economic operation of its
generation facilities that are not being utilized to meet its retail demand or
when margin opportunities exist between the wholesale sales and power purchase
prices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Revenues decreased $22.5 million, or 1%, to $1,550.4 million from
$1,572.9 million in the prior year.&nbsp; This decrease was primarily the
result of lower wholesale average prices and lower retail sales volume,
partially offset by higher average retail rates and increased wholesale sales
volume.&#160; The revenue components for the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 are further discussed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail revenues increased $91.9 million
resulting primarily from a 20% increase in average retail rates due largely to
the incremental effect of the third phase of the EIR and the implementation of
the TCRR, RPM, Energy Efficiency and Alternative Energy rate riders, partially
offset by a 9% decrease in retail sales volume driven largely by the effects of
the economic recession and milder weather conditions.&#160; The milder weather conditions saw heating and
cooling degree days decrease by 4% and 14% to 5,561 days and 734 days,
respectively.&#160; As a result, retail
revenues had a favorable $191.7 million price variance and an unfavorable $99.7
million sales volume variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wholesale revenues decreased $111.6
million primarily as a result of a 56% decrease in wholesale average prices,
partially offset by a 41% increase in sales volume, resulting in an unfavorable
$230.5 million wholesale price variance and a favorable $118.9 million sales
volume variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RTO capacity and other revenues,
consisting primarily of compensation for use of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
transmission assets, regulation services, reactive supply and operating
reserves, as well as capacity payments under the RPM construct, decreased $2.8
million compared to the prior year.&#160; This
decrease primarily resulted from $22.2 million of lower transmission and
congestion revenues, partially offset by additional revenue of $19.4 million
that was realized from the PJM capacity auction.&#160; Beginning June&nbsp;1, 2009 when the TCRR and
RPM rate deferral riders became effective, the Ohio retail jurisdiction share
of this change had no impact on Net income.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">47<a name="PB_47_004333_9799"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, Revenues increased $65.5 million, or 4%, to $1,572.9 million from
$1,507.4 million in the same period of the prior year.&nbsp; This increase was
primarily the result of higher average rates for retail and wholesale sales, as
well as an increase in RTO capacity and other revenues, partially offset by
lower retail and wholesale sales volumes.&#160;
The revenue components for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 are
further discussed below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail revenues increased $17.9 million
resulting primarily from a 4% increase in average retail rates due largely to
the second phase of the EIR, partially offset by a 2% decrease in sales
volume.&#160; The decrease in retail sales
volume was primarily a result of milder weather which caused cooling degree
days to decrease by 26% to 853 days, combined with a 6% decrease in the volume
of sales to industrial customers.&#160; The
lower sales volumes to industrial customers were driven largely by the downturn
in the economy which has severely affected the automotive and other related
industries in the region resulting in plant closures and reduced
production.&#160; These decreases were
partially offset by a 9% increase in heating degree days.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wholesales revenues decreased $38.2
million primarily as a result of a 35% decrease in sales volume due largely to
unplanned outages, partially offset by a 37% increase in wholesale average
rates, resulting in an unfavorable $117.4 million sales volume variance and a
favorable $79.2 million wholesale price variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RTO capacity and other revenues,
consisting primarily of compensation for use of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
transmission assets, regulation services, reactive supply and operating
reserves, as well as capacity payments under the RPM construct, increased $85.8
million compared to the prior year.&#160; This
increase primarily resulted from additional income realized from the PJM
capacity auction and increased PJM transmission and congestion revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DP&amp;L &#150; Cost of Revenues</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fuel costs, which include coal (net of
gains on sales), gas, oil and emission allowances (net of gains on sales),
increased $92.2 million, or 40%, compared to 2008, primarily due to the impact
of lower gains realized from the sales of coal and excess emission allowances
combined with a 7% increase in the usage of fuel due mainly to the improved
performance of our generating facilities.&#160;
In 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> realized $56.3 million
and $5.0 million in gains from the sales of coal and excess emission
allowances, respectively, compared to $83.4 million and $34.8 million,
respectively, during 2008.&#160; Also
contributing to the increase in fuel costs was a 3% increase in the average
cost of fuel consumed per kilowatt-hour largely resulting from higher market
prices of coal combined with outages at lower-cost units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchased power decreased $120.7 million
compared to 2008.&#160; The net decrease in
purchased power was due in part to lower volumes of purchased power and lower
average market rates of $74.8 million and $30.8 million, respectively.&#160; The improved performance of our generating
facilities, as mentioned in the preceding paragraph, resulted in increased
generation output and a reduced demand for higher-cost purchased power.&#160; Also contributing to the decrease in purchased
power were lower costs relating to other RTO charges as well as the net
deferral during 2009 of costs relating to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
transmission, capacity and other PJM-related charges which were incurred as a
member of PJM.&#160; This deferral is
discussed in greater detail in Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.&#160; These decreases were
partially offset by increased RTO capacity charges.&#160; We
purchase power to satisfy retail sales volume when generating facilities are
not available due to planned and unanticipated outages, or when market prices
are below the marginal costs associated with our generating facilities.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">48<a name="PB_48_004333_4015"></a></font></p>
