<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fuel costs, which include coal (net of
gains on sales), gas, oil and emission allowances (net of gains on sales),
decreased $84.0 million, or 27%, compared to 2007, primarily due to increases
in net gains of $33.6 million from the sale of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
excess emission allowances and $82.8 million realized from the sale of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> coal combined with a decrease in the usage of
fuel due mainly to a 6% decrease in generation output largely attributable to
unplanned outages. &#160;These decreases were
partially offset by increased fuel prices.&#160;
The successful installation of FGD equipment at Miami Fort, Killen and
J.M. Stuart stations has allowed us the ability to burn coal with a wide range
of sulfur content and, accordingly, we purchase and sell coal as we seek to
achieve optimum levels of production efficiency.&#160; Gains or losses from sales of coal and
emission allowances are recorded as components of fuel costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchased power costs increased $79.6
million, or 27%, compared to 2007.&#160; The
increase in purchased power primarily results from an $11.8 million increase
relating to higher average market rates and a $97.2 million increase in RTO
capacity and other RTO charges, partially offset by a $29.3 million decrease
relating to lower volumes of purchased power.&#160;
We purchase power to satisfy
retail sales volume when generating facilities are not available due to planned
and unplanned outages, or when market prices are below the marginal costs
associated with our generating facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(1)&nbsp;&#160; There is a corresponding increase in Revenues
associated with these programs resulting in no impact to Net income.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, Operation and maintenance expense
increased $20.4 million, or 7%, compared to 2008.&#160; This variance was primarily the result of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">higher pension costs due largely to a
decline in the values of pension plan assets from 2008 and increased benefit
costs,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increases in assistance for low-income
retail customers which is funded by the USF revenue rate rider,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">expenses related to new energy efficiency
programs put in place for our customers during 2009,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increases in employee benefit expense
funded by the ESOP and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">increased health insurance costs that were
partially related to higher disability reserves.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These increases are partially offset by:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">lower amortization of regulatory assets
related to the 2004/2005 deferred storm costs and PJM administrative fees in
2009 as these deferred costs were fully recovered through rates during 2008 and
in the first quarter of 2009, respectively, and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">decreases in expenses for generating
facilities largely due to unplanned outages in 2008 at lower-cost production
units resulting in higher costs in that year.&#160;
These decreases were partially offset by increased maintenance expenses
associated with unplanned outages at jointly-owned production units during
2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008,
Operation and maintenance expense decreased $8.8 million, or 3%, as compared to
2007.&#160; This variance was primarily due
to:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a decrease in employee compensation expense associated
with the ESOP due mainly to the additional shares that were released from the
ESOP in 2007,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a decrease in deferred compensation costs associated
to a large degree with deferred compensation liabilities for three former
executives,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a decrease in legal fees and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">lower pension costs primarily due to the plan funding
made in November&nbsp;2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These decreases were
partially offset by:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an increase in operating expenses at our generating
facilities largely due to the operation of the FGD and SCR equipment and
related gypsum disposal,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an increase in turbine maintenance costs incurred due
to an unplanned outage at a jointly-owned production unit and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an increase in boiler maintenance expenses in 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L
&#150; Depreciation and Amortization</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Depreciation and amortization expense increased $7.7 million, or 6%, as
compared to 2008 primarily as a result of higher asset balances at the
generating stations.&#160; These higher
balances were due largely to the completion of the FGD projects during 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, Depreciation and amortization expense
increased $3.3 million, or 3%, as compared to 2007.&#160; This increase was primarily a result of
higher plant balances due largely to the installation of FGD equipment,
partially offset by the impact of lower depreciation rates for generation
property which were put into effect on August&nbsp;1, 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L
&#150; General Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, General taxes decreased $7.4 million, or 6%,
compared to 2008 primarily due to lower property tax accruals in 2009 compared
to 2008 and lower kWh excise taxes resulting from lower retail sales volumes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, General taxes increased $13.9 million, or
13%, as compared to 2007, primarily as a result of higher property taxes due
mainly to capital improvements which have led to higher assessed property
values, combined with increased tax rates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L &#150; Investment Income</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Investment income (loss) decreased $4.2 million, or 60%, as compared to
2008 primarily as a result of lower gains realized from the sale of <b>DPL </b>common stock from <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Master Trust Plan used for deferred compensation distributions as well as lower
cash and short-term investment balances combined with overall lower market
yields on investments in 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, Investment income (loss) decreased $16.7 million, or 70%, as compared to
2007.&#160; This decrease was primarily the
result of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 39.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$14.8 million of gains realized in 2007
on the transfer of <b>DPL</b> common
stock to the <b>DP&amp;L</b> Retirement Income Plan
Trust (Pension) and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 39.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 39.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$3.2 million of gains realized in 2007
from the sale of financial assets held in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Master Trust Plan for deferred compensation which were used for the settlement
payment to three former executives.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 39.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L &#150; Net Gain on Settlement
of Executive Litigation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;21, 2007, we
settled litigation with three former executives.&#160; In exchange for our payment of $25 million,
the three former executives relinquished and dismissed all of their claims,
including those related to deferred compensation, RSUs, MVE incentives, stock
options and legal fees.&#160; As a result of
this settlement, in 2007, <b>DP&amp;L </b>realized
a net pre-tax gain in continuing operations of approximately $35.3
million.&#160; See Note 17 of Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L &#150;
</font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Interest Expense</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Interest expense increased $2.0 million, or 5%, as compared to 2008
primarily as a result of $6.4 million of lower capitalized interest due largely
to the completion of the FGD projects at our own and partner-operated
generating stations.&#160; This increase was
partially offset by:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a $1.6 million write-off in 2008
of unamortized debt issuance costs relating to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
$90 million variable rate pollution control bonds following their repurchase
from the bondholders in April&nbsp;2008 and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$2.0 million of deferred interest carrying costs on
regulatory assets primarily associated with the 2008 incremental storm costs
and the riders for RPM and TCRR.&#160; These
Regulatory assets are further discussed in Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated
Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, Interest expense increased $14.2 million, or 64%, as compared to 2007
primarily as a result of:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$12.9 million of lower capitalized interest due to the
completion of the FGD projects at Miami Fort, Killen, and J.M. Stuart stations,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the write-off of unamortized debt issuance costs
amounting to $1.6 million relating to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> $90
million variable rate pollution control bonds following their repurchase from
the bondholders in April&nbsp;2008 and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$0.9 million of additional Interest expense associated
with <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s </b>$90 million variable rate
pollution control bonds issued in November&nbsp;2007 and repurchased in April&nbsp;2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L &#150; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Other Income (Deductions)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, there were no material fluctuations in the balances of Other income
(deductions).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, Other deductions of $1.1 million changed from Other income of $2.9
million recorded in 2007.&#160; The change
from Other income to Other deductions primarily resulted from the recognition
in 2007 of a $2.1 million deferred credit related to a litigation settlement
(which was not part of the executive litigation settlement).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DP&amp;L
&#150;</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">  </font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income
Tax Expense</font></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Income tax expense increased $4.3 million, or 4%, compared to 2008, due
to estimate to actual adjustments of 2008 income taxes related to the Internal
Revenue Code Section&nbsp;199 deduction, adjustments to deferred tax
liabilities and a 2008 settlement relating to the Ohio Franchise Tax.&#160; These increases were partially offset by a
decrease in pre-tax book earnings, estimate to actual adjustments of 2008 state
tax liabilities, adjustments to our current tax receivables and the phase-out
of the Ohio Franchise Tax.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2008, Income tax
expense decreased $22.9 million, or 16%, as compared to 2007, primarily due to
a decrease in the effective tax rate reflecting the phase-out of the Ohio
Franchise Tax and the 2008 settlement of the Ohio Franchise Tax issue which
resulted in a recorded tax benefit of $8.5 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The significant items
that have impacted the cash flows for <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b> are further discussed in greater detail below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Cash
Provided by Operating Activities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The tariff-based revenue
from our energy business continues to be the principal source of cash from
operating activities while our primary uses of cash include payments for fuel, purchased
power, operation and maintenance expenses, interest and taxes.&#160; Management believes that the diversified
retail customer mix of residential, commercial and industrial classes coupled
with rate relief approved by the PUCO provides us with a reasonably predictable
gross cash flow from operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, Net cash provided by operating activities was primarily a result of
Earnings from continuing operations adjusted for noncash depreciation and
amortization, combined with the following significant transactions:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the
$201.6 million increase to Deferred income taxes primarily results from the
recognition of certain tax benefits for 2008 and 2009 relating to a change in
the tax accounting method for deductions pertaining to repairs, depreciation
and mixed service costs.&#160; Primarily due
to the recognition of these benefits during 2009, <b>DPL</b>
received a net cash refund of state and federal income taxes totaling $94.6
million and, in addition, was able to offset $69.0 million of these benefits
against income tax liabilities accrued in 2009;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the
$15.7 million of cash used to pay for transmission, capacity and other
PJM-related costs incurred during 2009, net of recoveries.&#160; These costs were recorded as a Regulatory
asset in accordance with the provisions of GAAP relating to regulatory accounting
(see Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements) and are expected to
be collected from customers during future years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Other
represents items that had a current period cash flow impact and includes
changes in working capital and other future rights or obligations to receive or
to pay cash.&#160; These items are primarily
impacted by, among other factors, the timing of when cash payments are made for
fuel, purchased power, operating costs, interest and taxes, and when cash is
received from our utility customers and from the sales of coal and excess
emission allowances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008,<b>  </b>Net cash provided by operating
activities was primarily a result of Earnings from continuing operations
adjusted for noncash depreciation and amortization, combined with the following
significant transactions:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Deferred
income taxes increased by $43.1 million as a result of the acceleration of the
deduction of newly installed FGD and SCR equipment for tax purposes, which had
the effect of reducing current period income tax payments and increasing cash
on hand,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the
$42 million cash payment made in 2008 to the ODT following a tax settlement
agreement and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the
$13.1 million of cash used to restore damage of a non-capital nature caused by
the hurricane-force winds of September&nbsp;2008 and other major 2008
storms.&#160; These costs were recorded as a
Regulatory asset in accordance with the provisions of GAAP relating to
regulatory accounting (see Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements)
and are expected to be collected from customers during future years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Other
represents items that had a current period cash flow impact and includes
changes in working capital and other future rights or obligations to receive or
to pay cash, such as regulatory assets and liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, Net cash provided by operating activities was primarily a result of
Earnings from continuing operations adjusted for noncash depreciation and
amortization and the noncash impact of the net gain realized on settlement of
the executive litigation.&#160; Other represents
items that had a current period cash flow impact and includes changes in
working capital and other future rights or obligations to receive or to pay
cash, such as regulatory assets and liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For all years, the
environmental-related capital expenditures relate to cash outflows incurred
during the installation and upgrades of FGD and SCR equipment.&#160; Other plant-related asset acquisitions relate
to investments in other generation, transmission and distribution equipment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009,<b> DP&amp;L </b>continued to see reductions
in its environmental-related capital expenditures due to the completion of FGD
and SCR projects.&#160; The expenditures in
2009 relate to the construction of FGD and SCR equipment at the Conesville
generation station which was substantially completed and placed into service
during the fourth quarter of 2009.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> also continued to make upgrades and other
investments in other generation, transmission and distribution equipment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008,<b> DP&amp;L</b> saw reduced cash outflows
associated with environmental-related expenditures compared to 2007 due to
projects relating to the installation of FGD and SCR equipment that had either
been completed or were nearing completion.&#160;
In addition, <b>DP&amp;L</b> was
forced to replace a portion of its distribution lines and equipment following
the damage caused by the hurricane-force winds of September&nbsp;2008 and other
2008 storms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007,<b>  </b>the proceeds received from asset sales
relate to the sale of two DPLE peaker units and an aircraft previously owned by
a <b>DPL</b> subsidiary.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL &#150; Net Cash used for Financing
Activities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> Net cash used for financing activities
for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, 2008 and 2007 can be summarized as
follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="86%" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:86.66%;">
 <tr>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009,<b> DPL</b> redeemed long-term debt totaling
$227.4 million and paid common stock dividends of $128.8 million.&#160; Under a stock repurchase program approved by
the Board of Directors in October&nbsp;2009 (see Note 14 of Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements), <b>DPL</b> repurchased
approximately 2.4 million <b>DPL</b> common
shares for $64.4 million.&#160; In addition, <b>DPL</b> repurchased 8.6 million warrants for $25.2 million.&#160; <b>DPL&#146;s</b> cash
inflows during the period include $77.7 million received from the cash exercise
of 3.7 million warrants and the withdrawal of the remaining balance of
restricted funds of $14.5 million which was used primarily to fund the
construction of FGD equipment at the Conesville generation station.&#160; <b>DPL</b> also
received $9.0 million from option holders who exercised stock options due, in
part, to the increase in our average stock price compared to 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, <b>DPL</b> paid common stock dividends of
$120.5 million, retired $100 million of long-term debt and withdrew $32.5
million from restricted funds held in trust to pay for environmental-related
capital expenditures.&#160; In comparison to
2007,<b>  </b>the lower cash withdrawals from
restricted funds in 2008 were primarily due to the timing of costs incurred
relating to the installation of FGD and SCR equipment.&#160; In addition, the<b>  </b>reduced
cash proceeds in 2008 from the exercise of stock options were a direct result
of fewer options exercised.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, <b>DPL</b> retired $225 million of long-term
debt, paid common stock dividends of $111.7 million, withdrew $63.2 million
from restricted funds to pay for environmental-related capital expenditures and
received $14.6 million from the exercise of stock options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

balance of $14.5 million from restricted funds to pay for the Conesville FGD
and SCR projects.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008,<b> DP&amp;L</b> paid $155 million in
dividends to <b>DPL,</b> withdrew $32.5 million from
restricted funds held in trust and repaid the net $20 million short-term loan
from <b>DPL</b>.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, <b>DP&amp;L</b> paid $125 million in dividends
to <b>DPL,</b> withdrew $63.2 million from
restricted funds held in trust and received a net $20 million short-term loan
from <b>DPL</b>.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We expect our existing
sources of liquidity to remain sufficient to meet our anticipated
obligations.&#160; Our business is capital
intensive, requiring significant resources to fund operating expenses,
construction expenditures, scheduled debt maturities, and interest and dividend
payments.&#160; For 2010 and in subsequent
years, we expect to satisfy these requirements with a combination of cash from
operations and funds from the capital markets as our internal liquidity needs
and market conditions warrant.&#160; We also
expect that the borrowing capacity under credit facilities will continue to be
available to manage working capital requirements during those periods.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have access to $320
million of short-term financing under two revolving credit facilities.&#160; The first facility for $220 million expires November&nbsp;2011
and has three participating banks; the lead bank has a total commitment of 36%
while the other two have commitments of 32% each.&#160; The second facility is a 364-day $100 million
facility that matures April&nbsp;2010.&#160; A
total of six banks participate in this facility, with no bank having more than
26% of the total commitment.&#160; The two
bank groups have no common members.&#160; We
are currently evaluating the impact the maturity of the $100 million facility
will have on our future liquidity and would expect to be able to renew or
replace this facility as needed.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital projects are
subject to continuing review and are revised in light of changes in financial
and economic conditions, load forecasts, legislative and regulatory
developments and changing environmental standards, among other factors.&#160; <b>DPL </b>is
projecting to spend an estimated $590 million in capital projects for the
period 2010 through 2012, mostly through its subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Planned construction
additions for 2010 relate primarily to new investments in and upgrades to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> power plant equipment and
transmission and distribution systems.&#160;
In addition to our capital requirements above, on August&nbsp;4, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> re-filed its smart grid and advanced metering
infrastructure (AMI) business cases with the PUCO under which it would spend
approximately $270 million on capital projects during the period 2010 through
2012.&#160; Approval from the PUCO of these
cases is still pending.&#160; The re-filing at
the PUCO is further discussed in Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability to complete
capital projects and the reliability of future service will be affected by our
financial condition, the availability of internal funds and the reasonable cost
of external funds.&#160; We expect to finance
our construction additions with a combination of cash on hand, short-term
financing, long-term debt and cash flows from operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)&nbsp; Credit rating relates to <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Senior

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Off-Balance
Sheet Arrangements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL &#150; Guarantees</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the normal course of
business, <b>DPL </b>enters into various agreements with its
wholly-owned subsidiaries, DPLE and DPLER, providing financial or performance
assurance to third parties.&#160; These
agreements are entered into primarily to support or enhance the
creditworthiness otherwise attributed to DPLE and DPLER on a stand-alone basis, thereby facilitating the extension of
sufficient credit to accomplish DPLE&#146;s and DPLER&#146;s intended commercial
purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,
2009, <b>DPL</b> had $51 million of
guarantees to third parties for future financial or performance assurance under
such agreements, on behalf of DPLE and DPLER.&#160;
The guarantee arrangements entered into by<b> DPL</b>
with these third parties cover all present and future obligations of DPLE and
DPLER to such beneficiaries and are terminable at any time by <b>DPL</b> upon written notice to the beneficiaries.&#160; The carrying amount of obligations for commercial
transactions covered by these guarantees and recorded in our Consolidated
Balance Sheets was $0.6&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and $1.6 million
at December&nbsp;31, 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In two separate
transactions in November&nbsp;and December&nbsp;2006, <b>DPL</b>
also agreed to be a guarantor of the obligations of DPLE regarding the sale in April&nbsp;2007
of the Darby Electric Peaking Station to American Electric Power and the sale
of the Greenville Electric Peaking Station to Buckeye Electric Power,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; In both cases, <b>DPL</b>
agreed to guarantee the obligations of DPLE over a multiple-year period as
follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2009, neither <b>DPL</b> nor <b>DP&amp;L</b>
incurred any losses related to the guarantees of DPLE&#146;s obligations and we
believe it is remote that either <b>DPL</b>
or <b>DP&amp;L</b> would be required to
perform or incur any losses in the future associated with any of the above
guarantees of DPLE&#146;s obligations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L
&#150; Equity Ownership Interest</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> owns a 4.9% equity ownership interest in
OVEC, an electric generation company.&#160; As
of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> could be responsible for the
repayment of 4.9%, or $54.4 million, of a $1,110 million debt obligation that
matures in 2026.&#160; This would only happen
if OVEC defaulted on its debt payments.&#160;
As of December&nbsp;31, 2009,
we have no knowledge of such a default.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Coal contracts:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, through its principal subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L,</b> has entered into various
long-term coal contracts to supply the coal requirements for the generating
plants it operates.&#160; Some contract prices
are subject to periodic adjustment and have features that limit price
escalation in any given year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Limestone
contracts:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, through its principal subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L,</b> has entered into various
limestone contracts to supply limestone used in the operation of FGD equipment
at its generating facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchase orders
and other contractual obligations:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b> had various other contractual
obligations including non-cancelable contracts to purchase goods and services
with various terms and expiration dates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reserve for
uncertain tax positions:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to the uncertainty
regarding the timing of future cash outflows associated with our unrecognized
tax benefits of $19.3 million, we are unable to make a reliable estimate of the
periods of cash settlement with the respective tax authorities and have not
included such amounts in the contractual obligations table above.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">MARKET RISK</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
are subject to certain market risks including, but not limited to, changes in
commodity prices for electricity, coal, environmental emissions and gas and
fluctuations in interest rates.&#160; We use
various market risk sensitive instruments, including derivative contracts,
primarily to limit our exposure to fluctuations in commodity pricing.&#160; Our Commodity Risk Management Committee
(CRMC), comprising of members of senior management, is responsible for
establishing risk management policies and the monitoring and reporting of risk
exposures relating to our <b>DP&amp;L</b>-operated
generation units. The CRMC meets on a regular basis with the objective of
identifying, assessing and quantifying material risk issues and developing strategies
to manage these risks.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Commodity Pricing Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commodity pricing risk
exposure includes the impacts of weather, market demand, increased competition
and other economic conditions.&#160; To manage
the volatility relating to these exposures at our <b>DP&amp;L</b>-operated
generation units, we use a variety of non-derivative and derivative instruments
including forward contracts and futures contracts.&#160; These derivative instruments are used
principally for economic hedging purposes and none are held for trading purposes.&#160; The majority of our commodity contracts are
not considered derivative instruments under GAAP and are therefore excluded
from MTM accounting.&#160; Derivatives that
fall within the scope of derivative accounting under GAAP must be recorded at
their fair value and marked to market unless they qualify for hedge
accounting.&#160; MTM gains and losses on
derivative instruments that qualify for hedge accounting are deferred in AOCI
until the forecasted transactions occurs.&#160;
We adjust the derivative instruments that do not qualify for cash flow
hedging to fair value on a monthly basis and where applicable, we recognize a
corresponding Regulatory asset for above-market costs or a regulatory liability
for below-market costs in accordance with Regulatory accounting under GAAP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2008 and 2009, the
coal market has experienced unprecedented price volatility.&#160; The coal market has increasingly been
influenced by both international and domestic supply and consumption and, while
we have all of the total expected coal volume needed to meet our retail and
firm wholesale sales requirements for 2010 under contract, sales requirements
may change, particularly for retail load.&#160;
To the extent we are not able to hedge against price volatility or
recover increases through our fuel rider that began in January&nbsp;2010, our
results of operations, financial position or cash flows could be materially
affected.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The net asset/liability
of the MTM positions above are expected to mature within the next three years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For purposes of potential
risk analysis, we use a sensitivity analysis to quantify potential impacts of
market rate changes on the statements of results of operations.&#160; The sensitivity analysis represents
hypothetical changes in market values that may or may not occur in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

capacity in the wholesale market.&#160; Energy
in excess of the needs of existing retail customers is sold in the wholesale
market when we can identify opportunities with positive margins.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> fuel (including coal, gas, oil and
emission allowances) and purchased power costs as a percentage of total
operating costs in the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008 were 33% and
33%, respectively.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> fuel (including coal, gas, oil
and emission allowances) and purchased power costs as a percentage of total
operating costs were 33% and 34% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and
2008, respectively.&#160; We have
substantially all of the total expected coal volume needed to meet our retail
and firm wholesale sales requirements for 2010 under contract.&#160; The majority of our contracted coal is
purchased at fixed prices although some contracts provide for periodic pricing
adjustments.&#160; We do not expect to
purchase SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2 </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">allowances for 2010; however, the exact
consumption of SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2 </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">allowances will depend on market prices
for power, availability of our generation units and the actual sulfur content
of the coal burned.&#160; We do not plan to
purchase NOx allowances for 2010.&#160; Fuel
costs are impacted by changes in volume and price and are driven by a number of
variables including weather, reliability of coal deliveries, scheduled outages
and generation plant mix.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchased power costs
depend, in part, upon the timing and extent of planned and unplanned outages of
our generating capacity.&#160; We will
purchase power on a discretionary basis when wholesale market conditions
provide opportunities to obtain power at a cost below our internal generation
costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective January&nbsp;1,
2010, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is allowed to recover its Ohio
retail jurisdictional share of fuel and purchased power costs, of approximately
80%, as part of the fuel rider approved by the PUCO. The table below provides
the effect on annual net income as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, of a hypothetical
increase or decrease of 10% adjusted for the approximate 80% recovery in the prices of fuel and purchased
power:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Interest
Rate Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of our normal
investing and borrowing activities, our financial results are exposed to
fluctuations in interest rates, which we manage through our regular financing
activities.&#160; We maintain both cash on
deposit and investments in cash equivalents that may be affected by adverse
interest rate fluctuations.&#160; <b>DPL</b> has fixed-rate long-term debt and <b>DP&amp;L</b>
has both fixed and variable-rate long-term debt.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
variable-rate debt is comprised of publicly held pollution control bonds.&#160; The variable-rate bonds bear interest based
on a prevailing rate that is reset weekly based on a comparable market index.&#160; Market indexes can be affected by market
demand, supply, market interest rates and other economic conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
carrying value of <b>DPL&#146;s</b> debt was
$1,324.1 million at December&nbsp;31, 2009, consisting of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> first mortgage bonds, <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> tax-exempt pollution control
bonds, <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s </b>revolving credit facilities, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> unsecured notes and <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> capital lease.&#160; The fair value of this debt was $1,317.6
million, based on current market prices or discounted cash flows using current
rates for similar issues with similar terms and remaining maturities.&#160; The following table provides information
about <b>DPL&#146;s</b> debt obligations that
are sensitive to interest rate changes:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

bonds, tax-exempt pollution control bonds, revolving credit facilities and a
capital lease. &#160;The fair value of this
debt was $844.5 million, based on current market prices or discounted cash
flows using current rates for similar issues with similar terms and remaining
maturities.&#160; The following table provides
information about <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> debt
obligations that are sensitive to interest rate changes:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)&nbsp;Fixed

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Debt maturities occurring
in 2010 are discussed under FINANCIAL CONDITION, LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL
REQUIREMENTS.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Long-term Debt Interest Rate Risk Sensitivity
Analysis</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
estimate of market risk exposure is presented for our fixed-rate and
variable-rate debt at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008 for which an immediate
adverse market movement causes a potential material impact on our financial
position, results of operations, or the fair value of the debt.&#160; We believe that the adverse market movement
represents the hypothetical loss to future earnings and does not represent the
maximum possible loss nor any expected actual loss, even under adverse
conditions, because actual adverse fluctuations would likely differ.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, we did
not hold any market risk sensitive instruments which were entered into for
trading purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> debt is comprised of both fixed-rate
debt and variable-rate debt.&#160; In regard
to fixed rate debt, the interest rate risk with respect to <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
long-term debt, excluding capital lease obligations, primarily relates to the
potential impact a decrease of one percentage point in interest rates has on
the fair value of <b>DPL </b>$1,224.1
million of fixed-rate debt and not on <b>DPL&#146;s</b> financial
position or results of operations.&#160; On
the variable-rate debt, the interest rate risk with respect to <b>DPL&#146;s</b> long-term debt represents the potential impact an
increase of one percentage point in the interest rate has on <b>DPL&#146;s</b> results of operations related to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
$100 million variable-rate long-term debt outstanding as of December&nbsp;31,
2009.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#146;s interest rate risk with respect to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> long-term debt primarily relates to the potential
impact a decrease in interest rates of one percentage point has on the fair
value of <b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s $784.3 million of fixed-rate
debt and not on <b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s financial position or <b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s results of operations.&#160; On the variable-rate debt, the interest rate
risk with respect to <b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s
long-term debt represents the potential impact an increase of one percentage
point in the interest rate has on <b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s
results of operations related to <b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s $100
million variable-rate long-term debt outstanding as of December&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Equity
Price Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, approximately 35.0% of the defined benefit pension plan assets were
comprised of investments in equity securities and 65.0% related to investments
in fixed income securities, cash and cash equivalents, and alternative
investments.&#160; The equity securities are
carried at their market value of approximately $85.1&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31,
2009.&#160; A hypothetical 10% decrease in
prices quoted by stock exchanges would result in an $8.5 million reduction in
fair value as of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and approximately a $0.5 million
increase to the 2010 pension expense.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Credit
Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit risk is the risk
of an obligor&#146;s failure to meet the terms of any investment contract, loan
agreement or otherwise perform as agreed. Credit risk arises from all
activities in which success depends on issuer, borrower or counterparty
performance, whether reflected on or off the balance sheet.&#160; We limit our credit risk by assessing the
creditworthiness of potential counterparties before entering into transactions
with them and continue to evaluate their creditworthiness after transactions
have been originated.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use the three leading corporate credit
rating agencies and other current market-based qualitative and quantitative
data to assess the financial strength of counterparties on an ongoing basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;
We may require various forms of credit assurance from counterparties in order
to mitigate credit risk.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">CRITICAL
ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Consolidated Financial Statements are prepared in accordance with U.S.
GAAP.&#160; In connection with the preparation
of these financial statements, our management is required to make assumptions,
estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets,
liabilities, revenues, expenses and the related disclosure of contingent
liabilities.&#160; These assumptions, estimates
and judgments are based on our historical experience and assumptions that we
believed to be reasonable at the time.&#160;
However, because future events and their effects cannot be determined
with certainty, the determination of estimates requires the exercise of
judgment.&#160; Our critical accounting
estimates are those which require assumptions to be made about matters that are
highly uncertain.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Different estimates could
have a material effect on our financial results.&#160; Judgments and uncertainties affecting the
application of these policies and estimates may result in materially different
amounts being reported under different conditions or circumstances.&#160; Historically, however, recorded estimates
have not differed materially from actual results.&#160; Significant items subject to such judgments
include: the carrying value of property, plant and equipment; unbilled
revenues; the valuation of derivative instruments; the valuation of insurance
and claims liabilities; the valuation of allowances for receivables and deferred
income taxes; regulatory assets and liabilities; reserves recorded for income
tax exposures; litigation; contingencies; the valuation of AROs; and assets and
liabilities related to employee benefits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Impairments
and Assets Held for Sale:</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; In accordance with the
provisions of GAAP relating to the accounting for impairments, long-lived
assets to be held and used are reviewed for impairment whenever events or
circumstances indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable.&#160; When required, impairment losses on assets to
be held and used are recognized based on the fair value of the asset.&#160; We determine the fair value of these assets
based upon estimates of future cash flows, market value of similar assets, if available
or independent appraisals, if required.&#160;
In analyzing the fair value and recoverability using future cash flows,
we make projections based on a number of assumptions and estimates of growth
rates, future economic conditions, assignment of discount rates and estimates
of terminal values.&#160; An impairment loss
is recognized if the carrying amount of the long-lived asset is not recoverable
from its undiscounted cash flows.&#160; The
measurement of impairment loss is the difference between the carrying amount
and fair value of the asset.&#160; Long-lived
assets to be disposed of or held for sale are reported at the lower of carrying
amount or fair value less cost to sell.&#160;
We determine the fair value of these assets in the same manner as
described for assets held and used.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">63<a name="PB_63_003828_3020"></a></font></p>
