<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Revenue
Recognition (including Unbilled Revenue)</font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">:</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;
We consider revenue realized, or realizable, and earned when persuasive
evidence of an arrangement exists, the products or services have been provided
to the customer, the sales price is fixed or determinable, and collection is
reasonably assured.&#160; The determination of
the energy sales to customers is based on the reading of their meters, which
occurs on a systematic basis throughout the month.&#160; We recognize revenues using an accrual method
for retail and other energy sales that have not yet been billed, but where
electricity has been consumed.&nbsp; This is termed &#147;unbilled revenues&#148; and is
a widely recognized and accepted practice for utilities.&#160; At the end of each month, unbilled revenues
are determined by the estimation of unbilled energy provided to customers since
the date of the last meter reading, projected line losses, the assignment of
unbilled energy provided to customer classes and the average rate per customer
class.&#160; Given our estimation method and
the fact that customers are billed monthly, we believe it is unlikely that
materially different results will occur in future periods when these amounts
are subsequently billed.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Income
Taxes:</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Judgment and the use of estimates are
required in developing the provision for income taxes and reporting of
tax-related assets and liabilities.&#160; The
interpretation of tax laws involves uncertainty, since taxing authorities may
interpret them differently. Ultimate resolution of income tax matters may
result in favorable or unfavorable impacts to Net income and cash flows and
adjustments to tax-related assets and liabilities could be material.&#160; We have adopted the provisions of GAAP
relating to the accounting for uncertainty in income taxes.&#160; Taking into consideration the uncertainty and
judgment involved in the determination and filing of income taxes, these GAAP
provisions establish standards for recognition and measurement in financial
statements of positions taken, or expected to be taken, by an entity on its
income tax returns.&#160; Positions taken by
an entity on its income tax returns that are recognized in the financial
statements must satisfy a more-likely-than-not recognition threshold, assuming
that the position will be examined by taxing authorities with full knowledge of
all relevant information.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred income tax
assets and liabilities represent future effects on income taxes for temporary
differences between the bases of assets and liabilities for financial reporting
and tax purposes.&#160; We evaluate quarterly
the probability of realizing deferred tax assets by reviewing a forecast of
future taxable income and the availability of tax planning strategies that can
be implemented, if necessary, to realize deferred tax assets.&#160; Failure to achieve forecasted taxable income
or successfully implement tax planning strategies may affect the realization of
deferred tax assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory Assets and Liabilities:</font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Application of the provisions of GAAP
relating to regulatory accounting requires us to reflect the effect of rate
regulation in our Consolidated Financial Statements.&#160; For regulated businesses subject to federal
or state cost-of-service rate regulation, regulatory practices that assign
costs to accounting periods may differ from accounting methods generally
applied by nonregulated companies.&#160; When
it is probable that regulators will permit the recovery of current costs
through future rates charged to customers, we defer these costs as Regulatory
assets that otherwise would be expensed by nonregulated companies.&#160; Likewise, we recognize Regulatory liabilities
when it is probable that regulators will require customer refunds through
future rates and when revenue is collected from customers for expenses that are
not yet incurred.&#160; Regulatory assets are
amortized into expense and Regulatory liabilities are amortized into income
over the recovery period authorized by the regulator.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We evaluate whether or
not recovery of our Regulatory assets through future rates is probable and make
various assumptions in our analyses.&#160; The
expectations of future recovery are generally based on orders issued by
regulatory commissions or historical experience, as well as discussions with
applicable regulatory authorities.&#160; If
recovery of a regulatory asset is determined to be less than probable, it will
be written off in the period the assessment is made.&#160; We currently believe the recovery of our
Regulatory assets is probable.&#160; See Note
3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">AROs:&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with the provisions of GAAP relating to
the accounting for AROs, legal obligations associated with the retirement of
long-lived assets are required to be recognized at their fair value at the time
those obligations are incurred.&#160; Upon
initial recognition of a legal liability, costs are capitalized as part of the
related long-lived asset and allocated to expense over the useful life of the
asset.&#160; These GAAP provisions also
require that components of previously recorded depreciation related to the cost
of removal of assets upon retirement, whether legal AROs or not, must be
removed from a company&#146;s accumulated depreciation reserve.&#160; We make assumptions, estimates and judgments
that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities and expenses as they
relate to AROs.&#160; These assumptions and
estimates are based on historical experience and assumptions that we believe to
be reasonable at the time.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">64<a name="PB_64_003828_7748"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Insurance and Claims Costs</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160;
In addition to insurance obtained from third-party providers, MVIC, a
wholly-owned captive subsidiary of <b>DPL</b>, provides insurance coverage solely
to us, our subsidiaries and, in some cases, our partners in commonly-owned
facilities we operate, for workers&#146; compensation, general liability, property
damage, and directors&#146; and officers&#146; liability.&#160;
Insurance and Claims Costs on the Consolidated Balance Sheets of <b>DPL</b> include insurance reserves of approximately $16.2
million and $17.6 million for 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160; Furthermore, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is responsible for claim costs below certain coverage thresholds of MVIC for
the insurance coverage noted above.&#160; In
addition, <b>DP&amp;L</b> has medical, life and
disability reserves for claims costs below certain coverage thresholds of
third-party providers.&#160; <b>DPL </b>and<b> DP&amp;L </b>record
these additional insurance and claims costs of approximately $11.3 million and
$9.8 million for 2009 and 2008, respectively, within Other current liabilities
and Other deferred credits on the balance sheets.&#160; The MVIC reserves at <b>DPL</b>
and the workers&#146; compensation, medical, life and disability reserves at <b>DP&amp;L</b> are actuarially determined based on a reasonable
estimation of insured events occurring.&#160;
There is uncertainty associated with the loss estimates and actual
results may differ from the estimates.&#160;
Modification of these loss estimates based on experience and changed
circumstances is reflected in the period in which the estimate is re-evaluated.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Pension and Postretirement Benefits:&#160; </font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
account for and disclose pension and postretirement benefits in accordance with
the provisions of GAAP relating to the accounting for pension and other postretirement
plans.&#160; These GAAP provisions require the
use of assumptions, such as the discount rate and long-term rate of return on
assets, in determining the obligations, annual cost, and funding requirements
of the plans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For
2010, we are maintaining our long-term rate of return assumptions of 8.50% for
pension and 6.00% for other postemployment benefit plan assets representing our
long-term assumptions based on our current portfolio mix.&nbsp; We have
decreased our assumed discount rate to 5.75% for pension and 5.35% for
postretirement benefits expense to reflect current duration-based yield curve
discount rates.&nbsp; A one percent change in the rate of return assumption for
pension would result in an increase or decrease to the 2010 pension expense of
approximately $2.5 million.&#160; A one
percent change in the discount rate for pension would result in an increase or
decrease to the 2010 pension expense of approximately $2.0 million.&nbsp; We do
not anticipate any special adjustments to expense in 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In future periods,
differences in the actual return on pension and other post-employment benefit
plan assets and assumed return, or changes in the discount rate, will affect
the timing of contributions to the plans, if any.&#160; We provide postretirement health care
benefits to employees who retired prior to 1987.&#160; A one percentage point change in the assumed
health care cost trend rate would affect postretirement benefit costs by
approximately $0.1 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Contingent and Other Obligations:&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
the conduct of our business, we are subject to </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a number of federal and state laws and regulations, as
well as other factors and conditions that potentially subject us to
environmental, litigation, insurance and other risks.&#160; We periodically evaluate our exposure to such
risks and record reserves for those matters where a loss is considered probable
and reasonably estimable in accordance with GAAP.&#160; In recording such reserves, we may make
assumptions, estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of
assets, liabilities and expenses as they relate to contingent and other
obligations.&#160; These assumptions and
estimates are based on historical experience and assumptions and may be subject
to change.&#160; We, however, believe such
estimates and assumptions are reasonable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b><a name="NotesToConsolidatedFinancialState_041208"></a></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This report includes the
combined filing of <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L.&#160; DP&amp;L </b>is
the principal subsidiary of <b>DPL </b>providing
approximately 98% of <b>DPL&#146;s </b>total
consolidated revenue and approximately 95% of <b>DPL&#146;s </b>total
consolidated asset base.&#160; Throughout this
report, the terms &#147;we,&#148; &#147;us,&#148; &#147;our&#148; and &#147;ours&#148; are used to refer to both <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>,
respectively and altogether, unless the context indicates otherwise.&#160; Discussions or areas of this report that
apply only to <b>DPL</b> or <b>DP&amp;L</b>
will clearly be noted in the section.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Some of the Notes
presented in this report are only applicable to <b>DPL</b> or <b>DP&amp;L</b>
as indicated.&#160; The other Notes apply to
both registrants and the financial information presented is segregated by
registrant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Overview and Summary of Significant
Accounting Policies</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Description of Business</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">is a diversified
regional energy company organized in 1985 under the laws of Ohio.&#160; <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
principal subsidiary is <b>DP&amp;L</b>.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is a public utility incorporated in 1911 under the laws of Ohio.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is engaged in generation, transmission, distribution and the sale of
electricity to residential, commercial, industrial and governmental customers
in a 6,000 square mile area of West Central Ohio.&#160; Electricity for <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> 24 county service area is primarily generated at
eight coal-fired power plants and is distributed to more than 500,000 retail
customers.&#160; Principal industries served
include automotive, food processing, paper, plastic manufacturing and defense.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
sales reflect the general economic conditions and seasonal weather patterns of
the area.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> sells any excess energy and capacity into the
wholesale market.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> other significant subsidiaries include
DPLE, which engages in the operation of peaking generating facilities; DPLER,
which is a CRES provider selling retail electric energy and other energy
services; and MVIC, our captive insurance company that provides insurance
services to us and our subsidiaries.&#160; All
of <b>DPL&#146;s</b> subsidiaries are wholly-owned.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">also has a wholly-owned business trust,
DPL Capital Trust II, formed for the purpose of issuing trust capital
securities to investors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>
conduct their principal business in one business segment &#151; Electric.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> electric transmission and distribution
businesses are subject to rate regulation by federal and state regulators while
its generation business is not subject to such regulation.&#160; Accordingly, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
applies the accounting standards for regulated operations to its electric
transmission and distribution businesses and records regulatory assets when
incurred costs are expected to be recovered in future customer rates, and
regulatory liabilities when current cost recoveries in customer rates relate to
expected future costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial Statement Presentation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> prepare Consolidated Financial Statements
for <b>DPL</b>.&#160;
<b>DPL&#146;s</b> Consolidated Financial Statements
include the accounts of <b>DPL</b> and
its wholly-owned subsidiaries.&#160; DPL
Capital Trust II is not consolidated, consistent with the provisions of GAAP
relating to variable interest entities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> has an undivided ownership interest in
seven electric generating facilities and numerous transmission facilities.&#160; These undivided interests in jointly owned
facilities are accounted for on a pro rata basis in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All material intercompany
accounts and transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have evaluated all
subsequent events through February&nbsp;11, 2010 which is the date these
financial statements were filed with the SEC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires us to make
estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets and
liabilities, the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities, and the
revenue and expenses of the periods reported.&#160;
Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160; Significant items subject to such estimates
and judgments include: the carrying value of property, plant and equipment;
unbilled revenues; the valuation of derivative instruments; the valuation of
insurance and claims liabilities; the valuation of allowances for receivables
and deferred income taxes; regulatory assets and liabilities; reserves recorded
for income tax exposures; litigation; contingencies; the valuation of AROs; and
assets and liabilities related to employee benefits.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">77<a name="PB_77_004338_5796"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Revisions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the preparation of
our annual report on Form&nbsp;10-K for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
we identified certain immaterial items that had not been correctly presented in
our prior period balance sheets.&#160;
Accordingly, we have made the following adjustments to our prior period
balance sheets to conform to the current period presentation. These adjustments
did not have any impact on our gross margin, operating income, net income,
earnings per share or cash flows as previously reported.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property Taxes</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain accrued taxes
representing property tax liabilities had been previously classified as a
current liability and should have been classified as a noncurrent
liability.&#160; As a result of this
reclassification, accrued taxes decreased at <b>DPL</b>
by $57.5 million from $130.4 million to $72.9 million and also by the same
$57.5 million at <b>DP&amp;L</b> from $128.0 million to
$70.5 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160;
This same reclassification also increased other deferred credits at <b>DPL</b> by $57.5 million from $50.7 million to $108.2 million
and at <b>DP&amp;L</b> by $57.5 million from $50.8
million to $108.3 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred Taxes</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain deferred taxes
that related to amounts recorded in accumulated other comprehensive
income/(loss) for pension-related costs had been previously classified within
deferred taxes and should have been classified within accumulated other comprehensive
income/(loss).&#160; In addition, certain
deferred taxes that related to amounts recoverable from customers in future
rates had also been incorrectly presented.&#160;
As a result of these two deferred tax items, deferred taxes decreased at
<b>DPL</b> by $59.6 million from $433.7
million to $374.1 million and at <b>DP&amp;L</b> by
$59.5 million from $417.8 million to $358.3 million as of December&nbsp;31,
2008.&#160; These same reclassifications also
decreased accumulated other comprehensive loss at <b>DPL</b>
by $21.5 million from $44.6 million to $23.1 million and at <b>DP&amp;L</b> by $21.4 million from $37.5 million to $16.1
million and decreased regulatory assets at both <b>DPL</b>
and <b>DP&amp;L</b> by $38.1 million from $233.7
million to $195.6 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160; These reclassifications also resulted in an
increase in accumulated other comprehensive income at <b>DPL</b>
by $9.8 million from a loss of $9.2 million to income of $0.6 million and at <b>DP&amp;L</b> by $10.6 million from $6.5 million to $17.1 million
as of December&nbsp;31, 2007 and an increase in accumulated other comprehensive
income at <b>DPL</b> by $11.3 million from a loss of
$6.5 million to income of $4.8 million and at <b>DP&amp;L</b>
by $13.0 million from $15.1 million to $28.1 million as of December&nbsp;31,
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue
Recognition</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues are recognized
from retail and wholesale electricity sales and electricity transmission and
distribution delivery services.&#160; We
consider revenue realized, or realizable, and earned when persuasive evidence
of an arrangement exists, the products or services have been provided to the
customer, the sales price is fixed or determinable, and collection is
reasonably assured.&#160; The determination of
energy sales to customers is based on the reading of their meters and this
occurs on a systematic basis throughout the month.&#160; We recognize the revenues on our statements
of results of operations using an accrual method for retail and other energy
sales that have not yet been billed, but where electricity has been
consumed.&nbsp; This is termed &#147;unbilled revenues&#148; and is a widely recognized
and accepted practice for utilities.&#160; At
the end of each month, unbilled revenues are determined by the estimation of
unbilled energy provided to customers since the date of the last meter reading,
projected line losses, the assignment of unbilled energy provided to customer
classes and the average rate per customer class.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of the power produced
at the generation plants is sold to an RTO and we in turn purchase it back from
the RTO to supply our customers.&#160; These
power sales and purchases are reported on a net hourly basis as revenues or
purchased power on our statements of results of operations.&#160; We record expenses when purchased electricity
is received and when expenses are incurred, with the exception of the
ineffective portion of certain power purchase contracts that are derivatives
and qualify for hedge accounting, as well as certain derivative contracts that
do not qualify for hedge accounting, causing gains or losses to be recorded
prior to the receipt of electricity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Allowance for Uncollectible Accounts</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We establish provisions
for uncollectible accounts by using both historical average loss percentages to
project future losses and by establishing specific provisions for known credit
issues.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">78<a name="PB_78_004338_2897"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Property, Plant and Equipment</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We record our
ownership share of our undivided interest in jointly-held plants as an asset in
property, plant and equipment.&#160; Property,
plant and equipment are stated at cost.&#160;
For regulated transmission and distribution property, cost includes
direct labor and material, allocable overhead expenses and an allowance for
funds used during construction (AFUDC).&#160;
AFUDC represents the cost of borrowed funds and equity used to finance
regulated construction projects.&#160;
Capitalization of AFUDC ceases at either project completion or at the
date specified by regulators.&#160; AFUDC
capitalized in 2009, 2008 and 2007 was not material.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For unregulated
generation property, cost includes direct labor and material, allocable
overhead expenses and interest capitalized during construction using the
provisions of GAAP relating to the accounting for capitalized interest.&#160; Capitalized interest was $2.4 million in
2009, $8.9 million in 2008 and $21.8 million in 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For substantially all
depreciable property, when a unit of property is retired, the original cost of
that property less any salvage value is charged to Accumulated depreciation and
amortization.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property is evaluated for
impairment when events or changes in circumstances indicate that its carrying
amount may not be recoverable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Repairs
and Maintenance</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Costs associated with
maintenance activities, primarily power plant outages, are recognized at the
time the work is performed.&#160; These costs,
which include labor, materials and supplies, and outside services required to
maintain equipment and facilities, are capitalized or expensed based on
FERC-defined units of property.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation expense is
calculated using the straight-line method, which allocates the cost of property
over its estimated useful life.&#160; For <b>DPL&#146;s</b> generation, transmission, and
distribution assets, straight-line depreciation is applied on an average annual
composite basis using group rates that approximated 2.7% in 2009, 2.7% in 2008
and 2.9% in 2007.&#160; In July&nbsp;2007, <b>DPL</b> completed a depreciation rate study for non-regulated
generation property based on its property, plant and equipment balances during
2007.&#160; The results of the depreciation
study concluded that <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
depreciation rates should be reduced due to projected asset lives beyond
previously estimated useful lives.&#160; <b>DPL</b> adjusted the depreciation rates for its non-regulated
generation property, effective August&nbsp;1, 2007.&#160; For the period from August&nbsp;1, 2007 to December&nbsp;31,
2007, the reduction in depreciation expense increased income from continuing
operations by approximately $9.5 million, increased net income by approximately
$6.0 million, and increased basic EPS by approximately $0.06 per share.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is a
summary of <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Property, plant
and equipment with corresponding composite depreciation rates at December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008:</font></p>

composite basis using group rates that approximated 2.7% in 2009, 2.6% in 2008
and 2.8% in 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">AROs</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We recognize AROs in
accordance with GAAP.&#160; GAAP requires
legal obligations associated with the retirement of long-lived assets to be
recognized at their fair value at the time those obligations are incurred.&#160; Upon initial recognition of a legal
liability, costs are capitalized as part of the related long-lived asset and
depreciated over the useful life of the related asset.&#160; Our legal obligations associated with the
retirement of our long-lived assets consisted primarily of river intake and
discharge structures, coal unloading facilities, loading docks, ice breakers
and ash disposal facilities.&#160; Our
generation AROs are recorded within other deferred credits on the balance
sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimating the amount and
timing of future expenditures of this type requires significant judgment.&#160; Management routinely updates these estimates
as additional information becomes available.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in the Liability for
Generation AROs</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Asset
Removal Costs</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We continue to record
cost of removal for our regulated transmission and distribution assets through
our depreciation rates and recover those amounts in rates charged to our
customers.&#160; There are no known legal AROs
associated with these assets.&#160; We have
recorded $99.1 million and $96.0&nbsp;million in estimated costs of removal at December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, respectively, as regulatory liabilities for our transmission and
distribution property.&#160; These amounts
represent the excess of the cumulative removal costs recorded through
depreciation rates versus the cumulative removal costs actually incurred.&#160; See Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory
Accounting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with GAAP,
regulatory assets and liabilities are recorded in the balance sheets for our
regulated transmission and distribution businesses.&#160; Regulatory assets are the deferral of costs
expected to be recovered in future customer rates and Regulatory liabilities
represent current recovery of expected future costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We evaluate our
Regulatory assets each period and believe recovery of these assets is
probable.&#160; We have received or requested
a return on certain regulatory assets for which we are currently recovering or
seeking recovery through rates.&#160; We
record a return after it has been authorized in an order by a regulator.&#160; If we were required to terminate application
of these GAAP provisions for all of our regulated operations, we would have to
write off the amounts of all regulatory assets and liabilities to the
statements of results of operations at that time.&#160; See Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Inventories</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inventories are carried
at average cost and include coal, limestone, oil and gas used for electric
generation, and materials and supplies used for utility operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We account for our
emission allowances as inventory and record emission allowance inventory at
weighted average cost.&nbsp; We calculate the weighted average cost by each
vintage (year) for which emission allowances can be used and charge to fuel
costs the weighted average cost of emission allowances used each month.&#160; Net gains or losses on the sale of excess
emission allowances, representing the difference between the sales proceeds and
the weighted average cost of emission allowances, are recorded as a component
of our fuel costs and are reflected in Operating income when realized.&#160; During the periods ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, 2008 and 2007, we recognized gains from the sale of emission allowances
in the amounts of $5.0 million, $34.8 million and $1.2 million,
respectively.&#160; Beginning in January&nbsp;2010,
most of the gains on emission allowances will be used to reduce the overall
fuel rider charged to the Ohio retail jurisdiction.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,
2009, we had substantially placed into service FGD equipment at most of our <b>DP&amp;L </b>and partner-operated facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GAAP requires an asset
and liability approach for financial accounting and reporting of income taxes
with tax effects of differences, based on currently enacted income tax rates,
between the financial reporting and tax basis of accounting reported as
deferred tax assets or liabilities in the balance sheets.&#160; Deferred tax assets are recognized for
deductible temporary differences.&#160;
Valuation allowances are provided against deferred tax assets unless it
is more likely than not that the asset will be realized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investment tax credits,
which have been used to reduce federal income taxes payable, have been deferred
for financial reporting purposes.&#160; These
deferred investment tax credits are amortized over the useful lives of the
property to which they are related.&#160; For
rate-regulated operations, additional deferred income taxes and offsetting
regulatory assets or liabilities are recorded to recognize that income taxes
will be recoverable or refundable through future revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> files a consolidated U.S. federal income
tax return in conjunction with its subsidiaries.&#160; The consolidated tax liability is allocated
to each subsidiary based on the separate return method which is specified in
our tax allocation agreement and which provides a consistent, systematic and
rational approach.&#160; See Note 8 of Notes
to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stock-Based Compensation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We measure the cost of
employee services received and paid with equity instruments based on the
fair-value of such equity on the grant date.&#160;
This cost is recognized in results of operations over the period that
employees are required to provide service.&#160;
Liability awards are initially recorded based on the fair-value of
equity instruments and are to be re-measured for the change in stock price at
each subsequent reporting date until the liability is ultimately settled.&#160; The fair-value for employee share options and
other similar instruments at the grant date are estimated using option-pricing
models and any excess tax benefits are recognized as an addition to paid-in
capital.&#160; The reduction in income taxes
payable from the excess tax benefits is presented in the statements of cash
flows within Cash flows from financing activities.&#160; See Note 12 of Notes to Consolidated
Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Cash and cash equivalents are stated at cost, which
approximates fair value.&#160; All highly
liquid short-term investments with original maturities of three months or less
are considered cash equivalents.</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial
Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We classify our
investments in debt and equity financial instruments of publicly traded
entities into different categories: held-to-maturity and available-for-sale.&#160; Available-for-sale securities are carried at
fair value and unrealized gains and losses on those securities, net of deferred
income taxes, are presented as a separate component of shareholders&#146;
equity.&#160; Other-than-temporary declines in
value are recognized currently in earnings.&#160;
Financial instruments classified as held-to-maturity are carried at
amortized cost.&#160; The cost basis for
public equity security and fixed maturity investments is average cost and
amortized cost, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">Financial Derivatives</font></i></b></h3>

<h3 style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></h3>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All
derivatives are recognized as either assets or liabilities in the balance
sheets and are measured at fair value.&#160;
Changes in the fair value are recorded in earnings unless they are
designated as a cash flow hedge of a forecasted transaction or qualify for the
normal purchases and sales exception.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We use forward contracts
and options to reduce our exposure to changes in energy and commodity prices
and as a hedge against the risk of changes in cash flows associated with
expected electricity purchases.&#160; These
purchases are required to meet full load requirements during times of peak
demand or during planned and unplanned generation facility outages.&#160; We also hold forward sales contracts that
hedge against the risk of changes in cash flows associated with power sales
during periods of projected generation facility availability.&#160; We use cash flow hedge accounting when the
hedge is deemed to be effective and MTM accounting when the hedge is not
effective.&#160; See Note 11 of Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">Insurance and Claims Costs</font></i></b></h3>

<h3 style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></h3>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to insurance
obtained from third-party providers, MVIC, a wholly-owned captive subsidiary of
<b>DPL</b>, provides insurance coverage
to us, our subsidiaries and, in some cases, our partners in commonly owned
facilities we operate, for workers&#146; compensation, general liability, property
damage, and directors&#146; and officers&#146; liability.&#160;
Insurance and claims costs on the Consolidated Balance Sheets of <b>DPL</b> include insurance reserves of approximately $16.2 million
and $17.6 million for 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160; Furthermore, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is responsible for claim costs below certain coverage thresholds of MVIC for
the insurance coverage noted above.&#160; In
addition, <b>DP&amp;L</b> has medical, life, and
disability reserves for claims costs below certain coverage thresholds of
third-party providers.&#160; <b>DPL </b>and<b> DP&amp;L </b>record
these additional insurance and claims costs of approximately $11.3 million and
$9.8 million for 2009 and 2008, respectively, within Other current liabilities
and Other deferred credits on the balance sheets.&#160; The MVIC reserves at <b>DPL</b>
and the workers&#146; compensation, medical, life, and disability reserves at <b>DP&amp;L</b> are actuarially determined based on a reasonable
estimation of insured events occurring.&#160;
There is uncertainty associated with these loss estimates and actual
results may differ from the estimates.&#160; Modification
of these loss estimates based on experience and changed circumstances is
reflected in the period in which the estimate is re-evaluated.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL
Capital Trust II</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> has a wholly-owned business trust, DPL
Capital Trust II (the Trust), formed for the purpose of issuing trust capital
securities to third-party investors.&#160;
Effective 2003, <b>DPL</b>
deconsolidated the Trust upon adoption of the accounting standards related to
variable interest entities and currently treats the Trust as a nonconsolidated
subsidiary.&#160; The Trust, which holds
mandatorily redeemable trust capital securities, is reported as two components
on <b>DPL&#146;s</b> consolidated balance sheet.&#160; The investment in the Trust, which amounts to
$3.8 million and $5.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, respectively,
is included in Other deferred assets within Other noncurrent assets.&#160; <b>DPL</b> also has a
note payable to the Trust amounting to $142.6 million and $195.0 million at December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, respectively, that was established upon the Trust&#146;s
deconsolidation in 2003.&#160; See Note 7 of
Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the
obligations under the note payable mentioned above, <b>DPL</b>
also agreed to a security obligation which represents a full and unconditional
guarantee of payments to the capital security holders of the Trust.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Pension and Postretirement Benefits</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We recognize the
funded status of our benefit plan; recognize as a component of other
comprehensive income (OCI), net of tax, the gains or losses and prior service
costs or credits that arise during the period but are not recognized as
components of net periodic benefit cost; measure defined benefit plan assets
and obligations as of the date of our fiscal year-end; and disclose in Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements additional information about certain effects
on net periodic benefit costs for the next fiscal year that arise from delayed
recognition of the gains or losses, prior service costs or credits, and
transition assets or obligations. </font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;See Note 9 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)</font></i><i><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-style:italic;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L </font></i></b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">sells power to DPLER to satisfy
the electric requirements of its retail customers.&#160; The revenues associated with sales to DPLER
are recorded as wholesale sales in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Financial Statements.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(b)</font></i><i><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-style:italic;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">MVIC, a wholly-owned captive
insurance subsidiary of <b>DPL,</b> provides
insurance coverage to <b>DP&amp;L</b> and
other <b>DPL </b>subsidiaries for workers&#146;
compensation, general liability, property damages and directors&#146; and officers&#146;
liability.&#160; These amounts represent
insurance premiums paid by <b>DP&amp;L</b> to
MVIC.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Recently
Adopted Accounting Standards</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FASB
Codification</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We adopted FASC 105, &#147;Generally
Accepted Accounting Principles&#148; (formerly SFAS No.&nbsp;168, &#147;The FASB
Accounting Standards Codification and the Hierarchy of Generally Accepted
Accounting Principles </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#151;
a replacement of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;162&#148;),
on September&nbsp;30, 2009.&#160; The
objective of this Statement is to replace Statement No.&nbsp;162 and to
establish the FASC as the source of authoritative accounting principles
recognized by the FASB to be applied by nongovernmental entities in the
preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP.&#160; Rules&nbsp;and interpretive releases of the
SEC under authority of federal securities laws are also sources of
authoritative GAAP for SEC registrants.&#160;
This update did not have a material impact on our overall results of
operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Disclosures about Derivative
Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We adopted an update to
FASC 815, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#148; (formerly SFAS No.&nbsp;161, &#147;Disclosures
about Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities &#151; an amendment to FASB
Statement No.&nbsp;133&#148;), on January&nbsp;1, 2009.&#160; This update requires an entity to provide
enhanced disclosures about: (a)&nbsp;how and why an entity uses derivative
instruments; (b)&nbsp;how derivative instruments and related hedged items are
accounted for under FASC 815 and its related interpretations; and (c)&nbsp;how
derivative instruments and related hedged items affect an entity&#146;s financial
position, financial performance and cash flows.&#160;
This update did not have a material impact on our overall results of
operations, financial position or cash flows.&#160;
See Note 11 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Participating
Securities and EPS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
adopted an update to FASC 260, &#147;Earnings per Share&#148; (formerly Staff Position
EITF 03-6-1, &#147;Determining Whether Instruments Granted in Share-Based Payment
Transactions Are Participating Securities&#148;) on January&nbsp;1, 2009.&#160; This update clarifies that unvested
share-based awards that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends or dividend
equivalents (whether paid or unpaid) are participating securities and must be
included in the computation of EPS pursuant to the two-class method.&#160; This update did not have a material impact on
our overall results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Meaning
of &#147;Indexed to a Company&#146;s Own Stock&#148;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
adopted an update to FASC 815, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#148; (formerly EITF Issue No.&nbsp;07-5,
&#147;Determining Whether an Instrument (or Embedded Feature) is Indexed to an
Entity&#146;s Own Stock&#148;), on January&nbsp;1, 2009.&#160;
This update gives guidance on when a financial instrument is considered
to be indexed to a company&#146;s own stock to meet the criteria for FASC
815-10-15-74(a)&nbsp;(formerly paragraph 11(a)&nbsp;of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;133,
&#147;Accounting for Derivative Financial Instruments.&#148;)&#160; This update did not have a material impact on
our overall results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Interim
Disclosures about Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
adopted an update of FASC 825, &#147;Financial Instruments&#148; (formerly Staff Position
SFAS 107-1 and APB 28-1, &#147;Interim Disclosures about Fair Value of Financial
Instruments&#148;), on June&nbsp;30, 2009.&#160;
This update requires disclosure about the fair value of financial
instruments for interim reporting periods of publicly traded companies as well
as in annual financial statements.&#160; This
update did not have a material impact on our overall results of operations,
financial position or cash flows.&#160; See
Note 10 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Subsequent
Events</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We adopted FASC 855, &#147;Subsequent
Events&#148; (formerly SFAS 165), on June&nbsp;30, 2009.&#160; FASC 855 incorporates the guidance in the
American Institute of Certified Public Accountants&#146; Auditing Standard 560 &#151;
Subsequent Events, into the accounting guidance.&#160; This new standard does not change current
accounting practices.&#160; FASC 855 did not have a material impact on
our overall results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Disclosures
about Pensions and Other Postretirement Benefits</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
adopted an update to FASC 715, &#147;Compensation &#151; Retirement Plans&#148; (formerly
Staff Position SFAS 132(R)-1, &#147;Employers&#146; Disclosures about Postretirement
Benefit Plan Assets&#148;), on December&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; This update requires disclosures about
benefit plan assets similar to the disclosure required in FASC 820, &#147;Fair Value
Measurements and Disclosures.&#148;&#160; It also
requires discussions on investment allocation decisions, major categories of
plan assets and significant concentrations of risk in plan assets for the
period.&#160; This update did not have a
material impact on our overall results of operations, financial position or
cash flows.&#160; See Note 9 of Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Redeemable
Equity Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
adopted ASU 2009-04, &#147;Accounting for Redeemable Equity Instruments, an
amendment to Section&nbsp;480-10-S99,&#148; (ASU 2009-04) on October&nbsp;1,
2009.&#160; ASU 2009-04 clarifies that SEC
Accounting Series&nbsp;Release 268 pertains to preferred stocks and other
redeemable securities including common stock, derivative instruments,
non-controlling interest, securities held by an ESOP and share-based payment
arrangements with employees.&#160; This update
did not have a material impact on our overall results of operations, financial
position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Measuring
Liabilities at Fair Value</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
adopted ASU 2009-05, &#147;Measuring Liabilities at Fair Value,&#148; (ASU 2009-05) on October&nbsp;1,
2009.&#160; ASU 2009-05 provides additional
guidance clarifying the measurement of liabilities at fair value.&#160; This update did not have a material impact on
our overall results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Investments in Certain Entities
that Calculate Net Asset Value per Share</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We adopted ASU 2009-12, &#147;Fair
Value Measurements and Disclosures,&#148; (ASU 2009-12) on December&nbsp;31,
2009.&#160; ASU 2009-12 updates FASC 820-10, &#147;Fair
Value Measurements and Disclosures &#151; Overall&#148; and allows, as a practical
expedient, a reporting entity to measure the fair value of an investment that
is within the scope of these amendments on the basis of the net asset value per
share of the investment if the net asset value of the investment is calculated
in a manner consistent with the measurement principles of FASC 946, &#147;Financial
Services &#151; Investment Companies.&#148;&#160; This update did not have a material impact
on our overall results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Recently
Issued Accounting Standards</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Variable
Interest Entities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2009, the
FASB issued ASU 2009-02 &#147;Omnibus Update&#148; (formerly SFAS No.&nbsp;167, a
revision to FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;46(R), &#147;<em style="letter-spacing:0pt;"><i>Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities,&#148;) </i></em><em style="letter-spacing:0pt;"><i style="font-style:normal;">(ASU 2009-02) that is effective for </i></em>annual reporting
periods beginning after November&nbsp;15, 2009.&#160;
We expect to adopt this ASU in the first quarter of 2010.&#160; This standard updates FASC 810, &#147;Consolidation.&#148;&#160; ASU 2009-02 changes how a company determines
when an entity that is insufficiently capitalized or is not controlled through
voting (or similar rights) should be consolidated.&#160; The determination of whether a company is
required to consolidate an entity is based on, among other things, an entity&#146;s
purpose and design and a company&#146;s ability to direct the activities of the
entity that most significantly impact the entity&#146;s economic performance.&#160; We do not expect these new rules&nbsp;to have
a material impact on our overall results of operations, financial position or
cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fair
Value Disclosures</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
January&nbsp;2010, the FASB issued ASU 2010-06 &#147;Fair Value Measurements and
Disclosures&#148; (ASU 2010-06) effective for annual reporting periods beginning
after December&nbsp;15, 2009.&#160; We expect
to adopt this ASU on January&nbsp;1, 2010.&#160;
This standard updates FASC 820, &#147;Fair Value Measurements.&#148;&#160; ASU 2010-06 requires additional disclosures
about fair value measurements including transfers in and out of Levels 1 and 2
and a higher level of disaggregation for the different types of financial
instruments.&#160; For the reconciliation of
Level 3 fair value measurements, information about purchases, sales, issuances
and settlements should be presented separately.&#160;
We do not expect these new rules&nbsp;to have a material impact on our
overall results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">3.&#160; Regulatory Matters</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with GAAP,
regulatory assets and liabilities are recorded in the balance sheets for our
regulated electric transmission and distribution businesses.&#160; Regulatory assets are the deferral of costs
expected to be recovered in future customer rates and regulatory liabilities
represent current recovery of expected future costs or gains probable of
recovery in future rates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We evaluate our
regulatory assets each period and believe recovery of these assets is
probable.&#160; We have received or requested
a return on certain regulatory assets for which we are currently recovering or
seeking recovery through rates.&#160; We
record a return after it has been authorized in an order by a regulator.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory assets and
liabilities on the balance sheets include:</font></p>
