<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)</font></i><i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-style:italic;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></i><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">F &#150; Recovery of incurred costs
plus rate of return.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">C &#150; Recovery of incurred costs
only.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">B &#150; Balance has an offsetting
liability resulting in no impact on rate base.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">D &#150; Recovery not yet determined,
but is probable of occurring in future rate proceedings.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred recoverable
income taxes</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
represent deferred income tax assets recognized from the normalization of
flow-through items as the result of amounts previously provided to
customers.&#160; This is the cumulative
flow-through benefit given to regulated customers that will be collected from
them in future years.&#160; Since currently
existing temporary differences between the financial statements and the related
tax basis of assets will reverse in subsequent periods, these deferred
recoverable income taxes are amortized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pension benefits</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent the qualifying FASC 715, &#147;Compensation
&#151; Retirement Benefits&#148; costs of our regulated operations that for ratemaking
purposes are deferred for future recovery.&#160;
We recognize an asset for a plan&#146;s overfunded status or a liability for
a plan&#146;s underfunded status, and recognize, as a component of other comprehensive
income (OCI), the changes in the funded status of the plan that arise during
the year that are not recognized as a component of net periodic benefit cost.&#160; This regulatory asset represents the
regulated portion that would otherwise be charged as a loss to OCI.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unamortized loss on
reacquired debt</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
represents losses on long-term debt reacquired or redeemed in prior
periods.&#160; These costs are being amortized
over the life of the original issues in accordance with FERC rules.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Electric Choice systems
costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent costs
incurred to modify the customer billing system for unbundled customer rates and
electric choice utility bills relative to other generation suppliers and
information reports provided to the state administrator of the low-income
payment program.&#160; In March&nbsp;2006, the
PUCO issued an order that approved our tariff as filed.&#160; We began collecting this rider immediately
and expect to recover all costs over five years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regional transmission
organization costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
represent costs incurred to join a RTO.&#160;
The recovery of these costs will be requested in a future FERC rate
case.&#160; In accordance with FERC
precedence, we are amortizing these costs over a 10-year period beginning in
2004 when we joined the PJM RTO.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">TCRR, transmission,
ancillary and other PJM-related costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent the costs related to transmission,
ancillary service and other PJM-related charges that have been incurred as a
member of PJM.&#160; We review retail rates
and are able to make true-up adjustments on an annual basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;19,
2009, the PUCO approved <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
request to defer transmission, capacity, ancillary and other costs incurred
since July&nbsp;31, 2008 consistent with the provisions of SB 221.&#160; In May&nbsp;2009, the PUCO granted <b>DP&amp;L</b> authority to recover these costs through retail
rates beginning June&nbsp;1, 2009.&#160;
Subsequently, an application for rehearing was filed claiming the PUCO&#146;s
order allowing for recovery of RPM capacity costs through a TCRR was
unlawful.&#160; The PUCO issued an order
granting rehearing and, on September&nbsp;9, 2009, issued an order directing <b>DP&amp;L</b> to remove the deferred and current RPM capacity
costs from the TCRR rider but also indicating that these RPM capacity costs may
be recoverable under a separate rider.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> made a compliance filing on September&nbsp;23,
2009, where it removed such costs from the TCRR rider and proposed a new RTO
RPM rider for the recovery of such costs.&#160;
The PUCO approved the two separate riders in November&nbsp;2009.&#160; The sum of the rate collected through the
current TCRR rider and the new RTO RPM rider equals the rate collected through
the original TCRR rider.&#160; Accordingly,
during the period ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
deferred total net RTO costs in the amount of $23.5 million.&#160; In addition, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
also deferred $1.1 million relating to Regional Transmission Expansion Plan
(RTEP) costs and $0.9 million relating to interest and operation and
maintenance expenses.&#160; Of the total
deferred costs amounting to $25.5 million, $9.8 million relates to the period August&nbsp;1,
2008 through December&nbsp;31, 2008, and $15.7 million relates to the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; The
deferral of these costs resulted in a favorable impact to our results of
operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RPM capacity costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent the PJM-related costs from the
calculations of the PJM Reliability Pricing Model that allocates capacity among
the users of the PJM System.&#160; As
discussed above, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is recovering these costs
through a PUCO-approved RTO RPM rider.&#160;
The sum of the rate collected through the current TCRR rider and the new
RTO RPM rider equals the rate collected through the original TCRR rider.&#160; We review this rate and are able to make
true-up adjustments to it on an annual basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred storm costs -
2008</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> relate to
costs incurred to repair the damage caused by hurricane force winds in September&nbsp;2008,
as well as other major 2008 storms.&#160; On January&nbsp;14,
2009, the PUCO granted <b>DP&amp;L</b> the
authority to defer these costs with a return until such time that <b>DP&amp;L</b> seeks recovery in a future rate proceeding.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Power plant emission fees</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent costs paid to the State of
Ohio since 2002 for environmental monitoring.&#160;
An application is pending before the PUCO to amend an approved rate
rider that had been in effect to collect fees that were paid and deferred in
years prior to 2002.&#160; The deferred costs
incurred prior to 2002 have been fully recovered.&#160; As the previously approved rate rider
continues to be in effect, we believe these costs are probable of future rate
recovery.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CCEM smart grid and
advanced metering infrastructure costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent costs incurred as a result of studying and
developing distribution system upgrades and implementation of advanced metering
infrastructure.&#160; Consistent with the
Stipulation, <b>DP&amp;L</b> re-filed its smart grid
and advanced metering infrastructure business cases with the PUCO on August&nbsp;4,
2009 seeking recovery of costs associated with a 10-year plan to deploy smart
meters, distribution and substation automation, core telecommunications,
supporting software and in-home technologies.&nbsp; On August&nbsp;5, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> submitted an application for American Recovery and
Reinvestment Act (ARRA) funding under the Integrated and/or Crosscutting
Systems topic area for the Smart Grid Investment Grant Program.&#160; On October&nbsp;27, 2009, we were notified by
the United States Department of Energy (DOE) that we will not receive funding
under the ARRA.&#160; A technical conference
in this case was held at the PUCO in October&nbsp;2009 for the smart grid case,
and a subsequent PUCO entry established a comment and reply comment
period.&#160; A hearing is not yet scheduled
for this case.&#160; Based on past PUCO precedent
and the Ohio legislature&#146;s intent behind SB221, we believe these costs are
probable of future recovery in rates.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">88<a name="PB_88_005322_3641"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CCEM energy efficiency
program costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
represent costs incurred to develop and implement various new customer programs
addressing energy efficiency.&#160; A portion
of these costs is being recovered over three years as part of the Stipulation
beginning July&nbsp;1, 2009; the remaining costs are subject to a two-year
true-up process for any over/under recovery of costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> primarily include consumer education
advertising costs regarding electric deregulation, settlement system costs,
other PJM and rate case costs, and alternative energy costs that are or will be
recovered over various periods.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory Liabilities</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated costs of
removal &#151; regulated property</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> reflect an estimate of amounts collected in customer
rates that are expected to be incurred to remove existing transmission and
distribution property from service upon retirement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SECA net revenue subject to refund</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represents our deferral of amounts
collected in customer rates during 2005 and 2006.&#160; SECA revenue and expenses represent FERC-ordered
transitional payments for the use of transmission lines within PJM.&#160; A hearing was held in early 2006 to determine
if these transitional payments are subject to refund, however, no ruling has
been issued.&#160; We began receiving and
paying these transitional payments in May&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Postretirement benefits</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> represent the qualifying FASC 715, &#147;Compensation &#151;
Retirement Benefits&#148; gains related to our regulated operations that, for
ratemaking purposes, are probable of being reflected in future rates.&#160; We recognize an asset for a plan&#146;s overfunded
status or a liability for a plan&#146;s underfunded status, and recognize, as a
component of OCI, the changes in the funded status of the plan that arise
during the year that are not recognized as a component of net periodic benefit
cost.&#160; This regulatory liability
represents the regulated portion that would otherwise be reflected as a gain to
OCI.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other costs</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> primarily include derivative activity related to fuel
costs that will be settled over various periods.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">4.&#160; Ownership
of Coal-fired Facilities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and other Ohio utilities have undivided
ownership interests in seven coal-fired electric generating facilities and
numerous transmission facilities.&#160;
Certain expenses, primarily fuel costs for the generating units, are
allocated to the owners based on their energy usage.&#160; The remaining expenses, investments in fuel
inventory, plant materials and operating supplies, and capital additions are
allocated to the owners in accordance with their respective ownership
interests.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009,
we had $42 million of
construction work in process at such facilities.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
share of the operating cost of such facilities is included within the
corresponding line in the Statements of Results of Operations and <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> share of the investment in the
facilities is included in the Balance Sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> undivided ownership interest in such
facilities as well as our wholly-owned coal fired Hutchings plant at December&nbsp;31,
2009, is as follows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">5.&#160; Assets Sales</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Peaker
Sales</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2006, in
connection with DPLE&#146;s (a wholly-owned subsidiary of <b>DPL</b>)
decision to sell the Greenville Station and Darby Station electric peaking
generation facilities, <b>DPL</b> concluded
that the related assets were impaired.&nbsp; Greenville Station consisted of
four natural gas peaking units with a net book value of approximately $66
million. Darby Station consisted of six natural gas peaking units with a net
book value of approximately $156 million.&#160;
During the fourth quarter of 2006, <b>DPL</b> recorded a
$71.0 million impairment charge to write-down the assets to their fair
value.&#160; The Greenville Station and Darby
Station assets were sold by DPLE in April&nbsp;2007 for $49.2 million and
$102.0 million, respectively, in two separate transactions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Aircraft Sale</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
June&nbsp;7, 2007, Miami Valley CTC,&nbsp;Inc. (an indirect, wholly-owned
subsidiary of <b>DPL</b>), sold its
corporate aircraft and associated inventory and parts for $7.4 million.&#160; The net book value of the assets sold was
approximately $1.0 million, and severance and other costs of approximately $0.4
million were accrued.&#160; Miami Valley CTC,&nbsp;Inc.
recorded a net gain on the sale of approximately $6.0 million during the second
quarter ending June&nbsp;30, 2007, which was included in <b>DPL&#146;s </b>Operation and maintenance expense.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">6.&#160;
Discontinued Operations</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;13,
2005, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> subsidiaries, MVE,&nbsp;Inc.
(MVE) and MVIC, entered into an agreement to sell their respective interests in
forty-six private equity funds to AlpInvest/Lexington 2005, LLC, a joint
venture of AlpInvest Partners and Lexington Partners,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; During 2005, MVE and MVIC completed the sale
of their interests in forty-three funds and a portion of another of those
private equity funds.&#160; During 2005, MVE
entered into alternative closing arrangements with AlpInvest/Lexington 2005,
LLC for funds where legal title to said funds could not be transferred until a
later time.&#160; Pursuant to these
arrangements, MVE transferred the economic aspects of the remaining private
equity funds, consisting of two funds and a portion of one fund, to
AlpInvest/Lexington 2005, LLC without a change in ownership of the
interests.&#160; The ownership interest in
these funds was transferred in 2006 and 2007, at which time <b>DPL</b> recognized previously deferred gains.&#160; <b>DPL</b> recognized
$18.9 million ($12.1 million after tax) of these previously deferred gains in
2006 and the remaining balance of these gains in the amount of $7.9 million,
net of associated expenses ($4.9 million after tax), were recognized in
2007.&#160; This transaction was recorded in
discontinued operations for each period presented.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the May&nbsp;21,
2007 settlement of the litigation with three former executives (see Note 17 of
Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements), the three former executives
relinquished all of their rights to certain deferred compensation, restricted
stock units, MVE incentives, stock options and reimbursement of legal
fees.&#160; The reversal of accruals related
to the performance of the financial asset portfolio was recorded in
discontinued operations.&#160; Additionally, a
portion of the $25 million settlement expense was allocated to discontinued
operations.&#160; These transactions resulted
in a net gain of $8.1 million, net of associated expenses ($5.1 million after
tax), on the settlement of litigation being recorded in discontinued operations
in 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were no
discontinued operations recorded in 2009 or 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Debt and Debt Covenants</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;21,
2009, <b>DPL</b> purchased $52.4 million principal
amount of DPL Capital Trust II 8.125% capital securities in a privately
negotiated transaction.&#160; As part of this
transaction, <b>DPL</b> paid a $3.7 million, or 7%,
premium which was recognized as an expense in the fourth quarter of 2009 and
recorded within interest expense on the Consolidated Statements of Results of
Operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;21, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> entered into a $100 million unsecured revolving
credit agreement with a syndicated bank group.&#160;
The agreement is for a 364-day term expiring on April&nbsp;20,
2010.&#160; The facility contains one
financial covenant: <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
total debt to total capitalization ratio is not to exceed 0.65 to 1.00.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, this covenant
is met with a ratio of 0.40 to 1.00.&#160; As
of December&nbsp;31, 2009, there were no borrowings outstanding under this
facility.&#160; Fees associated with this
credit facility were approximately $0.7 million in 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL</b>
paid $175 million of the 8.00% Senior notes when the notes became due.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;4, 2008,
the OAQDA issued $100 million of collateralized, variable rate Revenue Refunding
Bonds Series&nbsp;A and B due November&nbsp;1, 2040.&#160; In turn, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
borrowed these funds from the OAQDA.&#160; The
payment of principal and interest on the bonds when due is backed by a standby
letter of credit (LOC) issued by a syndicated bank group.&#160; This LOC facility, which was for an initial
two-year period expiring in December&nbsp;2010, is irrevocable, has no
subjective acceleration clauses and also contains a provision that all
outstanding amounts drawn on the facility are due upon the LOC&#146;s expiration
date.&#160; Since this LOC facility will
expire in December&nbsp;2010, at which point the bondholders could call the
bonds, we have reflected these outstanding bonds as a current liability.&#160; Management will continue to monitor and
evaluate market conditions over the next several months and make a
determination to either seek a renewal of this standby letter of credit or to
explore alternative financing arrangements.&#160;
<b>DP&amp;L</b> used $10 million of the
proceeds from this bond issuance to finance its portion of the costs for
acquiring, constructing and installing certain solid waste disposal and air
quality facilities at the Conesville generation station.&#160; The remaining $90 million was used to redeem
the 2007 Series&nbsp;A Bonds as discussed in the next paragraph.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;15,
2007, the OAQDA issued $90 million of collateralized, variable rate OAQDA
Revenue Bonds, 2007 Series&nbsp;A due November&nbsp;1, 2040.&#160; In turn, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
borrowed these funds from the OAQDA.&#160; The
payment of principal and interest on the bonds when due was insured by an
insurance policy issued by Financial Guaranty Insurance Company (FGIC).&#160; During the first quarter of 2008, all three
credit rating agencies downgraded FGIC.&#160;
These downgrades, as well as the downgrades of our major bond insurers,
resulted in auction rate security bonds carrying substantially higher interest
rates in succeeding auctions and incurring failed auctions.&#160; On April&nbsp;4, 2008, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
converted the 2007 Series&nbsp;A Bonds from Auction Rate Securities to Variable
Rate Demand Notes.&#160; At that time, <b>DP&amp;L</b> repurchased these notes out of the market and
placed them with the Trustee to be held until the capital markets
corrected.&#160; These notes were redeemed in December&nbsp;2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
November&nbsp;21, 2006, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
entered into a $220 million unsecured revolving credit agreement.&#160; This agreement has a five-year term that
expires on November&nbsp;21, 2011 and provides<b> DP&amp;L</b>
with the ability to increase the size of the facility by an additional $50
million at any time.&#160; The facility
contains one financial covenant:&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> total debt to total capitalization ratio is not
to exceed 0.65 to 1.00.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, this covenant is met with a ratio of 0.40 to 1.00.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L </b>had no
outstanding borrowings under this credit facility at December&nbsp;31,
2009.&#160; Fees associated with this credit
facility were approximately $0.9 million in 2009 compared to $0.3 million in
2008.&#160; Changes in credit ratings,
however, may affect fees and the applicable interest.&#160; This revolving credit agreement contains a
$50 million letter of credit sublimit.&#160;
As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> had no
outstanding letters of credit against the facility.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> has
certain contractual agreements for the sale and purchase of power, fuel and
related energy services that contain credit rating related clauses allowing the
counter parties to seek additional surety under certain conditions.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

of New York as Trustee.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the December&nbsp;31,
2009 balance of unrecognized tax benefits, $21.6 million is due to uncertainty
in the timing of deductibility offset by $2.3 million of unrecognized tax
liabilities that would affect the effective tax rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We recognize interest and
penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in income taxes.&#160; The amount of interest and penalties accrued
was a benefit of $0.1 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and an expense of
less than $0.1 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160; The amount of interest and penalties recorded
in the statements of results of operations for 2009 and 2008 was a benefit of
$0.1 million and $9.0 million, respectively, and an expense of $4.1 million for
2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Following is a
summary of the tax years open to examination by major tax jurisdiction:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">U.S. Federal &#150; 2007 and forward</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">State and Local &#150; 2005 and forward</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None of the unrecognized
tax benefits are expected to significantly increase or decrease within the next
twelve months.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;13,
2006, we received correspondence from the ODT notifying us that the ODT had
completed their examination and review of our Ohio Corporation Franchise Tax
Returns for tax years 2002 through 2004 and that the final proposed audit
adjustments resulted in a balance due of $90.8 million before interest and
penalties.&#160; On June&nbsp;27, 2008, we
entered into a $42.0 million settlement agreement with the ODT resolving all
outstanding audit issues and appeals, including uncertain tax positions for tax
years 1998 through 2006.&#160; The $42 million
payment was made to the ODT in July&nbsp;2008.&#160;
Due to this settlement agreement, the balance of our unrecognized state
tax liabilities recorded at December&nbsp;31, 2007, in the amount of $56.3
million, was reversed resulting in a recorded income tax benefit of $8.5
million, net of federal tax impact, in 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">9.&#160; Pension and Postretirement Benefits </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> sponsors a defined benefit plan for
substantially all employees.&#160; For
collective bargaining employees, the defined benefits are based on a specific
dollar amount per year of service.&#160; For
all other employees, the defined benefit plan is based primarily on
compensation and years of service.&#160; We
fund pension plan benefits as accrued in accordance with the minimum funding
requirements of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974
(ERISA).&#160; In addition, we have a
Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan (SERP) for certain active and retired
key executives.&#160; Benefits under this SERP
have been frozen and no additional benefits can be earned.&#160; We<b>  </b>also have
unfunded liabilities related to retirement benefits for certain active,
terminated and retired key executives.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;23,
2006, <b>DPL</b>&#146;s Board of Directors approved a new
compensation and benefits program that includes The DPL Inc. Supplemental
Executive Defined Contribution Retirement Plan (SEDCRP) which replaces our SERP
that was terminated as to new participants in 2000.&#160; The Compensation Committee of the Board of
Directors designates the eligible employees.&#160;
Pursuant to the SEDCRP, we provide a supplemental retirement benefit to
participants by crediting an account established for each participant in
accordance with the Plan requirements.&#160;
We designate as hypothetical investment funds under the SEDCRP one or
more of the investment funds provided under The Dayton Power and Light Company
Employee Savings Plan.&#160; Each participant
may&nbsp;change his or her hypothetical investment fund selection at specified
times.&#160; If a participant does not elect a
hypothetical investment fund(s), then we select the hypothetical investment
fund(s)&nbsp;for such participant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A participant shall
become 100% vested in all amounts credited to his or her account upon the
completion of five vesting years, as defined in The Dayton Power and Light
Company Retirement Income Plan, or upon a change of control or the participant&#146;s
death or disability.&#160; If a participant&#146;s
employment is terminated, other than by death or disability, prior to such
participant becoming 100% vested in his or her account, the account shall be
forfeited as of the date of termination.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Qualified employees who
retired prior to 1987 and their dependents are eligible for health care and
life insurance benefits, while qualified employees who retired after 1987 are
eligible for life insurance benefits only.&#160;
We have funded a portion of the union-eligible health benefits using a
Voluntary Employee Beneficiary Association Trust.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory assets and
liabilities are recorded for the portion of the under- or over-funded
obligations related to the transmission and distribution areas of our electric
business and for the changes in the funded status of the plan that arise during
the year that are not recognized as a component of net periodic benefit
cost.&#160; These regulatory assets and
liabilities represent the regulated portion that would otherwise be charged or
credited to AOCI.&#160; We have historically
recorded these costs on the accrual basis and this is how these costs have been
historically recovered.&#160; This factor, combined
with the historical precedents from the PUCO and FERC, make these costs
probable of future rate recovery.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="1" width="25%" noshade color="black" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For purposes of
calculating the expected return on pension plan assets, under GAAP, the
market-related value of assets (MRVA) is used.&nbsp; GAAP requires that the
difference between actual plan asset returns and estimated plan asset returns
be admitted into the MRVA equally over a period not to exceed five years.&nbsp;
We use a methodology under which we admit the difference between actual and
estimated asset returns in the MRVA equally over a three year period.&nbsp; The
MRVA used in the 2009 calculation of expected return on pension plan assets was
approximately $275 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;26,
2007, <b>DP&amp;L </b>contributed $27.4 million in <b>DPL</b> common stock from its Master Trust assets to the
Retirement Income Plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our expected return on
plan asset assumptions, used to determine benefit obligations, are based on
historical long-term rates of return on investments, which use the widely
accepted capital market principle that assets with higher volatility generate a
greater return over the long run.&#160;
Current market factors, such as inflation and interest rates, as well as
asset diversification and portfolio rebalancing, are evaluated when long-term
capital market assumptions are determined.&#160;
Peer data and historical returns are reviewed to verify reasonableness
and appropriateness.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our overall expected
long-term rate of return on assets is approximately 8.50% for pension plan
assets and approximately 6.00% for retiree benefit plan assets.&#160; This expected return is based primarily on
historical returns and portfolio investment allocation.&#160; There can be no assurance of our ability to
generate those rates of return in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We expect to contribute
$10.4 million to our pension plans and $2.6 million to our other postretirement
benefit plans in 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Pension Protection
Act (the Act) of 2006 contained new requirements for our single employer
defined benefit pension plan.&#160; In
addition to establishing a 100% funding target for plan years beginning after December&nbsp;31,
2008, the Act also limits some benefits if the funded status of pension plans
drops below certain thresholds.&#160; Among
other restrictions under the Act, if the funded status of a plan falls below a
predetermined ratio which is 80% in 2010, lump-sum payments to new retirees are
limited to 50% of amounts that otherwise would have been paid and new benefit
improvements may not go into effect.&#160; For
the 2009 plan year, the funded status of our defined benefit pension plan as
calculated under the requirements of the Act was 101.7% and is estimated to be
91.7% until the 2010 status is certified in September&nbsp;2010 for the 2010
plan year.&#160; The Worker, Retiree, and
Employer Recovery Act of 2008 (WRERA), which was signed into law on December&nbsp;23,
2008, grants plan sponsors certain relief from funding requirements and benefit
restrictions of the Act.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Plan Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Plan assets are invested
using a total return investment approach whereby a mix of equity securities,
debt securities and other investments are used to preserve asset values,
diversify risk and achieve our target investment return benchmark.&#160; Investment strategies and asset allocations
are based on careful consideration of plan liabilities, the plan&#146;s funded
status and our financial condition.&#160;
Investment performance and asset allocation are measured and monitored
on an ongoing basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Plan assets are managed
in a balanced portfolio comprised of two major components:&#160; an equity portion and a fixed income
portion.&#160; The expected role of Plan
equity investments is to maximize the long-term real growth of Plan assets,
while the role of fixed income investments is to generate current income,
provide for more stable periodic returns and provide some protection against a
prolonged decline in the market value of Plan equity investments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-term strategic asset
allocation guidelines are determined by management and take into account the
Plan&#146;s long-term objectives as well as its short-term constraints.&#160; The target allocations for plan assets are
30-80% for equity securities, 30-65% for fixed income securities, 0-10% for
cash and 0-25% for alternative investments.&#160;
Equity securities include U.S. and international equity, while fixed
income securities include long-duration and high-yield bond funds and emerging
market debt funds.&#160; Other types of investments
include investments in hedge funds and private equity funds that follow several
different strategies.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="1" width="25%" noshade color="black" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .55in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This category includes
investments in equity securities of large, small and medium sized companies and
equity securities of foreign companies including those in developing countries.
The funds are valued using the net asset value method in which an average of
the market prices for the underlying investments is used to value the fund
except for the <b>DPL</b> common stock which is valued
using the closing price on the New York Stock Exchange.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .55in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This category includes
investments in investment-grade fixed-income instruments, U.S.
dollar-denominated debt securities of emerging market issuers and high yield
fixed-income securities that are rated below investment grade. The funds are
valued using the net asset value method in which an average of the market
prices for the underlying investments is used to value the fund.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .55in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .55in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(c)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This category comprises cash
held to pay beneficiaries.&#160; The fair
value of cash equals its book value.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .55in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(d)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This category represents a
private equity fund that specializes in management buyouts and a hedge fund of
funds made up of 30+ different hedge fund managers diversified over eight
different hedge strategies.&#160; The fair
value of the private equity fund is determined by the General Partner based on
the performance of the individual companies.&#160;
The fair value of the hedge fund is valued using the net asset value method
in which an average of the market prices for the underlying investments is used
to value the fund.</font></p>

securities.&#160; The funds are valued using
the net asset value method in which an average of the market prices for the
underlying investments is used to value the fund.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair values of our financial instruments are based on published
sources for pricing when possible.&#160; We
rely on modelled valuations only when no other method exists.&#160; The fair value of our financial instruments
represents estimates of possible value that may not be realized in the
future.&#160; The table below presents the

and 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Debt</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Debt
is fair valued based on current public market prices for disclosure purposes
only.&#160; Unrealized gains or losses are not
recognized in the financial statements as debt is presented at amortized cost
in the financial statements.&#160; The debt
amounts include the current portion payable in the next twelve months and have
maturities that range from 2010 to 2040.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Master Trust
Assets</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> established a
Master Trust to hold assets for the benefit of employees participating in
employee benefit plans and these assets are not used for general operating
purposes.&#160; These assets are primarily
comprised of open-ended mutual funds and <b>DPL</b> common
stock.&#160; The <b>DPL</b>
common stock held by the <b>DP&amp;L</b> Master
Trust is eliminated in consolidation and is not reflected in <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; The <b>DPL</b> common stock
is valued using current public market prices, while the open-ended mutual funds
are valued using the net asset value per unit.&#160;
These investments are accounted for as available-for-sale securities and
are recorded at fair value.&#160; Any
unrealized gains or losses are recognized in AOCI until the securities are
sold.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">had $0.3
million ($0.2 million after tax) in unrealized gains and no unrealized losses
on the Master Trust assets in AOCI at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and no unrealized
gains and $0.5 million ($0.3 million after tax) in unrealized losses in AOCI at
December&nbsp;31, 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> has $14.5
million ($9.5 million after tax) in unrealized gains and no unrealized losses
on the Master Trust assets in AOCI at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and $10.9 million
($7.0 million after tax) in unrealized gains and $0.5 million ($0.3 million
after tax) in unrealized losses in AOCI at December&nbsp;31, 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No
unrealized gains or losses are expected to be transferred to earnings in 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Transfer
of Master Trust Assets to Pension</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;26, 2007,
the Board of Directors approved a resolution permitting the transfer of 925,000
shares of <b>DPL </b>common stock from the <b>DP&amp;L</b> Master Trust to The Dayton Power and Light Company
Retirement Income Plan Trust (Pension).&#160;
This transaction was completed on November&nbsp;26, 2007, contributing
shares of <b>DPL </b>common stock with a fair value of
$27.4 million to the pension plan.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">105<a name="PB_105_055147_8627"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Asset
Value (NAV) per Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
table discloses the fair value and redemption frequency for those assets whose
fair value is estimated using the NAV per unit as of December&nbsp;31,
2009.&#160; These assets are part of the
Master Trust and exclude <b>DPL </b>common
stock which is valued using quoted market prices and not the NAV.&#160; Fair values estimated using the net asset
value per unit are considered Level 2 inputs within the fair value hierarchy,
unless they cannot be redeemed at the NAV on the reporting date.&#160; Investments that have restrictions on the
redemption of the investments are Level 3 inputs.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL</b> did not have any investments for sale at a price
different than the NAV.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a)</font></i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">This
category includes investments in high-quality, short-term securities.&#160; Investments in this category can be redeemed
immediately at the current net asset value per unit. </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(b)</font></i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">This
category includes investments in hedge funds representing an S&amp;P 500 index
and the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MCSI) U.S. Small Cap 1750
Index.&#160; Investments in this category can
be redeemed immediately at the current net asset value per unit.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(c)</font></i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">This
category includes investments in U.S. Treasury obligations and U.S. investment
grade bonds.&#160; Investments in this
category can be redeemed immediately at the current net asset value per unit.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(d)</font></i><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">This
category includes investments in stocks, bonds and short-term investments in a
mix of actively managed funds.&#160;
Investments in this category can be redeemed immediately at the current
net asset value per unit.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value Hierarchy</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair value is defined as
the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a
liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the
asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the
measurement date.&#160; The fair value
hierarchy requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs and
minimize the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value.&#160; These inputs are then categorized as Level 1
(quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities); Level 2
(observable inputs such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities or
quoted prices in markets that are not active); or Level 3 (unobservable
inputs).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Valuations of assets and
liabilities reflect the value of the instrument including the values associated
with counterparty risk.&#160; We include our
own credit risk and our counterparty&#146;s credit risk in our calculation of fair
value using the Global Corporate Cumulative Average Default Rates.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 1 inputs are used
for <b>DPL</b> common stock held by the Master
Trust and for derivative contracts such as heating oil futures.&#160; The fair value is determined by reference to
quoted market prices and other relevant information generated by market
transactions.&#160; Level 2 inputs are used to
value derivatives such as financial transmission rights where the quoted prices
are from a relatively inactive market; forward power contracts and forward
NYMEX-quality coal contracts which are traded on the OTC market but which are
valued using prices on the NYMEX for similar contracts on the OTC market; and
open-ended mutual funds that are in the Master Trust valued using the end of
day NAV.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Non-recurring fair value
measurements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value of an ARO
is estimated by discounting expected cash outflows to their present value at
the initial recording of the liability.&#160;
Cash outflows are based on the approximate future disposal cost as
determined by market information, historical information or other management
estimates.&#160; These inputs to the fair
value of the AROs would be considered Level 3 inputs under the fair value
hierarchy.&#160; We added a new ARO for a
landfill and additional layers to our existing landfill and asbestos AROs in
the amount of $2.7 million during 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> had $45.3 million and $15.0 million in
money market funds classified as cash and cash equivalents in its Consolidated
Balance Sheets at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160; The money market funds have quoted prices
that are generally equivalent to par.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">11.&#160; Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the normal
course of business, <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b> enter into various financial instruments, including
derivative financial instruments.&#160; We use
derivatives principally to manage the risk of changes in market prices for
commodities.&#160; The derivatives that we use
to economically hedge these risks are governed by our risk management policies
for forward and futures contracts. Our net positions are continually assessed
within our structured hedging programs to determine whether new or offsetting
transactions are required.&#160; The objective
of the hedging program is generally to mitigate financial risks while ensuring
that we have adequate resources to meet our requirements.&#160; We monitor and value derivative positions
monthly as part of our risk management processes.&#160; We use published sources for pricing when
possible to mark positions to market.&#160;
All of our derivative instruments are used for risk management purposes
and are designated as a cash flow hedge or marked to market each reporting
period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,
2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> had the following outstanding
derivative instruments:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash
Flow Hedges</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As part of our risk
management processes, we identify the relationships between hedging instruments
and hedged items, as well as the risk management objective and strategy for
undertaking various hedge transactions. The MTM value of cash flow hedges as
determined by current public market prices will continue to fluctuate with
changes in market prices up to contract expiration.&#160; The effective portion of the hedging
transaction is recognized in AOCI and transferred to earnings when the hedged
forecasted transaction takes place or when the hedged forecasted transaction is
probable of not occurring.&#160; The
ineffective portion of the cash flow hedge is recognized in earnings in the
current period.&#160; All risk components were
taken into account to determine the hedge effectiveness of the cash flow
hedges.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We currently use cash
flow hedging with forward power contracts and in 2003 we entered into an
interest rate swap which was settled that same year.&#160; Approximately $2.1 million ($1.4 million net of
tax) of accumulated losses in AOCI related to the above mentioned power hedges
are expected to be reclassified to earnings over the next twelve months.&#160; The balance of the remaining deferred gain
from the interest rate swap in AOCI is being amortized into earnings over the
life of the related bonds.&#160; Approximately
$2.5 million ($1.6 million net of tax) of accumulated gains in AOCI related to
the above referenced interest rate hedge are expected to be reclassified to
earnings over the next twelve months. &#160;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, the maximum length of time that we are hedging our exposure to
variability in future cash flows related to forecasted transactions is 23
months and 106 months for the forward power positions and the interest rate
hedge, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">*Includes counterparty

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Mark
to Market</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain derivative contracts
are entered into on a regular basis as part of our risk management program but
do not qualify for hedge accounting or the normal purchase and sales exceptions
under FASC 815.&#160; Accordingly, such
contracts are recorded at fair value with changes in the fair value charged or
credited to the statements of results of operations in the period in which the
change occurred.&#160; This is commonly
referred to as &#147;MTM&#148; accounting.&#160;
Contracts we enter into as part of our risk management program may be
settled financially, by physical delivery or net settled with the
counterparty.&#160; We currently MTM Financial
Transmission Rights (FTRs), heating oil futures and forward NYMEX-quality coal
contracts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> enters into coal contracts from time to
time to supply its generating plants.&#160; We
perform a quarterly evaluation of the different coal markets to determine if
these coal contracts are considered derivative instruments under FASC 815.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> has
concluded that NYMEX and NYMEX look-a-like coal contracts are considered derivative
instruments because they have been determined to be readily convertible to cash
under FASC 815.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain qualifying
derivative instruments have been designated as normal purchases or normal sales
contracts, as provided in FASC 815.&#160;
Derivative contracts that have been designated as normal purchases or
normal sales under FASC 815 are not subject to MTM accounting treatment and are
recognized in the statements of results of operations on an accrual basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory
Assets and Liabilities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
FASC 980, &#147;Regulated Operations,&#148; if a cost is probable of recovery in future
rates, it should be deferred as a regulatory asset.&#160; If a gain is probable of being returned to
customers, it should be deferred as a regulatory liability.&#160; Portions of the derivative contracts that are
marked to market each reporting period and are related to the retail portion of
<b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> load requirements are
included as part of the fuel factor approved by the PUCO beginning January&nbsp;1,
2010.&#160; Therefore, the Ohio jurisdictional
retail portion of the heating oil futures and the NYMEX-quality coal contracts
are deferred as a regulatory asset or liability until the contracts
settle.&#160; If these unrealized gains and
losses are no longer deemed to be probable of recovery through our rates, they
will be reclassified into earnings in the period such determination is made.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain of our OTC commodity derivative contracts are
under master netting agreements that contain provisions that require our debt
to maintain an investment grade credit rating from credit rating agencies.&#160; If our debt were to fall below investment
grade, we would be in violation of these provisions, and the counterparties to
the derivative instruments could request immediate payment or demand immediate
and ongoing full overnight collateralization of the MTM loss.&#160; The aggregate fair value of all derivative
instruments that are in a MTM loss position at December&nbsp;31, 2009, is $4.7
million.&#160; This amount is offset by $1.2
million in a broker margin account which offsets our loss positions on the
NYMEX Clearport traded heating oil and coal contracts.&#160; If our debt were to fall below investment
grade, we would have to post collateral for the remaining $3.5 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">12.&#160; Stock-Based Compensation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2006, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> shareholders approved The DPL Inc. Equity and
Performance Incentive Plan (the EPIP) which became immediately effective and
will remain in effect for a term of ten years, unless terminated sooner in
accordance with its terms.&#160; The
Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors will designate the employees
and directors eligible to participate in the EPIP and the times and types of
awards to be granted.&#160; Under the EPIP,
the Compensation Committee may&nbsp;grant equity-based compensation in the
form&nbsp;of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock,
restricted stock units, performance shares and units, and other stock-based
awards.&#160; Awards may&nbsp;be subject to
the achievement of certain management objectives.&#160; In addition, the EPIP provides, upon
recommendation of the Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board, for a
grant of a special equity award to recognize outstanding performance.&#160; A total of 4,500,000 shares of <b>DPL</b> common stock were reserved for issuance under the EPIP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table
summarizes share-based compensation expense recorded at <b>DPL</b>
and <b>DP&amp;L</b>:</font></p>
