<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Share-based awards issued
in <b>DPL&#146;s </b>common stock will be distributed
from treasury stock.&#160; <b>DPL</b> has sufficient treasury stock to satisfy all outstanding
share-based awards.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Determining
Fair Value</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Valuation
and Amortization Method &#151; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We estimate the fair value of stock options and RSUs
using a Black-Scholes-Merton model; performance shares are valued using a Monte
Carlo simulation; restricted shares are valued at the closing market price on
the day of grant and the Directors&#146; RSUs are valued at the closing market price
on the day prior to the grant date.&#160; We
amortize the fair value of all awards on a straight-line basis over the
requisite service periods, which are generally the vesting periods.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Expected
Volatility &#151; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our expected volatility assumptions are based on the historical
volatility of <b>DPL</b> common stock.&#160; The volatility range captures the high and
low volatility values for each award granted based on its specific terms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Expected
Life &#151; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
expected life assumption represents the estimated period of time from grant
until exercise and reflects historical employee exercise patterns.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Risk-Free
Interest Rate &#151; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The risk-free interest rate for the expected term of
the award is based on the corresponding yield curve in effect at the time of
the valuation for U.S. Treasury bonds having the same term as the expected life
of the award, i.e., a five year bond rate is used for valuing an award with a
five year expected life.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Expected
Dividend Yield &#151; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected dividend yield is based on <b>DPL&#146;s</b> current dividend rate, adjusted as necessary to
capture anticipated dividend changes and the 12 month average <b>DPL</b> common stock price.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Expected
Forfeitures &#151; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The forfeiture rate used to calculate compensation expense is based on <b>DPL&#146;s</b> historical experience, adjusted as necessary to
reflect special circumstances.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2000, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> Board of Directors adopted and <b>DPL&#146;s</b> shareholders approved The DPL Inc.
Stock Option Plan.&#160; On April&nbsp;26,
2006, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> shareholders approved The DPL
Inc. 2006 Equity and Performance Incentive Plan (EPIP).&#160; With the approval of the EPIP, no new awards
will be granted under The DPL Inc. Stock Option Plan, but shares relating to
awards that are forfeited or terminated under The DPL Inc. Stock Option Plan
may be granted under the EPIP.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, there were no unvested stock options.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Restricted
Stock Units (RSUs)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RSUs were granted to
certain key employees prior to 2001.&#160; As
a result of the settlement of the former executive litigation, all disputed
RSUs (1.3 million) were forfeited by three former executives (see Note 17 of
Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements).&#160;
There were 3,311 RSUs outstanding as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, none of
which has vested.&#160; The non-vested RSUs
will be paid in cash upon vesting in 2010.&#160;
Non-vested RSUs are valued quarterly at fair value using the
Black-Scholes-Merton model to determine the amount of compensation expense to
be recognized.&#160; Non-vested RSUs do not
earn dividends.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation expense is
recognized each quarter based on the change in the market price of <b>DPL</b> common stock.</font></p>

2009, 2008 and 2007, liabilities recorded for outstanding RSUs were $0.1
million, $0.2 million and $0.6 million, respectively, which are included in
Other deferred credits on the balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Performance
Shares</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
the EPIP, the Board adopted a Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP) under which <b>DPL</b> will grant a targeted number of performance shares of
common stock to executives.&#160; Grants under
the LTIP will be awarded based on a Total Shareholder Return Relative to Peers
performance.&#160; No performance shares will
be earned in a performance period if the three-year Total Shareholder Return
Relative to Peers is below the threshold of the 40</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;percentile.&#160;
Further, the LTIP awards will be capped at 200% of the target number of
performance shares, if the Total Shareholder Return Relative to Peers is at or
above the threshold of the 90</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;percentile.&#160;
The Total Shareholder Return Relative to Peers is considered a market
condition under FASC 718.&#160; There is a
three year requisite service period for each portion of the performance shares.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Restricted Shares</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the EPIP, the Board granted shares of <b>DPL</b> Restricted Shares to various executives.&#160; The Restricted Shares are registered in the
executive&#146;s name, carry full voting privileges, receive dividends as declared
and paid on all <b>DPL</b> common stock and vest after a
specified service period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July&nbsp;2008,
the Board of Directors granted compensation awards to a select group of
management employees.&#160; The management
restricted stock awards have a three-year requisite service period, carry full
voting privileges and receive dividends as declared and paid on all <b>DPL</b> common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;17,
2009, the <b>DPL</b> Board of Directors approved a
two-part equity compensation award under <b>DPL&#146;s </b>2006<b>  </b>Equity and Performance Incentive Plan for certain of <b>DPL&#146;s</b> executive officers.&#160;
The first part is a restricted share grant and the second part is a
matching restricted share grant.&#160; A total
of 90,036 restricted shares were granted on September&nbsp;17, 2009 as part of
the restricted share grant.&#160; These
restricted shares generally vest after five years if the participant remains
continuously employed with <b>DPL</b> or a
subsidiary and if the year over year average basic EPS has increased by at
least 1% per year from 2009 - 2013.&#160;
Under the matching restricted share grant, participants will have a
three-year period from the date of plan implementation during which they may
purchase <b>DPL</b> common stock equal in value to up
to two times their base salary.&#160; <b>DPL</b> will match the shares purchased with another grant of
restricted stock (matching restricted share grant).&#160; The percentage match by <b>DPL</b>
is detailed in the table below.&#160; The
matching restricted share grant will generally vest over a three year period if
the participant continues to hold the originally purchased shares and remains
continuously employed with <b>DPL </b>or a
subsidiary<b>.</b> The restricted shares are registered
in the executive&#146;s name, carry full voting privileges and receive dividends as
declared and paid on all <b>DPL</b> common
stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Non-Employee Director Restricted Stock Units</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the EPIP, as part of their annual
compensation for service to <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>, each non-employee Director receives a retainer in
RSUs on the date of the annual meeting of shareholders.&#160; The RSUs will become non-forfeitable on April&nbsp;15
of the following year.&#160; All of the RSUs
become non-forfeitable in the event of death, disability, or change in control;
but if the Director resigns or retires prior to the April&nbsp;15 vesting date,
the vested shares will be distributed on a pro rata basis.&#160; The RSUs accrue quarterly dividends in the
form of additional RSUs.&#160; Upon vesting,
the RSUs will become exercisable and will be distributed in <b>DPL</b> common stock, unless the Director chooses to defer
receipt of the shares until a later date.&#160;
The RSUs are valued at the closing stock price on the day prior to the
grant and the compensation expense is recognized evenly over the vesting
period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management Performance Shares</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;28,
2008, the Board of Directors granted compensation awards for select management
employees.&#160; The grants have a three year
requisite service period and certain performance conditions during the performance
period.&#160; The management performance
shares can only be awarded in <b>DPL </b>common
stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">13.&nbsp;&nbsp;Redeemable Preferred Stock</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">has $100 par value preferred stock,
4,000,000 shares authorized, of which 228,508 are outstanding as of December&nbsp;31,
2009.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
also has $25 par value preferred stock, 4,000,000 shares authorized, none of

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The <b>DP&amp;L</b> preferred stock may be redeemed at <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> option as determined by its Board of Directors at
the per-share redemption prices indicated above, plus cumulative accrued
dividends.&#160; In addition, <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> Amended Articles of Incorporation contain
provisions that permit preferred stockholders to elect members of the Board of
Directors in the event that cumulative dividends on the preferred stock are in
arrears in an aggregate amount equivalent to at least four full quarterly
dividends.&#160; Since this potential
redemption-triggering event is not solely within the control of <b>DP&amp;L</b>, the preferred stock is presented on the Balance
Sheets as &#147;Redeemable Preferred Stock&#148; in a manner consistent with temporary
equity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As
long as any <b>DP&amp;L</b> preferred stock is
outstanding, <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> Amended Articles of
Incorporation also contain provisions restricting the payment of cash dividends
on any of its common stock if, after giving effect to such dividend, the
aggregate of all such dividends distributed subsequent to December&nbsp;31,
1946 exceeds the net income of <b>DP&amp;L</b>
available for dividends on its common stock subsequent to December&nbsp;31,
1946, plus $1.2&nbsp;million.&#160; This
dividend restriction has historically not impacted <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s </b>ability
to pay cash dividends and, as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
retained earnings of $640.3 million were all available for common stock
dividends payable to <b>DPL. </b>&#160;We do not expect this restriction to have an
effect on the payment of cash dividends in the future.&#160; <b>DPL</b> records
dividends on preferred stock of <b>DP&amp;L</b> within
Interest expense on the Statements of Results of Operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">14.&nbsp;&nbsp;Common
Shareholders&#146; Equity</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> has 250,000,000 authorized common shares, of which
118,966,767 are outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Dividend Reinvestment Plan</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;1, 2009, <b>DPL</b> introduced
a new direct stock purchase and dividend reinvestment plan. The plan provides
both registered shareholders and new investors with the ability to purchase
shares and also to reinvest their dividends.&#160;
This plan is administered by Computershare Trust Company, N.A., and not
by <b>DPL</b>.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Shareholder Rights Plan</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2001, <b>DPL</b>&#146;s Board of
Directors renewed its Shareholder Rights Plan, attaching one right to each
common share outstanding at the close of business on December&nbsp;13,
2001.&#160; The rights separate from the
common shares and become exercisable at the exercise price of $130 per right in
the event of certain attempted business combinations.&#160; The renewed plan expires on December&nbsp;31,
2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Warrants</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2000, <b>DPL</b> entered
into a series of recapitalization transactions which included the issuance of
31.6 million warrants for an aggregate purchase price of $50 million.&#160; The warrants are exercisable, in whole or in
part, for common shares at any time during the twelve-year period commencing on
March&nbsp;13, 2000.&#160; Each warrant is
exercisable for one common share, subject to anti-dilution adjustments (e.g.,
stock split, stock dividend) at an exercise price of $21.00 per common share.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, in the event of a declaration, issuance or consummation of
any dividend, spin-off or other distribution or similar transaction by <b>DPL</b> of the capital stock of any of its subsidiaries,
additional warrants of such subsidiary will be issued to the warrant holder so
that after the transaction, the warrant holder will have the same interest in
the fully diluted number of common shares of such subsidiary the warrant holder
had in <b>DPL</b> immediately prior to such
transaction.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the warrant agreement, <b>DPL</b> has
authorized common shares sufficient to provide for the exercise in full of all
outstanding warrants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The warrants repurchased were cancelled by <b>DPL </b>on
the dates they were repurchased.&#160; As a
result of the warrants exercised under both cash and cashless provisions, <b>DPL</b> issued a total of 5.0 million shares of common stock
from treasury stock and in turn received total cash proceeds of $77.7
million.&#160; <b>DPL</b>
used a portion of the proceeds to repurchase warrants directly from holders and
the remaining proceeds were used to repurchase shares under its Stock
Repurchase Program discussed below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stock Repurchase Program</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;28, 2009, the <b>DPL</b> Board of
Directors approved a Stock Repurchase Program under which <b>DPL</b>
may use proceeds from the exercise of warrants to repurchase warrants or its
common stock from time to time in the open market, through private transactions
or otherwise. The Stock Repurchase Program will run through June&nbsp;30, 2012,
which is three months after the end of the warrant exercise period.&#160; Under the Stock Repurchase Program, <b>DPL</b> repurchased a total of 2.4 million shares at an average
per share price of $26.96 during the quarter ended December&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2009, the amount still
available that could be used to repurchase stock under the Stock Repurchase
Program is approximately $3.9 million but could be higher if additional
warrants are exercised for cash in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ESOP</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During October&nbsp;1992,
our Board of Directors approved the formation of a Company-sponsored ESOP to
fund matching contributions to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> 401(k)&nbsp;retirement
savings plan and certain other payments to eligible full-time employees.&#160; This leveraged ESOP is funded by an exempt
loan, which is secured by the ESOP shares.&#160;
As debt service payments are made on the loan, shares are released on a
pro rata basis.&#160; ESOP shares used to fund
matching contributions to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> 401(k)&nbsp;vest
after three years of service; other compensation shares awarded vest
immediately.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In general, participants
are eligible for lump sum payments upon termination of their employment and the
submission and subsequent approval of an application for benefits.&#160; Earlier distributions can occur for a
Qualified Domestic Relations Order or for death.&#160; Otherwise, distribution must occur within 60
days after the plan year in which the later of one of the following events
occur: 65</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;birthday, 10</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;anniversary of participation, or termination
of employment.&#160; Participants are allowed
to take distributions during employment if older than 59&#189; and/or for a hardship
as defined in the Plan document.&#160;
Additionally, participants may elect on a quarterly basis to diversify
their vested ESOP shares into <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> 401(k)&nbsp;retirement
savings plan.&#160; Distributions are made in
cash unless the participant requests the distribution be made in stock.&#160; A repurchase obligation exists for vested
shares held by the ESOP if they cannot be sold in the open market.&#160; The fair value of shares subject to the
repurchase obligation at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008 was approximately
$57.6 million and $42.4 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1992, the Plan entered
into a $90 million loan agreement with <b>DPL</b> in order to
purchase shares of <b>DPL</b> common
stock in the open market.&#160; The term loan
agreement provided for principal and interest on the loan to be paid prior to October&nbsp;9,
2007, with the right to extend the loan for an additional ten years.&#160; In 2007, the maturity date was extended to October&nbsp;7,
2017.&#160; Effective January&nbsp;1, 2009,
the interest on the loan was amended to a fixed rate of 2.06%, payable
annually.&#160; Dividends received by the ESOP
for unallocated shares are used to repay the principal and interest on the ESOP
loan to <b>DPL</b>.&#160;
Dividends on the allocated shares are charged to retained earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The ESOP used the full
amount of the loan to purchase 4.7 million shares of <b>DPL</b>
common stock in the open market.&#160; As a
result of the 1997 stock split, the ESOP held 7.1 million shares of <b>DPL </b>common stock.&#160; The
cost of shares held by the ESOP and not yet released is reported as a reduction
of Common shareholders&#146; equity.&#160; At December&nbsp;31,
2009, Common shareholders&#146; equity reflects the cost of 2.8 million unreleased
shares held in suspense by the DPL Inc. Employee Stock Ownership Trust.&#160; The fair value of the 2.8 million ESOP shares
held in suspense at December&nbsp;31, 2009 was $77.5 million.&#160; When shares are committed to be released from
the ESOP, compensation expense is recorded based on the fair value of the
shares committed to be released, with a corresponding credit to our
equity.&#160; Compensation expense associated
with the ESOP, which is based on the fair value of the shares committed to be
released for allocation, amounted to $4.0 million in 2009, $1.5 million in 2008
and $9.0 million in 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For purposes of EPS
computations and in accordance with GAAP, we treat ESOP shares as outstanding
if they have been allocated to participants, released or have been committed to
be released.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, the ESOP has 4.2 million shares allocated to participants with an
additional 21 thousand shares which have been released but unallocated to
participants.&#160; ESOP cumulative shares
outstanding for the calculation of EPS were 4.2 million in 2009, 4.0 million in
2008 and 3.9 million in 2007.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">121<a name="PB_121_023256_141"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">15.&#160; Comprehensive Income (Loss)</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Comprehensive income
(loss) is defined as the change in equity (net assets) of a business entity
during a period from transactions and other events and circumstances from
non-owner sources.&#160; It includes all
changes in equity during a period except those resulting from investments by
owners and distributions to owners.&#160;&#160;
Comprehensive income (loss) has two components: Net income (loss) and
Other comprehensive income (loss).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table
provides the tax effects allocated to each component of Other comprehensive
income (loss) for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, 2008 and 2007:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">16.&#160; EPS</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic
EPS is based on the weighted-average number of <b>DPL</b> common shares outstanding during the year.&#160; Diluted EPS is based on the weighted-average
number of <b>DPL</b> common and
common-equivalent shares outstanding during the year, except in periods where
the inclusion of such common-equivalent shares is anti-dilutive.&#160; Excluded from outstanding shares for these
weighted-average computations are shares held by <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Master Trust Plan for deferred compensation and unreleased shares held by <b>DPL&#146;s</b> ESOP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The common-equivalent
shares excluded from the calculation of diluted EPS, because they were
anti-dilutive, were not material for all the periods ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, 2008 and 2007.&#160; These shares may be
dilutive in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following illustrates
the reconciliation of the numerators and denominators of the basic and diluted
EPS computations:</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">17.&#160; Executive Litigation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;21, 2007, we
settled litigation with three former executives.&nbsp; As part of this
settlement, the three former executives relinquished and dismissed all their
claims including those related to certain deferred compensation, RSUs, MVE
incentives, stock options and legal fees. The RSUs and stock options
relinquished and forfeited were 1.3 million and 3.6 million, respectively.&#160; Prior to the settlement date, we had accrued
obligations of $64.2 million.&nbsp; Included in these amounts was $3.1 million
associated with the forfeiture of stock options.&#160; In exchange for our payment of $25 million
and the relinquishment by the former executives of certain contested
compensation discussed above, all of these claims by all parties were settled
and released.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of this
settlement, during 2007, <b>DPL </b>realized
a net pre-tax gain in continuing and discontinued operations of approximately
$31.0 million and $8.2 million, respectively.&nbsp; The net gain is comprised
of the reversal of the $64.2 million of accrued obligations less the $25
million settlement.&nbsp; The obligations related to the discontinued
operations were associated with the management of <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
financial asset portfolio, which was conducted in our MVE subsidiary.&#160; The MVE operations were discontinued in 2005
with the sale of the financial asset portfolio.&#160;
The $25 million settlement expense was allocated between continuing and
discontinued operations based on the proportionate share of the obligations of
each.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of this
settlement during 2007, <b>DP&amp;L </b>realized
a net pre-tax gain in continuing operations of $35.3 million.&nbsp; Accrued
obligations associated with the former executives&#146; litigation were recorded by <b>DP&amp;L</b> since the obligations were associated with our
non-qualified benefit plans.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> had no ownership of <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
discontinued financial asset portfolio business, therefore these liabilities
were reversed and <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> net
pre-tax gain was recorded within continuing operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The $25 million
settlement was funded from the sale of financial assets held in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> Master Trust Plan for deferred compensation.&#160; As part of this transaction, during the
second quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2007, <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b> recorded a $3.2 million realized gain which was
reflected in investment income<b>.</b></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">18.&#160; Insurance Recovery</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;30, 2007, <b>DP&amp;L</b> executed a settlement agreement
for $14.5 million with one of our insurers, Associated Electric&nbsp;&amp; Gas
Insurance Services (AEGIS), under a fiduciary liability policy to recoup a
portion of legal fees associated with our litigation against three former
executives.&#160; This was recorded as a
reduction to operation and maintenance expense during 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;16, 2007, <b>DPL</b> filed a claim with Energy Insurance
Mutual (EIM) to recoup legal expenses associated with our litigation against
certain former executives.&nbsp; Arbitration on that claim occurred on May&nbsp;13,
2009.&#160; </font><tt><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
arbitration panel issued a ruling in Phase 1 of the arbitration on September&nbsp;25,
2009, finding that most of the claims involving the former executives were
covered. &nbsp;</font></tt><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
accordance with GAAP, <b>DPL</b> recorded
expenses totaling $7.5 million in 2008 but has not recorded any assets for
possible recovery of these expenses.&#160; The
matter is pending.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">19.&#160; Contractual Obligations, Commercial
Commitments and Contingencies</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL &#151;
Guarantees</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the normal course of
business, <b>DPL </b>enters into various agreements with its
wholly-owned subsidiaries, DPLE and DPLER, providing financial or performance
assurance to third parties.&#160; These
agreements are entered into primarily to support or enhance the
creditworthiness otherwise attributed to DPLE and DPLER on a stand-alone basis, thereby facilitating the extension of
sufficient credit to accomplish DPLE&#146;s and DPLER&#146;s intended commercial
purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,
2009, <b>DPL</b> had $51 million of
guarantees to third parties for future financial or performance assurance under
such agreements, on behalf of DPLE and DPLER.&#160;
The guarantee arrangements entered into by<b> DPL</b>
with these third parties cover all present and future obligations of DPLE and
DPLER to such beneficiaries and are terminable at any time by <b>DPL</b> upon written notice to the beneficiaries. The carrying
amount of obligations for commercial transactions covered by these guarantees
and recorded in our Consolidated Balance Sheets was $0.6 million and
$1.6&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">125<a name="PB_125_030756_4141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To date, neither <b>DPL</b> nor <b>DP&amp;L </b>have
incurred any losses related to the guarantees of DPLE&#146;s obligations and we
believe it is remote that either <b>DPL</b>
or <b>DP&amp;L</b> would be required to
perform or incur any losses in the future associated with any of the above
guarantees of DPLE&#146;s obligations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L
&#151; Equity Ownership Interest</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> owns a 4.9% equity ownership interest in an electric
generation company which is recorded using the cost method of accounting under
GAAP.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> could be responsible for the
repayment of 4.9%, or $54.4 million, of a $1,110 million debt obligation that
matures in 2026.&#160; This would only happen
if this electric generation company defaulted on its debt payments.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, we have no
knowledge of such a default.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-term
debt:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> long-term debt as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, consists
of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> first mortgage bonds
and tax-exempt pollution control bonds and <b>DPL&#146;s</b>
unsecured senior notes.&#160; These long-term
debt amounts include current maturities but exclude unamortized debt discounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DP&amp;L&#146;s</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> long-term debt as of December&nbsp;31,
2009, consists of first mortgage bonds and tax-exempt pollution control
bonds.&#160; These long-term debt amounts
include current maturities but exclude unamortized debt discounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">See Note 7 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest payments:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest payments associated with the long-term debt
described above.&#160; The interest payments
relating to variable-rate debt are projected using the interest rate prevailing
at December&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pension and postretirement payments:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL, </b>through its principal subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>,
had estimated future benefit payments as outlined in Note 9 of Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements.&#160; These
estimated future benefit payments are projected through 2019.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;text-indent:.7pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital leases:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL, </b>through its principal subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>,
had one immaterial capital lease that expires in September&nbsp;2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating leases:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL, </b>through its principal subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>,
had several immaterial operating leases with various terms and expiration
dates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Coal contracts:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL, </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">through its principal
subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>,</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> has entered into various long-term coal
contracts to supply the coal requirements for the generating plants it
operates.&#160; Some contract prices are
subject to periodic adjustment and have features that limit price escalation in
any given year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Limestone
contracts:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL, </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">through its principal
subsidiary <b>DP&amp;L</b>,</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> has entered into various limestone
contracts to supply limestone used in the operation of FGD equipment at its
generating facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchase orders and other contractual obligations:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>
had various other contractual obligations including non-cancelable contracts to
purchase goods and services with various terms and expiration dates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reserve for uncertain tax positions:</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to the uncertainty regarding the timing of future
cash outflows associated with our unrecognized tax benefits of $19.3 million,
we are unable to make a reliable estimate of the periods of cash settlement
with the respective tax authorities and have not included such amounts in the
contractual obligations table above.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 14.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the normal
course of business, we are subject to various lawsuits, actions, proceedings,
claims and other matters asserted under laws and regulations.&#160; We believe the amounts provided in our
Consolidated Financial Statements, as prescribed by GAAP, are adequate in light
of the probable and estimable contingencies.&#160;
However, there can be no assurances that the actual amounts required to
satisfy alleged liabilities from various legal proceedings, claims, tax
examinations, and other matters, including the matters discussed below, and to
comply with applicable laws and regulations, will not exceed the amounts
reflected in our Consolidated Financial Statements.&#160; As such, costs, if any, that may be incurred
in excess of those amounts provided as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, cannot be
reasonably determined.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Governmental and
Regulatory Inquiries</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;10, 2004, <b>DPL&#146;s</b> and <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
Corporate Controller sent a memorandum (the Memorandum) to the Chairman of the
Audit Committee of our Board of Directors.&#160;
The Memorandum expressed the Corporate Controller&#146;s &#147;concerns,
perspectives and viewpoints&#148; regarding financial reporting and governance
issues within <b>DPL</b> and <b>DP&amp;L</b>.&#160; In response, the Board initiated an internal
investigation whose findings and recommendations led to corrective action taken
regarding internal controls, process issues and the tone at the top.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;28, 2004, the
U.S. Attorney&#146;s Office for the Southern District of Ohio, assisted by the
Federal Bureau of Investigation, notified <b>DPL</b>
and <b>DP&amp;L</b> that it had initiated
an inquiry involving matters connected to our internal investigation.&#160; This inquiry remains pending.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On or about June&nbsp;24,
2004, the SEC commenced a formal investigation into the issues raised by the
Memorandum.&#160; This investigation remains
pending.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Environmental
Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DPL</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">,<b> DP&amp;L</b> and our
subsidiaries&#146; facilities and operations are subject to a wide range of
environmental regulations and laws by federal, state and local
authorities.&#160; As well as imposing
continuing compliance obligations, these laws and regulations authorize the
imposition of substantial penalties for noncompliance, including fines,
injunctive relief and other sanctions. In the normal course of business, we
have investigatory and remedial activities underway at these facilities to
comply, or to determine compliance, with such regulations.&nbsp; We record liabilities
for losses that are probable of occurring and can be reasonably estimated.<b>&#160; DPL,</b>
through its wholly owned captive insurance subsidiary MVIC, has an actuarially
calculated reserve of $1.2 million for environmental matters.&#160; We evaluate the potential liability related
to probable losses quarterly and may revise&nbsp;our estimates.&nbsp; Such
revisions in the estimates of the potential liabilities could have a material
effect on our results of operations, financial position or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Air Quality</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1990, the federal
government amended the CAA to further regulate air pollution.&#160; Under the law, the USEPA sets limits on how
much of a pollutant can be in the air anywhere in the United States.&#160; The CAA allows individual states to have
stronger pollution controls, but states are not allowed to have weaker
pollution controls than those set for the whole country.&#160; The CAA has a material effect on our
operations and such effects are detailed below with respect to certain programs
under the CAA.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;27, 2003,
the USEPA published final rules&nbsp;regarding the equipment replacement
provision (ERP) of the routine maintenance, repair and replacement (RMRR)
exclusion of the CAA.&nbsp; Activities at power plants that fall within the
scope of the RMRR exclusion do not trigger new source review requirements,
including the imposition of stricter emission limits.&#160; On December&nbsp;24, 2003, the United States
Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit stayed the effective date of the rule&nbsp;pending
its decision on the merits of the lawsuits filed by numerous states and
environmental organizations challenging the final rules.&#160; On June&nbsp;6, 2005, the USEPA issued its
final response on the reconsideration of the ERP exclusion.&#160; The USEPA clarified its position, but did not
change any aspect of the 2003 final rules.&#160;
This decision was appealed and the D.C. Circuit vacated the final rules&nbsp;on
March&nbsp;17, 2006.&#160; The scope of the
RMRR exclusion remains uncertain due to this action by the D.C Circuit, as well
as multiple litigations not directly involving us where courts are defining the
scope of the exception with respect to the specific facts and circumstances of
the particular power plants and activities before the courts.&#160; While we believe that we have not engaged in
any activities with respect to our existing power plants that would trigger the
new source review requirements, if new source review requirements were imposed
on any of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> existing power plants, the
results could be materially adverse to us.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The USEPA issued a
proposed rule&nbsp;on October&nbsp;20, 2005 concerning the test for measuring
whether modifications to electric generating units should trigger application
of New Source Review (NSR) standards under the CAA.&#160; A supplemental rule&nbsp;was also proposed on
May&nbsp;8, 2007 to include additional options for determining if there is an
emissions increase when an existing electric generating unit makes a physical
or operational change.&#160; The rule&nbsp;was
challenged by environmental organizations and has not been finalized.&#160; While we cannot at this time predict the
outcome of this rulemaking, any finalized rules&nbsp;could materially affect
our operations.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;17,
2003, the USEPA proposed the Interstate Air Quality Rule&nbsp;(IAQR) designed
to reduce and permanently cap SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and NOx emissions from electric
utilities.&#160; The proposed IAQR focused on
states, including Ohio, whose power plant emissions are believed to be
significantly contributing to fine particle and ozone pollution in other
downwind states in the eastern United States.&#160;
On June&nbsp;10, 2004, the USEPA issued a supplemental proposal to the
IAQR, now renamed the CAIR.&#160; The final rules&nbsp;were
signed on March&nbsp;10, 2005 and were published on May&nbsp;12, 2005.&#160; CAIR created an interstate trading program
for annual NOx emission</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">128<a name="PB_128_032150_3736"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">allowances and made
modifications to an existing trading program for SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; On August&nbsp;24, 2005, the USEPA proposed
additional revisions to the CAIR.&#160; On July&nbsp;11,
2008, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit issued a
decision to vacate the USEPA&#146;s CAIR and its associated Federal Implementation
Plan and remanded to the USEPA with instructions to issue new regulations that
conformed with the procedural and substantive requirements of the CAA.&#160; The Court&#146;s decision, in part, invalidated
the new NOx annual emission allowance trading program and the modifications to
the SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;emission trading program established by the March&nbsp;10,
2005 rules, and created uncertainty regarding future NOx and SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;emission
reduction requirements and their timing.&#160;
The USEPA and a group representing utilities filed a request on September&nbsp;24,
2008 for a rehearing before the entire
Court.&nbsp; On December&nbsp;23, 2008, the U.S. Court of Appeals issued
an order on reconsideration that permits CAIR to remain in effect until the
USEPA issues new regulations that would conform to the CAA requirements and the
Court&#146;s July&nbsp;11, 2008 decision.&nbsp; In January&nbsp;2010, the Court
ordered the USEPA to file a response to a Petition for Mandamus filed by
parties in the original case who are now seeking a Court order to require the
USEPA to issue new regulations by March&nbsp;1, 2010.&nbsp; We are currently
unable to predict the outcome of this Petition or the timing or impact of any
new regulations relating to CAIR.&#160; CAIR
has and will continue to have a material effect on our operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2007, the Ohio
EPA revised their State Implementation Plan (SIP) to incorporate a CAIR program
consistent with the IAQR.&#160; The Ohio EPA
had received partial approval from the USEPA and had been awaiting full program
approval from the USEPA when the U.S. Court of Appeals issued its July&nbsp;11,
2008 decision.&#160; As a result of the December&nbsp;23,
2008 order, the Ohio EPA proposed revised rules&nbsp;on May&nbsp;11, 2009,
which were finalized on July&nbsp;15, 2009. On September&nbsp;25, 2009, the
USEPA issued a full SIP approval for the Ohio CAIR program.&#160; We do not expect that full SIP approval of
the Ohio CAIR program will have a significant impact on operations.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
the fourth quarter of 2007, <b>DP&amp;L</b> began
a program for selling excess emission allowances, including annual NOx</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">emission allowances and
SO</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2 </font><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">emission
allowances that were the subject of CAIR trading programs.&#160; In subsequent quarters, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
recognized gains from the sale of excess emission allowances to third
parties.&#160; The court&#146;s CAIR decision
affected the trading market for excess allowances and impacted <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> program for selling additional excess allowances
in 2008.&#160; Although in January&nbsp;2009
we resumed selling excess allowances due to the revival of the trading market,
the long-term impact of the court&#146;s decision, and of the actions the USEPA or
others will take in response to this decision,<b>  </b>is
not fully known at this time and could have an adverse effect on us.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;30,
2004, the USEPA published its proposal to restrict mercury and other air toxins
from coal-fired and oil-fired utility plants.&#160;
The USEPA &#147;de-listed&#148; mercury as a hazardous air pollutant from
coal-fired and oil-fired utility plants and, instead, proposed a cap-and-trade
approach to regulate the total amount of mercury emissions allowed from such
sources.&#160; The final Clean Air Mercury Rule&nbsp;(CAMR)
was signed March&nbsp;15, 2005 and was published on May&nbsp;18, 2005.&#160; On March&nbsp;29, 2005, nine states sued the
USEPA, opposing the cap-and-trade regulatory approach taken by the USEPA.&#160; In 2007, the Ohio EPA adopted rules&nbsp;implementing
the CAMR program.&#160; On February&nbsp;8,
2008, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit struck
down the USEPA regulations, finding that the USEPA had not complied with
statutory requirements applicable to &#147;de-listing&#148; a hazardous air pollutant and
that a cap-and-trade approach was not authorized by law for &#147;listed&#148; hazardous
air pollutants.&#160; A request for rehearing
before the entire Court of Appeals was denied and a petition for review before
the U.S. Supreme Court was filed on October&nbsp;17, 2008.&#160; On February&nbsp;23, 2009, the U.S. Supreme
Court denied the petition.&#160; The USEPA is
expected to move forward on setting Maximum Available Control Technology (MACT)
standards for coal- and oil-fired electric generating units.&#160; Upon publication in the federal register
following finalization, affected exempt generating units (EGUs) will have three
years to come into compliance with the new requirements.&#160; At this time, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is unable to determine the impact of the promulgation of new MACT standards on
its financial position or results of operations; however, a MACT standard could
have a material adverse effect on our operations, in particular, our unscrubbed
units.&#160; We cannot at this time project
the final costs we may incur to comply with any resulting mercury restriction
regulations.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;5,
2005, the USEPA published its final non-attainment designations for the National
Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) for Fine Particulate Matter 2.5 (PM
2.5).&nbsp; These designations included counties and partial counties in which <b>DP&amp;L</b> operates and/or owns generating facilities.&nbsp;
On March&nbsp;4, 2005, <b>DP&amp;L</b> and
other Ohio electric utilities and electric generators filed a petition for
review in the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals, challenging the final rule&nbsp;creating
these designations.&nbsp; On November&nbsp;30, 2005, the court ordered the
USEPA to decide on all petitions for reconsideration by January&nbsp;20,
2006.&#160; On January&nbsp;20, 2006, the
USEPA denied the petitions for reconsideration.&#160;
On July&nbsp;7, 2009, the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the USEPA
non-attainment designations for the areas impacting <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
generation plants, however, on October&nbsp;8, 2009, the USEPA issued new
designations based on 2008 monitoring data that showed all areas in attainment
to the standard with the exception of several counties in northeastern
Ohio.&#160; The USEPA is expected to propose revisions
to the PM 2.5 standard in late 2010 as part of its routine five-year
rule&nbsp;review cycle.&#160; At this time, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is unable to determine the impact the revisions to
the PM 2.5 standard will have on its financial position or results of
operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">129<a name="PB_129_032212_9621"></a></font></p>
