<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of
Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;5,
2004, the USEPA issued its proposed regional haze rule, which addresses how
states should determine the Best Available Retrofit Technology (BART) for
sources covered under the regional haze rule.&nbsp; Final rules&nbsp;were
published July&nbsp;6, 2005, providing states with several options for
determining whether sources in the state should be subject to BART.&nbsp; In
the final rule, the USEPA made the determination that CAIR achieves greater
progress than BART and may be used by states as a BART substitute.&nbsp;
Numerous units owned and operated by us will be impacted by BART. &nbsp;We
cannot determine the extent of the impact until Ohio determines how BART will be
implemented.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to a U.S.
Supreme Court decision that the USEPA has the authority to regulate CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;emissions from
motor vehicles, the USEPA made a finding that CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and certain other gases are pollutants under
the CAA.&nbsp; The USEPA has not yet identified the specifics of how these
newly designated pollutants will be regulated.&#160;
In April&nbsp;2009, the USEPA issued a proposed endangerment finding
under the CAA.&#160; The proposed finding
determined that CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and other GHGs from motor vehicles threaten
the health and welfare of future generations by contributing to climate
change.&#160; If the proposed finding is
finalized, it could lead to the regulation of CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and other GHGs from sources other than motor
vehicles, including coal-fired plants that we own and operate.&#160; Recently, several bills have been introduced
at the federal level to regulate GHG emissions.&#160;
In June&nbsp;2009, the U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 2454,
the American Clean Energy and Security Act (ACES).&#160; This proposed legislation targets a reduction
in the emission of GHGs from large sources by 80% in 2050 through an economy
wide cap and trade program.&#160; ACES also
includes energy efficiency and renewable energy initiatives.&#160; Approximately 99% of the energy we produce is
generated by coal.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
share of CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2 </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">emissions at generating stations we own
and co-own is approximately 16 million tons annually.&#160; Proposed GHG legislation finalized at a
future date could have a significant effect on <b>DP&amp;L&#146;</b>s
operations and costs, which could adversely affect our net income, cash flows
and financial position.&#160; However, due to
the uncertainty associated with such legislation, we are currently unable to
predict the final outcome or the financial impact that this legislation will
have on us.&#160; On September&nbsp;22, 2009,
the USEPA issued a final rule&nbsp;for mandatory reporting of GHGs from large
sources that emit 25,000 metric tons per year or more of CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">,&#160; including
electric generating units.&#160; The first
report is due in March&nbsp;2011 for 2010 emissions.&#160; This reporting rule&nbsp;will guide development
of policies and programs to reduce emissions.&#160;
<b>DP&amp;L</b> does not anticipate that this
reporting rule&nbsp;will result in any significant cost or other impact on
current operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;15,
2009, the USEPA proposed revisions to its primary National Ambient Air Quality
Standard (NAAQS) for nitrogen dioxide.&#160;
This change could affect certain emission sources in heavy traffic areas
like the I-75 corridor between Cincinnati and Dayton.&#160; At this point, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
cannot determine the effect of this potential change, if any, on its
operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
USEPA proposed revisions to its primary NAAQS for SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;on November&nbsp;16, 2009.&#160; This would replace the current 24-hour
standard and current annual standard.&#160;
This regulation is expected to be finalized in 2010.&#160; At this time, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
cannot determine the effect of this potential change, if any, on its
operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;16,
2009, the USEPA announced that it would reconsider the 2008 national ground
level ozone standard.&#160; A more stringent
ambient ozone standard may lead to stricter NOx emission standards in the
future.&#160; At this point, <b>DP&amp;L</b> cannot determine the effect of this potential
change, if any, on its operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Air
Quality &#151; Litigation Involving Co-Owned Plants</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2000, as
amended in June&nbsp;2004, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a complaint in
the United States District Court, Southern District of Indiana, Indianapolis
Division against Cinergy Corp. (now part of Duke Energy) and two Cinergy
subsidiaries for alleged violations of the CAA at various generation units
operated by PSI Energy,&nbsp;Inc. and CG&amp;E, including generation units
co-owned by  <b>DP&amp;L</b> (Beckjord Unit 6 and Miami Fort Unit 7).&nbsp;
A retrial has been held in which the second jury found for Duke Energy on some
allegations, but for plaintiffs with respect to units at another one of Duke
Energy&#146;s wholly-owned facilities.&#160; In a
separate phase II remedies trial with respect to violations found in the first
trial, Duke Energy was ordered to close down three of its wholly-owned
generating units by September&nbsp;2009, surrender some emission allowances and
pay a fine.&#160; None of the violations found
or remedies ordered relate to generating units owned in part by <b>DP&amp;L</b>.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">130<a name="PB_130_032225_8715"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
2004, eight states and the City of New York filed a lawsuit in Federal District
Court for the Southern District of New York against American Electric Power
Company,&nbsp;Inc. (AEP), one of AEP&#146;s subsidiaries, Cinergy Corp. (a
subsidiary of Duke Energy Corporation (Duke Energy)) and four other electric
power companies.&#160; A similar lawsuit was
filed against these companies in the same court by Open Space Institute,&nbsp;Inc.,
Open Space Conservancy,&nbsp;Inc. and The Audubon Society of New
Hampshire.&#160; The lawsuits allege that the
companies&#146; emissions of CO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;contribute to global warming and constitute a
public or private nuisance.&#160; The lawsuits
seek injunctive relief in the form of specific emission reduction commitments.&#160; In 2005, the Federal District Court dismissed
the lawsuits, holding that the lawsuits raised political questions that should
not be decided by the courts.&#160; The
plaintiffs appealed.&#160; Finding that the
plaintiffs have standing to sue and can assert federal common law nuisance
claims, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit on September&nbsp;21,
2009 vacated the dismissal of the Federal District Court and remanded the
lawsuits back to the Federal District Court for further proceedings.&#160; Although we are not named as a party to these
lawsuits, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is a co-owner of coal-fired
plants with Duke Energy and AEP (or their subsidiaries) that could be affected
by the outcome of these lawsuits.&#160; The
Second Circuit Court&#146;s decision could also encourage these or other plaintiffs
to file similar lawsuits against other electric power companies, including
us.&#160; We are unable at this time to
predict with certainty the impact that these lawsuits might have on us.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;21,
2004, the Sierra Club filed a lawsuit against <b>DP&amp;L </b>and
the other owners of the J.M. Stuart generating station in the U.S. District
Court for the Southern District of Ohio for alleged violations of the CAA and
the station&#146;s operating permit.&#160; On August&nbsp;7,
2008, a consent decree was filed in the U.S. District Court in full settlement
of these CAA claims.&nbsp; Under the terms of the consent decree, <b>DP&amp;L</b> and the other owners of the J.M. Stuart generating
station agreed to: (i)&nbsp;certain emission targets related to NOx, SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and particulate
matter; (ii)&nbsp;make energy efficiency and renewable energy commitments that
are conditioned on receiving PUCO approval for the recovery of costs; (iii)&nbsp;forfeit
5,500 SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;allowances; and (iv)&nbsp;provide funding to a
third party non-profit organization to establish a solar water heater rebate
program.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
and the other owners of the station also entered into an attorneys&#146; fee
agreement to pay a portion of the Sierra Club&#146;s attorney and expert witness
fees.&nbsp; The parties to the lawsuit filed a joint motion on October&nbsp;22,
2008, seeking an order by the U.S. District Court approving the consent decree
with funding for the third party non-profit organization set at $300,000.&#160; On October&nbsp;23, 2008, the U.S. District
Court approved the consent decree.&#160; On October&nbsp;21,
2009, the Sierra Club filed with the U.S. District Court a motion for
enforcement of the consent decree based on the Sierra Club&#146;s interpretation of
the consent decree that would require certain NOx emissions that <b>DP&amp;L</b> has been excluding from its computations to be
included for purposes of complying with the emission targets and reporting
requirements of the consent decree.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
believes that it is properly computing and reporting NOx emissions under the
consent decree and has opposed the Sierra Club&#146;s motion.&#160; A decision on the motion is expected before
the end of the first quarter 2010.&#160;
Because J.M. Stuart Station&#146;s NOx emissions are well below the 2009 and
2010 limits in the consent decree under either method of calculation, an
adverse decision would have no effect in 2010 on operations or costs.&#160; An adverse decision could affect compliance
costs in future years when the NOx limits are further reduced under the consent
decree.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Air
Quality &#151; Notices of Violation Involving Co-Owned Plants</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> On March&nbsp;13, 2008, Duke Energy Ohio Inc., the operator of the
Zimmer generating station, received a NOV and a Finding of Violation from the
USEPA alleging violations of the CAA, the Ohio State Implementation Program
(SIP) and permits for the Station in areas including SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, opacity and increased heat input.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> is a
co-owner of the Zimmer generating station and could be affected by the eventual
resolution of this matter.&#160; Duke Energy
Ohio Inc. is expected to act on behalf of itself and the co-owners with respect
to this matter.&#160; At this time, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is unable to predict the outcome of this matter.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> In June&nbsp;2000, the USEPA issued a NOV to the <b>DP&amp;L</b>-operated J.M. Stuart generating station (co-owned
by <b>DP&amp;L</b>, CG&amp;E, and CSP)
for alleged violations of the CAA.&#160; The
NOV contained allegations consistent with NOVs and complaints that the USEPA
had recently brought against numerous other coal-fired utilities in the
Midwest.&#160; The NOV indicated the USEPA
may: (1)&nbsp;issue an order requiring compliance with the requirements of the
Ohio SIP; or (2)&nbsp;bring a civil action seeking injunctive relief and civil
penalties of up to $27,500 per day for each violation.&#160; To date, neither action has been taken.&#160; At this time, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
cannot predict the outcome of this matter.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;1999,
the USEPA filed civil complaints and NOVs against operators and owners of
certain generation facilities for alleged violations of the CAA.&#160; Generation units operated by CG&amp;E
(Beckjord Unit 6) and CSP (Conesville Unit 4) and co-owned by <b>DP&amp;L</b> were referenced in these
actions.&#160; Numerous northeast states have
filed complaints or have indicated that they will be joining the USEPA&#146;s action
against CG&amp;E and CSP.&#160; Although <b>DP&amp;L</b> was not identified in the NOVs,
civil complaints or state actions, the results of such proceedings could
materially affect <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
co-owned plants.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">131<a name="PB_131_032242_563"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> In December&nbsp;2007, the Ohio EPA issued a NOV to the <b>DP&amp;L</b>-operated Killen generating station (co-owned by <b>DP&amp;L</b> and CG&amp;E) for alleged violations of the
CAA.&#160; The NOVs alleged deficiencies in
the continuous monitoring of opacity.&#160; We
submitted a compliance plan to the Ohio EPA on December&nbsp;19, 2007.&#160; To date, no further actions have been taken
by the Ohio EPA.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Air
Quality &#151; Other Issues Involving Co-Owned Plants</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2006, <b>DP&amp;L</b> detected a malfunction with its emission monitoring
system at the <b>DP&amp;L</b>-operated Killen
generating station (co-owned by <b>DP&amp;L</b> and
CG&amp;E) and ultimately determined its SO</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and NOx emissions data were under
reported.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
has petitioned the USEPA to accept an alternative methodology for calculating
actual emissions for 2005 and the first quarter 2006.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L </b>has
sufficient allowances in its general account to cover the understatement and is
working with the USEPA to resolve the matter.&#160;
Management does not believe the ultimate resolution of this matter will
have a material impact on results of operations, financial position or cash
flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Air
Quality &#151; Notices of Violation Involving Wholly-Owned Plants</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
2007, the Ohio EPA and the USEPA issued NOVs to <b>DP&amp;L</b>
for alleged violations of the CAA at the O.H. Hutchings Station.&#160; The NOVs alleged deficiencies relate to stack
opacity and particulate emissions.&#160;
Discussions are under way with the USEPA, the U.S. Department of Justice
and Ohio EPA.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
has provided data to those agencies regarding its maintenance expenses and
operating results.&#160; On December&nbsp;15,
2008, <b>DP&amp;L</b> received a request from the
USEPA for additional documentation with respect to those issues and other CAA
issues including issues relating to capital expenses and any changes in
capacity or output of the units at the O.H. Hutchings station.&#160; During
2009, <b>DP&amp;L</b> has continued to
submit various other operational and performance data to the USEPA in compliance
with its request.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L </b>is
currently unable to determine the timing, costs or method by which the issues
may be resolved and continues to work with the USEPA on this issue.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;18,
2009, the USEPA issued a NOV to <b>DP&amp;L</b> for
alleged New Source Review (NSR) violations of the CAA at the O.H. Hutchings
Station relating to capital projects performed in 2001 involving Unit 3 and
Unit 6.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
does not believe that that the two projects described in the NOV were
modifications subject to NSR.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> is unable to determine the timing, costs or method
by which these issues may be resolved and continues to work with the USEPA on
this issue.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Water Quality</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;9,
2004, the USEPA issued final rules&nbsp;pursuant to the Clean Water Act
governing existing facilities that have cooling water intake structures.&nbsp;
The rules&nbsp;require an assessment of impingement and/or entrainment of
organisms as a result of cooling water withdrawal.&#160; A number of parties appealed the rules&nbsp;to
the Federal Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit in New York and the Court
issued an opinion on January&nbsp;25, 2007 remanding several aspects of the rule&nbsp;to
the USEPA for reconsideration.&nbsp; Several parties petitioned the U.S.
Supreme Court for review of the lower court decision.&#160; On April&nbsp;14, 2008, the Supreme Court
elected to review the lower court decision on the issue of whether the USEPA
can compare costs with benefits in determining the best technology available
for minimizing adverse environmental impact at cooling water intake
structures.&#160; Briefs were submitted to the
Court in the summer of 2008 and oral arguments were held in December&nbsp;2008.&#160; In April&nbsp;2009, the U.S. Supreme Court
ruled that the USEPA did have the authority to compare costs with benefits in
determining best technology available.&#160;
The USEPA is developing proposed regulations which it hopes to issue for
public comment by mid-2010.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;4,
2004, the Ohio EPA issued a final National Pollutant Discharge Elimination
System permit (the Permit) for J.M. Stuart Station that continued our authority
to discharge water from the station into the Ohio River.&#160; During the three-year term of the Permit, we conducted a thermal discharge study
to evaluate the technical feasibility and economic reasonableness of water cooling
methods other than cooling towers.&#160; In December&nbsp;2006,
we submitted an application for the renewal of the Permit that was due to
expire on June&nbsp;30, 2007.&#160; In July&nbsp;2007
we received a draft permit proposing to continue our authority to discharge
water from the station into the Ohio River.&#160;
On February&nbsp;5, 2008 we received a letter from Ohio EPA indicating
that they intended to impose a compliance schedule as part of the final Permit,
that requires us to implement one of two diffuser options for the discharge of
water from the station into the Ohio River as identified in the thermal
discharge study.&#160; Subsequently,
representatives from <b>DP&amp;L</b> and
the Ohio EPA have agreed to allow <b>DP&amp;L</b> to
restrict public access to the water discharge area as an alternative to installing
one of the diffuser options.&#160; Ohio EPA
issued a revised draft permit that was received on November&nbsp;12, 2008.&#160; In December&nbsp;2008, the USEPA requested
that the Ohio EPA provide additional information regarding the thermal
discharge in the draft permit.&#160; In June&nbsp;2009,
<b>DP&amp;L</b> provided information to the
USEPA in response to their request to Ohio EPA.&#160;
The timing for issuance of a final permit is uncertain.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">132<a name="PB_132_032253_9497"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2009,
the USEPA announced that it will be revising technology-based regulations
governing water discharges from steam electric generating facilities such as
J.M. Stuart, Killen and O.H. Hutchings Stations.&#160; The rulemaking will include the collection of
information via an industry-wide questionnaire as well as targeted water
sampling efforts at selected facilities.&#160;
Subsequent to the information collection effort, it is anticipated that
the USEPA will release a proposed rule&nbsp;in 2011 with final regulations
issued in late 2012 or early 2013.&#160; At
present, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is unable to predict the
impact this rulemaking will have on its operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Land Use and Solid Waste Disposal</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2002, <b>DP&amp;L</b> and other parties received a special notice that the
USEPA considers us to be a PRP for the clean-up of hazardous substances at the
South Dayton Dump landfill site.&#160; In August&nbsp;2005,
<b>DP&amp;L</b> and other parties
received a general notice regarding the performance of a Remedial Investigation
and Feasibility Study (RI/FS) under a Superfund Alternative Approach.&#160; In October&nbsp;2005, <b>DP&amp;L</b> received a special notice letter
inviting it to enter into negotiations with the USEPA to conduct the
RI/FS.&#160; No recent activity has occurred
with respect to that notice or PRP status.&#160;
More recently, <b>DP&amp;L</b> has
received requests by the USEPA and the existing PRP group to allow access to be
given to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service center building
site, which is across the street from the landfill site.&#160; The USEPA requested access to drill
monitoring and test wells to determine the extent of the landfill site&#146;s
contamination as well as to assess whether certain chemicals used at the
service center building site might have migrated through groundwater to the
landfill site.&#160; Pursuant to an
Administrative Order issued by the USEPA requiring access to <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> service center building site, <b>DP&amp;L</b> has granted such access and drilling of soil
borings and installation of monitoring wells occurred in the fall of 2009.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L </b>believes
the chemicals used at its service center building site were appropriately
disposed of and have not contributed to the contamination at the South Dayton
Dump landfill site.&#160; While <b>DP&amp;L</b> is unable at this time to predict the outcome of
this matter, if <b>DP&amp;L</b> were required to
contribute to the clean-up of the site, it could have a material adverse effect
on us.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is also unable at this time to predict whether the monitoring and test wells
may lead to any actions relating to the service center building site
independent of the South Dayton Dump clean-up.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2003,
<b>DP&amp;L </b>and other parties received a
special notice that the USEPA considers us to be a PRP for the clean-up of
hazardous substances at the Tremont City landfill site.&#160; Information available to <b>DP&amp;L </b>does
not demonstrate that it contributed hazardous substances to the site.&#160; While <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
unable at this time to predict the outcome of this matter, if <b>DP&amp;L</b> were required to contribute to the clean-up of the
site, it could have a material adverse effect on us.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2007,
a PRP group contacted <b>DP&amp;L</b>
seeking our financial participation in a settlement that the group had reached
with the federal government with respect to the clean-up of an industrial site
once owned by Carolina Transformer,&nbsp;Inc.&#160;
<b>DP&amp;L</b>&#146;s business records clearly
show we did not conduct business with Carolina Transformer that would require
our participation in any clean-up of the site.&#160;
<b>DP&amp;L </b>has declined to participate in
the clean-up of this site.&#160; While <b>DP&amp;L</b> is unable at this time to predict the outcome of
this matter, if <b>DP&amp;L</b> were required to
contribute to the clean-up of the site, it could have a material adverse effect
on us.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2008, a
major spill occurred at an ash pond owned by the Tennessee Valley Authority
(TVA) as a result of a dike failure.&#160; The
spill generated a significant amount of national news coverage, and support for
tighter regulations for the storage and handling of coal combustion products.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> has
ash ponds at the Killen, O.H. Hutchings and J.M. Stuart stations which it
operates, and also at generating stations operated by others but in which <b>DP&amp;L</b> has an ownership interest.&#160; We frequently inspect our ash ponds and do
not anticipate any similar failures.&#160; It
is widely expected that the federal government will propose new regulations
covering ash generated from the combustion of coal and including additional
monitoring, testing, or construction standards with respect to ash ponds and
ash landfills.&#160; During March&nbsp;2009,
the USEPA, through a formal Information Collection Request, collected
information on ash pond facilities across the country, including those at
Killen and J.M. Stuart stations.&#160;
Subsequently the USEPA collected similar information for O.H. Hutchings
Station.&#160; In addition, during August&nbsp;and
October&nbsp;2009, representatives of the USEPA visited J.M. Stuart Station to
collect information on plant operations relative to the production and handling
of by-products.&#160; Due to the wide range of
possible outcomes, <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
unable at this time to predict the timing or the financial impact of any future
governmental initiative that may occur.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
addition, as a result of the TVA ash pond spill, there has been increasing
advocacy to regulate coal combustion byproducts as hazardous waste under the
Resource Conservation Recovery Act, Subtitle C.&#160;
On October&nbsp;15, 2009, the USEPA provided a draft rule&nbsp;to the
Office of Management and Budget for interagency review.&#160; The draft rule&nbsp;proposed to regulate coal
ash as a hazardous waste, with limited beneficial reuse.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
unable at this time to predict the financial impact of this regulation, but if
coal combustion byproducts are regulated as hazardous waste, it is expected to
have a material adverse impact on operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">133<a name="PB_133_032308_3641"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Legal and
Other Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2007, <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed a lawsuit against a coal supplier seeking
damages incurred due to the supplier&#146;s failure to supply approximately 1.5
million tons of coal to two jointly owned plants under a coal supply agreement,
of which approximately 570 thousand tons was <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
share.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b> obtained replacement coal
to meet its needs.&#160; The supplier has
denied liability, and is currently in federal bankruptcy proceedings.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
unable to determine the ultimate resolution of this matter at this time.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b> has not recorded any assets relating to possible
recovery of costs in this lawsuit.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;16, 2007, <b>DPL</b> filed a claim with Energy Insurance
Mutual (EIM) to recoup legal expenses associated with our litigation against
certain former executives.&nbsp; Arbitration on that claim occurred on May&nbsp;13,
2009.&#160; </font><tt><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
arbitration panel issued a ruling in Phase 1 of the arbitration on September&nbsp;25,
2009, finding that most of the claims involving the former executives were
covered.</font></tt><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The matter is pending.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a member of PJM, <b>DP&amp;L</b>
is also subject to charges and costs associated with PJM operations as approved
by the FERC.&nbsp; FERC Orders issued in 2007 regarding the allocation of costs
of large transmission facilities within PJM, could result in additional costs
being allocated to <b>DP&amp;L </b>of
approximately $12 million or more annually by 2012.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed a notice of appeal to the
U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit on March&nbsp;18, 2008 challenging the
allocation method.&nbsp; The appeal was consolidated with other appeals taken
by other interested parties of the same FERC Orders and the consolidated cases
were assigned to the 7</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;Circuit.&nbsp; On August&nbsp;6, 2009, the 7</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;Circuit ruled that the
FERC had failed to provide a reasoned basis for the allocation method it had
approved.&#160; Rehearings were filed by other
interested litigants and denied by the Court, which then remanded the matter to
the FERC for further proceedings.&#160; On January&nbsp;21,
2010, the FERC issued a procedural order on remand establishing a paper hearing
process under which PJM will make an informational filing in late
February.&nbsp; Subsequently PJM and other parties, including <b>DP&amp;L</b>, will be able to file initial comments, testimony,
and recommendations and reply comments.&nbsp; Absent future changes to the
procedural schedule that may occur for a number of reasons including if
settlement discussions are held, the paper hearing process should be complete
and the case ready for FERC consideration in 2010.&nbsp; FERC did not establish
a deadline for its issuance of a substantive order.&nbsp; <b>DP&amp;L</b>
cannot predict the timing or the likely outcome of the proceeding.&#160; Until such time as FERC may act to approve a
change in methodology, PJM will continue to apply the allocation methodology
that had been approved by FERC in 2007.&#160;
Although we continue to maintain that these costs should be borne by the
beneficiaries of these projects and that <b>DP&amp;L</b> is not
one of these beneficiaries, any new credits or additional costs resulting from
the ultimate outcome of this proceeding will be reflected in <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> TCRR rider which is already in place to pass
through RTO-related costs and credits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2009, the
NERC, a FERC-certified electric reliability organization responsible for
developing and enforcing mandatory reliability standards, commenced a routine
audit of <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b> operations.&#160; The audit, which was for the period June&nbsp;18,
2007 to June&nbsp;25, 2009, evaluated <b>DP&amp;L&#146;s</b>
compliance with 42 requirements in 18 NERC-reliability standards.&#160; <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
currently subject to a compliance audit at a minimum of once every three years
as provided by the NERC Rules&nbsp;of Procedure. This audit was concluded in June&nbsp;2009
and its findings revealed that <b>DP&amp;L</b> had
some Possible Alleged Violations (PAVs) associated with five NERC Reliability
Standards.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to the
report, <b>DP&amp;L</b> filed mitigation plans with
NERC to address the PAVs.&#160; These
mitigation plans have been accepted and <b>DP&amp;L</b> is
currently awaiting a proposal for settlement from NERC.&#160; While we are currently unable to determine
the extent of penalties, if any, that may be imposed on <b>DP&amp;L</b>,
we do not believe such penalties will have a material impact on our results of
operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Report
of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></b><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_035151"></a></p>

<p align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of
Directors and Stockholders</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DPL Inc.:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the
accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets of DPL Inc. and subsidiaries (the
Company) as of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, and the related Consolidated
Statements of Results of Operations, Shareholders&#146; Equity and Cash Flows for
each of the years in the three-year period ended December&nbsp;31, 2009. In
connection with our audits of the consolidated financial statements, we have
audited the consolidated financial statement schedule, &#147;Schedule II &#151; Valuation
and Qualifying Accounts.&#148; We also have audited the Company&#146;s internal control
over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, based on criteria
established in <i>Internal Control &#151; Integrated Framework</i>
issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission
(COSO). The Company&#146;s management is responsible for these consolidated
financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial
reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over
financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#146;s Report on Internal
Control Over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion
on these consolidated financial statements and an opinion on the Company&#146;s
internal control over financial reporting based on our audits.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits
in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight
Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the
audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements
are free of material misstatement and whether effective internal control over
financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audits of the
consolidated financial statements included examining, on a test basis, evidence
supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing
the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management,
and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. Our audit of
internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of
internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material
weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating
effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audits also
included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the
circumstances. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our
opinions.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A company&#146;s internal
control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable
assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation
of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally
accepted accounting principles. A company&#146;s internal control over financial
reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)&nbsp;pertain to the
maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly
reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide
reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation
of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting
principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made
only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the
company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or
timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the
company&#146;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of its inherent
limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or
detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to
future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate
because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the
policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the
consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all
material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of
the years in the three-year period ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, in conformity
with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. Also in our opinion, the
Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over
financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, based on criteria established
in <i>Internal Control &#151; Integrated Framework</i>
issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">KPMG LLP</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Philadelphia, Pennsylvania<br>
February&nbsp;11, 2010</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-45.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9 &#151;&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes
in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</font></b><a name="Item9ChangesInAndDisagreementsWit_035238"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-45.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9A &#151;
Controls and Procedures</font></b><a name="Item9aControlsAndProcedures_035241"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Disclosure
Controls and Procedures</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Chief Executive
Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) are responsible for
establishing and maintaining our disclosure controls and procedures.&#160; These controls and procedures were designed
to ensure that material information relating to us and our subsidiaries are
communicated to the CEO and CFO.&#160; We
evaluated these disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period
covered by this report with the participation of our CEO and CFO.&#160; Based on this evaluation, our CEO and CFO
concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective: (i)&nbsp;to
ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we
file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported,
within the time periods specified in the SEC&#146;s rules&nbsp;and forms; and (ii)&nbsp;to
ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we
submit under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to our
management, including our principal executive and principal financial officers,
or persons performing similar functions, as appropriate, to allow timely
decisions regarding required disclosure.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There was no change in
our internal control over financial reporting during the most recently
completed fiscal period that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely
to materially affect, internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following report is
our report on internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31,
2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#146;s
Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
are responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over
financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f).&#160; Under the supervision and with the
participation of management, including the CEO and CFO, we conducted an
evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial
reporting based on the framework in <i>Internal
Control - Integrated Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring
Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160;
Based on an evaluation under the framework in <i>Internal Control - Integrated Framework, </i>we concluded that
our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&nbsp;31,
2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31,
2009, has been audited by KPMG LLP, the independent registered public
accounting firm that audited the financial statements contained herein, as
stated in their report which is included herein.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9B &#151;
Other Information</font></b><a name="Item9bOtherInformation_035319"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="1" width="25%" noshade color="black" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit fees relate to professional
services rendered for the audit of our annual financial statements and the
reviews of our quarterly financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit-related fees relate to services
rendered to us for assurance and related services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tax fees consisted principally of tax
compliance services. Tax compliance services are services rendered based upon
facts already in existence or transactions that have already occurred to
document, compute, and obtain government approval for amounts to be included in
tax filings.</font></p>
